body.text:
Aśokāvadānaṃ
Pāṃśupradānāvadānaṃ
body.translated_text:
<s>Aśokāvadāna</s> (The Legend of <s>Aśoka</s>)
<s>Pāṃśupradānāvadāna</s> (The Legend of the Gift of Dust)

children.text: yo 'sau svamāṃsatanubhiryajanāni kṛtvā- tapyac ciraṃ karuṇayā jagato hitāya /
children.translated_text: He who, making sacrifices of his own flesh and body, practised austerities for a long time out of compassion for the welfare of the world —

children.text: tasya śramasya saphalīkaraṇāya santaḥ sāvarjitaṃ śṛṇuta sāṃpratabhāṣyamāṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: in order to bring the fruit of his labours to fulfilment, O virtuous ones, listen attentively to what is now being narrated.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati / iti sūtraṃ vaktavyaṃ / atra tāvad bhagavattathāgatavadanāmbhodharavivarapratyudgatavacanasaratsaliladhārāsampātāpanītarāgadveṣamohamadamānamāyāśāṭhyapaṅkapaṭalānāṃ śabdanyāyāditarkaśāstrārthāvalokanotpannaprajñāpradīpaprotsāritakuśāstradarśanāndhakārāṇāṃ saṃsāratṛṣṇāchedipravarasaddharmapayaḥpānaśauṇḍānāṃ gurūṇāṃ saṃnighau sarvāvavādakaśreṣṭhaṃ śakrabrahmeśānayamavarūṇakuveravā[va]savasomādityādibhirapyapratihataśāsanaṃ kandarpadarpāpamardanaśūraṃ mahātmānam atimaharddhikaṃ sthaviropaguptamārabhya kāñcideva vibudhajanamanaḥ prasādakārīṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ samanusmariṣyāmaḥ / tatra tāvad gurubhiravahitaśrotrairbhavitavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard: At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Thus should the <s>sūtra</s> (discourse) be recited. Here then, we shall recall a certain righteous tale that gladdens the minds of the wise, beginning with the elder <s>Upagupta</s> — who was foremost among all instructors in the assembly of the teachers whose stain of passion, hatred, delusion, pride, conceit, deceit, and hypocrisy had been washed away by the downpour of the autumn-rain-like speech issuing from the opening of the cloud that is the mouth of the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s>; whose darkness of false doctrines had been driven away by the lamp of wisdom arisen from examining the meaning of the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) of logic such as grammar, reasoning, and the rest; who were ardent drinkers of the water of the excellent true <s>Dharma</s> that cuts the thirst of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence); whose teaching was unobstructed even by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and others; who was a hero in crushing the pride of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love); who was great-souled and possessed of supreme supernatural powers. Herein, the teachers should listen with attentive ears.

body.text: evamanuśrūyate / yadā bhagavān parinirvāṇakālasamaye 'palālanāgaṃ vinīya kumbhakārīṃ caṇḍālīṃ gopālīṃ ca teṣāṃ mathurāmanuprāptaḥ / tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma / asyāmānanda mathurāyāṃ mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya gupto nāma gāndhiko bhaviṣyati / tasya putro bhaviṣyati upaguptanāmālakṣaṇako buddho yo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakārya kariṣyati / tasyāvavādena bahavo bhikṣavaḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyanti / te 'ṣṭādaśahastāmāyāmenaṃ dvādaśahastāṃ vistāreṇa caturaṅgulamātrābhiḥ śalākābhir guhāṃ pūrayiṣyanti / eṣo 'gro me ānanda śrāvakāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati avavādakānāṃ yaduta upagupto bhikṣuḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus is it handed down by tradition. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), at the time approaching his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), having disciplined the <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) <s>Apalāla</s>, and the potter-woman, the <s>caṇḍālī</s> (outcaste woman), and the cowherd-woman, arrived at <s>Mathurā</s> with them, there the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'In this <s>Mathurā</s>, O <s>Ānanda</s>, a hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a perfume-seller named <s>Gupta</s>. His son will be named <s>Upagupta</s>, a Buddha without the marks, who a hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> will carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>. Through his instruction, many <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), by the complete abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), will directly realise <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an arhat). They will fill a cave eighteen cubits in length and twelve cubits in breadth with counting-sticks, each measuring four finger-breadths. This one, O <s>Ānanda</s>, will be the foremost of my <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) among instructors — namely, the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) <s>Upagupta</s>.'

body.text: paśyasi tvamānanda dūrata eva nīlanīlāmbararājiṃ / evaṃ bhadanta / eṣa ānanda urūmuṇḍo nāma parvataḥ / atra varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya śāṇakavāsī nāma bhikṣurbhaviṣyati / so 'tra urūmuṇḍaparvate vihāraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati / upaguptaṃ ca pravrājayiṣyati /
body.translated_text: 'Do you see, O <s>Ānanda</s>, that dark-blue line in the distance?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'That, O <s>Ānanda</s>, is the mountain called <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s>. Here, a hundred years after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) named <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s>. He will establish a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) on this <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s> mountain, and he will ordain <s>Upagupta</s> into the monastic order.'

body.text: mathurāyāmānanda naṭo bhaṭaśca dvau bhrātarau śreṣṭhinau bhaviṣyataḥ / tau urumuṇḍaparvate vihāraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyataḥ / tasya naṭabhaṭiketi
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Mathurā</s>, O <s>Ānanda</s>, there will be two brothers, a dancer (<s>Naṭa</s>) and a soldier (<s>Bhaṭa</s>), who will be chief merchants. They will establish a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) on <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s> mountain. It will be known by the name <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>.'

body.text: saṃjñā bhaviṣyati / etadagraṃ me ānanda bhaviṣyati śamathānukūlānāṃ śayyāsanānāṃ yadidaṃ naṭabhaṭikāraṇyāyatanaṃ /
body.translated_text: 'This, O <s>Ānanda</s>, will be the foremost among dwelling-places and seats conducive to <s>śamatha</s> (tranquillity meditation) — namely, the forest hermitage of <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>.'

body.text: athāyuṣmāna ānando bhagavantamidamavocat / āścarya bhadanta yad īdṛśamāyuṣmān upagupto bahujanahitaṃ kariṣyati / bhagavān āha / nānanda etarhi, yathātite 'pyadhvani tena vinipatitaśarīreṇāpyatraiva bahujanahitaṃ kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the venerable <s>Upagupta</s> will bring such great benefit to many people.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, O <s>Ānanda</s>; even in the past, even with a body that had fallen (into a lower birth), he brought great benefit to many right here.'

body.text: urūmuṇḍaparvate trayaḥ pārśvāḥ / ekatra pradeśe pañca pratyekabuddhaśātāni prativasanti / dvitīye pañcarṣiśatāni / tṛtīye pañcamarkaṭaśatāni / tatra yo 'sau pañcānāṃ markaṭaśatānāṃ yūthapatiḥ sa taṃ yūthamapahāya yatra pārśve pañca pratyekabuddhaśatāni prativasanti tatra gataḥ / tasya tān pratyekabuddhān dṛṣṭvā prasādo jātaḥ / sa teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ śīrṇaparṇāni mūlaphalāni copanāmayati, yadā ca te paryaṅkeṇopaviṣṭā bhavanti sa vṛddhānte kṛtvā yāvan navāntaṃ gatvā paryaṅkeṇopaviśati /
body.translated_text: On <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s> mountain there are three slopes. On one side, five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) dwell. On the second, five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers). On the third, five hundred monkeys. There, the leader of those five hundred monkeys, leaving his troop, went to the slope where the five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> dwelt. Upon seeing those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, faith arose in him. He offered them fallen leaves, roots, and fruits. And whenever they sat in the cross-legged posture, he would begin at one end and go to the other end, and then sit down cross-legged himself.

body.text: yāvat te pratyekabuddhāḥ parinirvṛtāḥ / sa teṣāṃ śīrṇaparṇāni mūlaphalāni copanāmayati / te na pratigṛṇhanti / sa teṣāṃ cīvarakarṇikāni ākarṣayati / pādau gṛṇhāti / yāvat sa markaṭaścintayati / niyatamete kālagatā bhaviṣyanti / tataḥ sa markaṭaḥ śocitvā paridevitvā ca dvitīyaṃ pārśvaṃ gato yatra pañcarṣiśatāni prativasanti /
body.translated_text: In time, those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing). He offered them fallen leaves, roots, and fruits, but they did not accept. He pulled at the corners of their robes. He grasped their feet. Then that monkey thought: 'Surely these ones must have died.' Then that monkey, having grieved and lamented, went to the second slope where the five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) dwelt.

body.text: te ca ṛṣayaḥ kecit kaṇṭakāpāśrayāḥ kecid bhasmāpāśrayāḥ kecidūrdhvahastāḥ kecit pañcātapāvasthitāḥ / sa teṣāṃ teṣām īryāpathān vikopayitumārabdhaḥ / ye kaṇṭakāpāśrayāsteṣāṃ kaṇṭakān uddharati / bhasmāpāśrayāṇāṃ bhasma vidhunoti / ūrdhvahastānāmadho hastaṃ pātayati / pañcātapāvasthitānāmagnim avakirati / yadā ca tairīryāpatho vikopito bhavati tadā sa teṣāmagrataḥ paryaṅkaṃ badhnāti /
body.translated_text: Those <s>ṛṣis</s> practised various austerities: some rested on thorns, some on ashes, some held their arms raised upward, and some stood in the posture of the five fires. He began to disturb their modes of practice. He pulled out the thorns from those who rested on thorns; he shook off the ashes from those who rested on ashes; he pulled down the arms of those who held them upward; and he scattered the fires of those who stood amidst the five fires. And whenever he had disrupted their practice, he would sit cross-legged before them.

body.text: yāvat tairṛṣibhirācāryāya niveditaṃ / tenāpi coktaṃ / paryaṅkeṇa tāvan niṣīdata / yāvattāni pañcarṣiśatāni paryaṅkeṇopaviṣṭāni / te 'nācāryakā anupadeśakāḥ saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣān dharmānāmukhīkṛtya pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ sākṣātkṛtavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>ṛṣis</s> reported this to their teacher. He too said: 'Then sit cross-legged!' Thereupon those five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> sat cross-legged. Without a teacher and without instruction, contemplating the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s> (factors of awakening), they directly realised <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening).

body.text: atha teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāmetadabhavad / yat kiñcadasmābhiḥ śreyo 'vāptaṃ tat sarvamimaṃ markaṭam āgamya / tairyāvat sa markaṭaḥ phalamūlaiḥ paripālitaḥ / kālagatasya ca taccharīraṃ gandhakāṣṭhairdhmāpitaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> had this thought: 'Whatever spiritual good we have attained, all of it has come about because of this monkey.' Then they nourished that monkey with fruits and roots. And when he died, they cremated his body with fragrant wood.

body.text: tat kiṃ manyase ānanda yo 'sau pañcānāṃ markaṭaśatānāṃ yūthapatiḥ sa eṣa upaguptaḥ / tadāpi tena vinipatitaśarīreṇāpyatraivorumuṇḍaparvate bahujanahitaṃ kṛtaṃ / anāgate 'pyadhvani varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mamātraivorumuṇḍaparvate bahujanahitaṃ kariṣyati / tacca yathaivaṃ tathopadarśayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, O <s>Ānanda</s>? He who was the leader of those five hundred monkeys — he is this very <s>Upagupta</s>. Even then, with a body fallen (into a lower birth), right here on <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s> mountain he brought great benefit to many. And in the future as well, a hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, right here on <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s> mountain he will bring great benefit to many. And how that will come about, we shall show.'

body.text: śāṇakavāsyupākhyānaṃ
body.translated_text: The Sub-tale of <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s>

body.text: yadā sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinā urumuṇḍe parvate vihāraḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ, samanvāharati / kimasau gandhika utpannaḥ / athādyāpi notpadyata iti / paśyatyutpannaḥ / sa yāvat samanvāharati / yo 'sau tasya putra upagupto nāmnālakṣaṇako buddho nirdiṣṭo yo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyatīti, kimasāvutpannaḥ / adyāpi notpadyata iti / paśyatyadyāpi notpadyate /
body.translated_text: When the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> had established a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) on <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s> mountain, he reflected: 'Has that perfume-seller been born yet? Or has he not yet been born?' He saw that he had been born. Then he reflected: 'That son of his, designated by name as <s>Upagupta</s>, a Buddha without the marks, who will carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s> a hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — has he been born? Or has he not yet been born?' He saw that he had not yet been born.

body.text: tena yāvadupāyena gupto gāndhiko bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasāditaḥ / sa yadābhiprasannastadā sthaviraḥ saṃbahulairbhikṣubhiḥ sārdhamekadivasaṃ tasya gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ aparasminnahani, ātmadvitīyaḥ / anyasminnahani, ekākī / yāvad gupto gāndhikaḥ sthaviraṃ śāṇakavāsinamekākinaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati / na khalvāryasya kaścit paścācchramaṇaṃ / sthavira uvāca / jarādharmāṇāṃ kuto 'smākaṃ paścācchramaṇo bhavati / yadi kecicchraddhāpurogeṇa
body.translated_text: Then, by skillful means, the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> inspired faith in <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller towards the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). When he had become faithful, the elder first entered his house one day with a large number of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks); the next day with just one companion; and on another day, alone. Then <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller, seeing the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> alone, said: 'Does the noble one not have any attendant monk?' The elder replied: 'For us who are subject to old age, how could there be an attendant monk? If some persons, led by faith,'

body.text: pravrajanti, te 'smākaṃ paścācchramaṇā bhavanti / gupto gāndhika uvāca / āryāhaṃ tāvad gṛhavāse parigṛddho viṣayābhirataśca / na mayā śakyaṃ pravrajituṃ / api tu yo 'smākaṃ putro bhavati taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ / sthavira uvāca / vatsa evamastu / api tu dṛḍhapratijñāṃ smarethāstvamiti /
body.translated_text: 'go forth into the homeless life, they become our attendant monks.' <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller said: 'Noble sir, I am attached to household life and devoted to sensual pleasures. It is not possible for me to go forth. But whichever son is born to us, him we shall give to the noble one as an attendant monk.' The elder said: 'My child, so be it. But remember your firm promise.'

body.text: yāvad guptasya gāndhikasya putro jātaḥ / tasyāśvagupta iti nāmadheya kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: In time, a son was born to <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller. He was given the name <s>Aśvagupta</s>.

body.text: sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā sthaviraśāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamadhigamyovāca / vatsa tvayā pratijñātaṃ yo 'smākaṃ putro bhaviṣyati taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ / ayaṃ ca putro jātaḥ / anujānīhi pravrājayiṣyāmīti / gāndhika uvāca / ārya ayamasmākamekaputraḥ / marṣayānyo yo 'smākaṃ dvitīyaḥ putro bhaviṣyati, taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: When he had grown up, the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> approached <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller and said: 'My child, you promised: "Whichever son is born to us, him we shall give to the noble one as an attendant monk." A son has now been born. Give permission, and I shall ordain him.' The perfume-seller said: 'Noble sir, this is our only son. Please be patient. Whichever second son is born to us, him we shall give to the noble one as an attendant monk.'

body.text: yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsī samanvāharati / kimayaṃ sa upaguptaḥ / paśyati neti / tena sthavireṇābhihita evamastviti / tasya yāvad dvitīyaḥ putro jātaḥ / tasya dhanagupta iti nāma kṛtaṃ / sopi yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā sthaviraśāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamuvāca / vatsa tvayā pratijñātaṃ yo 'smākaṃ putro bhaviṣyati taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ / ayaṃ ca te putro jātaḥ / anujānīhi pravrājayiṣyāmīti / gāndhika uvāca / ārya marṣaya eko 'smākaṃ bahirdhā dravyaṃ saṃcayiṣyati, dvitīyo 'ntargṛhe paripālanaṃ kariṣyatīti / api tu yo 'smākaṃ tṛtīyaḥ putro bhaviṣyati sa āryasya dattaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> reflected: 'Is this one that <s>Upagupta</s>?' He saw that he was not. So the elder said: 'So be it.' In time, a second son was born to him. He was given the name <s>Dhanagupta</s>. When he too had grown up, the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> said to <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller: 'My child, you promised: "Whichever son is born to us, him we shall give to the noble one as an attendant monk." A son has now been born to you. Give permission, and I shall ordain him.' The perfume-seller said: 'Noble sir, please be patient. One of our sons will accumulate wealth abroad, and the second will manage the household. But whichever third son is born to us, he is given to the noble one.'

body.text: yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsī samanvāharati / kimayaṃ sa upaguptaḥ / paśyati neti / tataḥ sthavira uvāca / evamastviti / yāvad guptasya gāndhikasya tṛtīyaḥ putro jātaḥ / abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'tikrānto mānuṣavarṇamasaṃprāptaśca divyavarṇaṃ / tasya vistareṇa jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā upagupta iti nāma kṛtam / so 'pi yadā mahān saṃvṛtto yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamabhigamyovāca / vatsa tvayā pratijñātaṃ yo 'smākaṃ tṛtīyaḥ putro bhaviṣyati taṃ vayamāryasya dāsyāmaḥ paścācchramaṇārthe / ayaṃ te tṛtīyaḥ putra utpannaḥ / anujānīhi pravrājayiṣyāmīti / gupto gāndhika uvāca / ārya samayataḥ / yadālābho 'nucchedo bhaviṣyatīti tadānujñāsyāmi /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> reflected: 'Is this one that <s>Upagupta</s>?' He saw that he was not. Then the elder said: 'So be it.' In time, a third son was born to <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller. He was handsome, good-looking, pleasing, having surpassed the complexion of humans yet not having attained the complexion of the gods. When an elaborate birth-celebration was performed for him, he was given the name <s>Upagupta</s>. When he too had grown up, the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> approached <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller and said: 'My child, you promised: "Whichever third son is born to us, him we shall give to the noble one for the purpose of becoming an attendant monk." This third son of yours has been born. Give permission, and I shall ordain him.' <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller said: 'Noble sir, on one condition: when there is profit and no loss, then I shall give permission.'

body.text: yadā tena samayaḥ kṛtastadā māreṇa sarvāvatī mathurā gandhāviṣṭā / te (mathurāvāsinaḥ) sarve upaguptasakāśād gandhān krīṇanti / sa prabhūtān dadāti /
body.translated_text: When this condition was made, <s>Māra</s> (the Evil One) caused all of <s>Mathurā</s> to be pervaded with fragrance. All the residents of <s>Mathurā</s> bought their perfumes from <s>Upagupta</s>. He gave in abundance.

body.text: yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ gataḥ / upaguptaśca gandhāpaṇe sthitaḥ / sa dharmeṇa vyavahāraṃ karoti / gandhān vikrīṇīte / sa sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinābhihitaḥ / vatsa kīdṛśāste cittacaitasikāḥ pravartante / kliṣṭā vākliṣṭā veti / upagupta uvāca / ārya naiva jānāmi kīdṛśāḥ kliṣṭāścittacaitasikāḥ kīdṛśā akliṣṭā iti / sthaviraśāṇakavāsī uvāca / vatsa
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> went to <s>Upagupta</s>. <s>Upagupta</s> was standing at the perfume shop. He conducted business honestly, selling perfumes. The elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> said to him: 'My child, what kind of mental states (<s>citta-caitasika</s>) arise in you — afflicted or unafflicted?' <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'Noble sir, I do not even know what afflicted mental states are like or what unafflicted ones are like.' The elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> said: 'My child,'

body.text: yadi kevalaṃ cittaṃ parijñātuṃ śakyasi pratipakṣaṃ mocayituṃ / tena tasya kṛṣṇikapaṭṭikā dattā pāṇḍurikā ca / yadi kliṣṭaṃ cittamutpadyate kṛṣṇikāṃ paṭṭikāṃ sthāpaya / athākliṣṭaṃ cittamutpadyate pāṇḍurāṃ paṭṭikāṃ sthāpaya / aśubhāṃ manasi kuru / buddhānusmṛtiṃ ca bhāvayasveti / tenāsya vyapadiṣṭaṃ /
body.translated_text: 'if you can at least observe the mind, you will be able to release the antidote.' Then he gave him a black tablet and a white one. 'When an afflicted mental state arises, place a black tablet. When an unafflicted mental state arises, place a white tablet. Contemplate the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>). And cultivate <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>).' Thus he instructed him.

body.text: tasya yāvadārabdhā akliṣṭāścittacaitasikāḥ pravartituṃ / sa dvau bhāgau kṛṣṇikānāṃ sthāpayati / ekaṃ pāṇḍurikāṇāṃ / yāvadardhaṃ kṛṣṇikānāṃ sthāpayati / ardhaṃ paṇḍurikāṇāṃ / yāvad dvau bhāgau pāṇḍurikāṇāṃ sthāpayati / ekaṃ kṛṣṇikānāṃ /
body.translated_text: When his unafflicted mental states (<s>cittacaitasika</s>) began to operate, he would set aside two portions for the dark ones (unwholesome thoughts) and one for the white ones (wholesome thoughts). Then he would set aside half for the dark ones and half for the white ones. Then he would set aside two portions for the white ones and one for the dark ones.

body.text: yāvadanupūrveṇa sarvāṇyeva śuklāni cittānyutpadyante / sa pāṇḍurikāṇāmeva paṭṭikāṃ sthāpayati / dharmeṇa vyavahāraṃ karoti /
body.translated_text: Gradually, only pure mental states arose in him. He placed down only the strip for the white ones. He conducted his business in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness).

body.text: mathurāyāṃ vāsavadattā nāma gaṇikā / tasyā dāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ gatvā gandhān krīṇāti / sā vāsavadattayā cocyate / dārikemuṣyate sa gāndhikastvayā, bahūn gandhān ānayasīti / dārikovāca / āryaduhita upagupto gāndhikadārako rūpasampannaścāturyamādhuryasampannaśca
body.translated_text: In <s>Mathurā</s> there was a courtesan named <s>Vāsavadattā</s>. Her maidservant went to <s>Upagupta</s> to buy perfumes. <s>Vāsavadattā</s> said to her: 'Girl, that perfume-seller is being cheated by you — you bring so many perfumes.' The girl said: 'Noble lady, <s>Upagupta</s>, the perfume-seller's son, is endowed with beauty, charm, and sweetness;

body.text: dharmeṇa vyavahāraṃ karoti / śrutvā ca vāsavadattāyā upaguptasakāśe sānurāgaṃ cittamutpannaṃ / tayā yāvad dāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ preṣitā / tvatsakāśamāgamiṣyāmi / icchāmi tvayā sārdhaṃ ratimanubhavituṃ / yāvad dāsyā upaguptasya niveditaṃ / upagupta uvāca / akālaste bhagini maddarśanāyeti /
body.translated_text: he conducts his business in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>.' Upon hearing this, a feeling of passionate attachment arose in <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s mind toward <s>Upagupta</s>. She sent the maidservant to <s>Upagupta</s> with the message: 'I wish to come to you. I desire to experience the pleasure of love with you.' The maidservant conveyed this to <s>Upagupta</s>. <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'It is not the right time, sister, for you to see me.'

body.text: vāsavadattā pañcabhiḥ purāṇaśataiḥ paricāryate / tasya buddhirutpannā / niyataṃ pañcapurāṇaśatāni notsahate dātuṃ / tayā yāvad dāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ preṣitā / na mamāryaputrasakāśāt kārṣāpaṇenāpi prayojanaṃ / kevalamāryaputreṇa saha ratimanubhaveyaṃ / dāsya tathā niveditaṃ / upagupta uvāca / akālaste bhagini maddarśanāyeti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vāsavadattā</s> charged five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> (ancient coins) for her services. He thought: 'Surely she will not be willing to forgo five hundred <s>purāṇas</s>.' She then sent the maidservant to <s>Upagupta</s> again: 'I have no need of even a single <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin) from the noble son. I only wish to experience the pleasure of love with the noble son.' The maidservant reported this accordingly. <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'It is not the right time, sister, for you to see me.'

body.text: yāvadanyataraḥ śreṣṭhiputro vāsavadattāyāḥ sakāśaṃ praviṣṭaḥ / anyataraśca sārthavāha uttarāpathāt pañcaśatamaśvapaṇyaṃ gṛhītvā mathurāmanuprāptaḥ / tenābhihitaṃ / katarā veśyā sarvapradhānā, tena śrutaṃ vāsavadatteti / sa pañcapurāṇaśatāni gṛhītvā bahūn ca prābhṛtān vāsavadattāyāḥ sakāśamabhigataḥ /
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, a certain merchant's son had entered <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s quarters. And a certain caravan-leader had arrived in <s>Mathurā</s> from the northern route, having brought five hundred horses for sale. He asked: 'Which courtesan is the foremost of all?' He was told: '<s>Vāsavadattā</s>.' Taking five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> and many gifts, he went to <s>Vāsavadattā</s>.

body.text: tato vāsavadattayā lobhākṛṣṭayā taṃ śreṣṭhiputraṃ praghātayitvāvaskare prakṣipya sārthavāhena saha ratiranubhūtā / yāvat sa śreṣṭhiputro
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, drawn by greed, had that merchant's son killed and thrown into a refuse heap, and enjoyed love with the caravan-leader. Then that merchant's son

body.text: bandhubhiravaskarād uddhṛtya rājño niveditaḥ / tato rājñābhihitaṃ / gacchantu bhavanto vāsavadattāṃ hastapādau karṇanāse ca chittvā śmaśāne chorayantu /
body.translated_text: was pulled out of the refuse heap by his relatives and reported to the king. Then the king commanded: 'Go and cut off <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s hands, feet, ears, and nose, and abandon her in the cremation ground.'

body.text: yāvattairvāsavadattā hastapādau karṇanāse ca chittvā śmaśāne choritā / yāvad upaguptena śrutaṃ vāsavadatā hastapādau karṇanāse ca chittvā śmaśāne choritā / tasya buddhirutpannā / pūrvaṃ tayā mama viṣayanimittaṃ darśanamākāṅkṣitaṃ / idāniṃ tu tasyā hastapādau karṇanāse ca vikartitau / idānīṃ tu tasya darśanakāla iti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: So they cut off <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s hands, feet, ears, and nose, and abandoned her in the cremation ground. When <s>Upagupta</s> heard that <s>Vāsavadattā</s> had been mutilated — hands, feet, ears, and nose cut off — and abandoned in the cremation ground, the following thought arose in him: 'Previously she longed to see me, motivated by sensual desire. Now her hands, feet, ears, and nose have been cut off. Now indeed is the time to see her.' And he said:

children.translated_text: When she was clad in fine garments and adorned with various ornaments,

children.text: mokṣārthināṃ janmaparāṅmukhāṇāṃ śreyastadāsyāstu na darśanaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: for those seeking liberation, turned away from birth, it would not have been good to see her.
But now is the time to see her, whose pride, passion, and joy have departed,
whose form, fixed by nature, has been mutilated by sharp swords.

body.text: yāvadekena dārakeṇa upasthāyakena chatramādāya praśānteneryāpathena śmaśānamanuprāptaḥ / tasyāśca preṣikā pūrvaguṇānurāgāt samīpe 'vasthitā kākādīn nivārayati / tayā ca vāsavadattāyā niveditaṃ /
body.translated_text: Taking an umbrella carried by a young attendant-boy, he proceeded with calm deportment to the cremation ground. Her maidservant, out of attachment to her former good qualities, stood nearby, driving away crows and the like. She informed <s>Vāsavadattā</s>:

body.text: āryuduhitaryasya tvayāhaṃ sakāśaṃ punaḥ punaranupreṣitā ayaṃ sa upagupto 'bhyāgataḥ / niyatameṣa kāmarāgārta āgato bhaviṣyati / śrutvā ca vāsavadattā kathayati /
body.translated_text: 'Noble lady, the one to whom I was sent again and again on your behalf — that <s>Upagupta</s> has arrived. Surely he has come afflicted by passionate desire.' Hearing this, <s>Vāsavadattā</s> said:

children.translated_text: Seeing me whose beauty is destroyed, suffering, stained with blood upon the ground,
how could there be passionate desire in him?

body.text: tataḥ preṣikāmuvāca / yau hastapādau karṇānāse ca maccharīrād vikartitau tau śleṣayeti / tayā yāvac chleṣayitvā paṭṭakena pracchāditā / upaguptaścāgatya vāsavadattāyā agrataḥ sthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then she said to the maidservant: 'Reattach the hands, feet, ears, and nose that have been cut from my body.' The maidservant reattached them and covered her with a cloth. <s>Upagupta</s> came and stood before <s>Vāsavadattā</s>.

body.text: tato vāsavadattā upaguptamagrataḥ sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati / āryaputra, yadā macchaśarīraṃ svasthabhūtaṃ viṣayaratyanukūlaṃ tadā mayā āryaputrasya punaḥ punar dūtī visarjitā / āryaputreṇābhihitaṃ / ākālaste bhagini mama darśanāyeti / idānīṃ mama hastapādau karṇanāse ca vikartitau / svarudhirakardama evāvasthitā / idānīṃ kimāgato 'si / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, seeing <s>Upagupta</s> standing before her, said: 'Noble son, when my body was healthy and suited for sensual pleasure, I sent a messenger to you again and again. You, noble son, said: "It is not the right time, sister, for you to see me." Now my hands, feet, ears, and nose have been cut off. I stand here in the mud of my own blood. Why have you come now?' And she said:

children.translated_text: When this body of mine, soft as a lotus bud, adorned with precious garments and ornaments,

children.text: babhūva gātraṃ mama darśanakṣamaṃ tadā na dṛṣṭo 'si mayālpabhāgyayā //
children.translated_text: was fit to be seen, then you were not seen by me, the unfortunate one.

children.text: etarhi kiṃ drāṣṭumihāgato 'si me yadā śarīraṃ mama darśanākṣamaṃ /
children.translated_text: Now why have you come here to see me, when my body is no longer fit to be seen,
bereft of playfulness, pleasure, joy, and wonder, terrifying, smeared with blood and mud?

body.text: upagupta uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Upagupta</s> said:

children.translated_text: I have not come to your presence, sister, afflicted by desire;
I have come to see the true nature of desires, which are inauspicious.
Concealed by garments, ornaments, and other external adornments favorable to passion,

children.text: nirīkṣyamāṇāpi hi yatnavabhdirnāpyatra dṛṣṭāsi bhavedyathā ca //
children.translated_text: even when carefully examined, you could not be truly seen as you really are.

children.text: idaṃ tu rūpaṃ tava dṛṣyametat sthitaṃ svabhāve racanād viyuktaṃ /
children.translated_text: But this form of yours is now to be seen, standing in its true nature, stripped of all adornment;

children.text: te 'paṇḍitāste ca vigarhaṇīyā ye prākṛte 'smin kṛṇape ramante //
children.translated_text: those who are unwise and those who are blameworthy — they delight in this ordinary, vile body.
Covered with skin, drenched in blood, wrapped in hide, thickly coated with flesh,

children.text: śirāsahasraiśca vṛte samantāt ko nāma rajyeta kutaḥ śarīre //
children.translated_text: surrounded on all sides by thousands of veins — who indeed would be attracted to, let alone attached to, such a body?

body.text: api ca bhagini /
body.translated_text: Moreover, sister:

children.translated_text: Seeing the outwardly beautiful forms, the fool becomes attached;
knowing them to be internally corrupt, the wise one becomes detached.
The impurity of this most degraded corpse, however degraded, is evident;
yet those seized by desire, having the notion of purity, regard these objects of desire as pure.

body.text: iha hi /
body.translated_text: For indeed:

children.translated_text: The foul smell is counteracted by various perfumes, though the body is a source of impurity;
the deformity is covered externally by various garments and ornaments;
the impurities of sweat, moisture, and filth are washed away with water —
yet this inauspicious, impure skeleton is resorted to by those enslaved by desire.

children.text: saṃbuddhasya tu te vacaḥ suvacasaḥ śṛṇvanti kurvantyapi
children.translated_text: But those who hear the words of the Fully Awakened One, the eloquent speaker, and act upon them,

children.text: te kāmān śramaśokaduḥkhajananān sabhdiḥ sadā garhitān /
children.translated_text: abandoning those desires — always condemned by the good — which generate toil, grief, and suffering,
with minds freed from the cause of desire, they go forth into the peaceful forest,

children.text: pāraṃ yānti bhavārṇavasya mahataḥ saṃśritya mārgaplavaṃ //
children.translated_text: and cross to the far shore of the great ocean of existence (<s>bhavārṇava</s>), having taken the raft of the Path.

body.text: śrutvā vāsavadattā saṃsārādudvignā buddhaguṇānusmaraṇāc cāvarjitahṛdayovāca /
body.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, filled with revulsion toward <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) and with a heart won over by recollecting the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>, said:

children.text: evametat tathā sarvaṃ yathā vadati paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is exactly so, all is just as the wise one says;

children.text: me tvāṃ sādhu samasādya buddhasya vacanaṃ śrutaṃ //
children.translated_text: by fortunately meeting you, I have heard the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: yāvad upaguptena vāsavadattāyā anupūrvikāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyāni saṃprakāśitāni / upaguptaśca vāsavadattāyāḥ śarīrasvabhāvamavagamya kāmadhātuvairāgyaṃ gataḥ / tena ātmiyayā dharmadeśanayā saha satyābhisamayād anāgāmiphalaṃ vāsavadattayā ca śrotāpattiphalaṃ prāptaṃ / tato vāsavadattā dṛṣṭasatyā upaguptaṃ saṃrāgayantī uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upagupta</s> gave <s>Vāsavadattā</s> a gradual discourse and revealed the <s>Noble Truths</s> (<s>Satya</s>) to her. And <s>Upagupta</s>, having understood the true nature of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s body, attained dispassion toward the realm of desire (<s>Kāmadhātu</s>). Through his own teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, together with the realization of the Truths, he attained the fruit of <s>Anāgāmin</s> (Non-returner), and <s>Vāsavadattā</s> attained the fruit of <s>Śrotāpatti</s> (Stream-entry). Then <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, having seen the Truths, spoke to <s>Upagupta</s> with devotion:

children.translated_text: By your spiritual power, the terrifying path to the lower realms, full of many faults, has been closed;
the supremely meritorious path to heaven has been opened, and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found by me.

body.text: api ca / eṣāhaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ tathagatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi / dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṅghaṃ cetyāha /
body.translated_text: Moreover: 'I go for refuge to that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>). I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s> and to the community of monks (<s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>),' she said.

children.translated_text: I go for refuge to the Victor (<s>Jina</s>), whose eyes are pure, white, and immaculate like fresh lotuses,
who is accompanied by gods and wise beings, who is free from passion — and to the <s>Saṅgha</s> as well.

body.text: yāvad upagupto vāsavadattāṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya prakrāntaḥ / aciraprakrānte copagupte vāsavadattā kālagatā deveṣūpapannā / daivataiśca mathurāyāmārocitaṃ / vāsavadattayā upaguptasakāśād dharmadeśanāṃ śrutvā āryasatyāni dṛṣṭāni / sā kālagatā deveṣūpapanneti / śrutvā ca mathurāvāstavyena janakāyena vāsavadattāyāḥ śarire pūjā kṛtā /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upagupta</s>, having instructed <s>Vāsavadattā</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, departed. Not long after <s>Upagupta</s>'s departure, <s>Vāsavadattā</s> died and was reborn among the gods. The deities announced in <s>Mathurā</s>: '<s>Vāsavadattā</s>, having heard the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> from <s>Upagupta</s>, saw the <s>Noble Truths</s>. She has died and been reborn among the gods.' Hearing this, the people of <s>Mathurā</s> performed worship at <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s body.

body.text: yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikam abhigamyovāca / anujānīhi upaguptaṃ pravrājayiṣyāmīti / gupto gāndhika uvāca / ārya eṣa samayaḥ / yadā na lābho na chedo bhaviṣyati tadānujñāsyāmīti /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> went to <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller and said: 'Permit me to ordain <s>Upagupta</s> as a monk.' <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller said: 'Venerable one, this is my condition: when there is neither profit nor loss in business, then I will give permission.'

body.text: yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsinā ṛddhyā tathādhiṣṭhitaṃ yathā na lābho na chedaḥ / tato gupto gāndhiko gaṇayati tulayati māpayati / paśyati na lābho na chedaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s>, through his supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), arranged it so that there was neither profit nor loss. Then <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller counted, weighed, and measured, and saw that there was neither profit nor loss.

body.text: tataḥ sthaviraśaṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikam uvāca / ayaṃ hi bhagavatā buddhena nirdiṣṭaḥ, mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyatīti / anujānīhi pravrājayiṣyāmīti /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> said to <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller: 'This one was designated by the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> himself: "A hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), he will carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>." Give your permission — I will ordain him.'

body.text: yāvad guptena gāndhekena abhyanujñātaḥ / tataḥ sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-seller gave his consent. The Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s>

body.text: upagupto naṭabhaṭikāraṇyāyatanaṃ nītaṃ / upasaṃpāditaśca jñapticaturthaṃ ca karma vyavasitaṃ / upaguptena ca sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: took <s>Upagupta</s> to the forest monastery of <s>Naṭabhaṭikāraṇya</s>. He was given full ordination (<s>upasaṃpadā</s>), and the formal act with the fourth proclamation was completed. And <s>Upagupta</s>, through the complete abandonment of all defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat).

body.text: tataḥ sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinābhihitaṃ / vatsa upagupta tvaṃ bhagavatā nirdiṣṭo varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mama upagupto nāma bhikṣurbhaviṣyati, alakṣaṇakto buddhaḥ / yo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyatīti / eṣo 'gro me ānanda śrāvakāṇāmavavādakānāṃ yadutopagupto bhikṣuḥ / idānīṃ vatsa śāsanahitaṃ kuruṣveti / upagupta uvāca / evamastviti /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> said: 'Son <s>Upagupta</s>, you were designated by the Blessed One: "A hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a monk named <s>Upagupta</s>, a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks. He will carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s> a hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>." "This one, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the foremost among my disciples who are instructors — namely, the monk <s>Upagupta</s>." Now, son, carry out the welfare of the Teaching.' <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'So be it.'

body.text: tataḥ sa dharmaśravaṇe 'dhīṣṭaḥ / mathurāyāṃ ca śabdo visṛtaḥ / upagupto nāmālakṣaṇako buddho 'dya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyatīti / śrutvā cānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi nirgatāni /
body.translated_text: Then he devoted himself to hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. And in <s>Mathurā</s> the word spread: 'The one named <s>Upagupta</s>, a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks, will teach the <s>Dharma</s> today.' Hearing this, many hundreds of thousands of living beings came forth.

body.text: yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ samāpadyāvalokayati / kathaṃ tathāgatasya pariṣan niṣaṇṇāḥ / paśyati cārdhacandrikākāreṇa parṣad avasthitā / yavad avalokayati kathaṃ tathāgatena dharmadeśanā kṛtā / paśyati pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyasaṃprakāśanā kṛtā / so 'pi pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyasaṃprakāśanāṃ kartumārabdhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, entering meditation (<s>samāpatti</s>), contemplated: 'How was the assembly of the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated?' He saw that the assembly was arranged in a half-moon shape. Then he contemplated: 'How did the <s>Tathāgata</s> give his teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>?' He saw that he first told a story of past deeds and then revealed the Truths. He too began by telling a story of past deeds and then proceeded to reveal the Truths.

body.text: māreṇa ca tasyāṃ parṣadi muktāhāravarṣamutsṛṣṭaṃ / vaineyānāṃ manāṃsi vyākulīkṛtāni / ekenāpi satyadarśanaṃ na kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: But <s>Māra</s> (the Evil One) released a shower of pearl necklaces upon that assembly. The minds of those to be trained were thrown into confusion. Not even one attained the vision of the Truths.

body.text: yāvat sthaviropagupto vyavalokayati / kenāyaṃ vyākṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ / paśyati māreṇa /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> looked about: 'By whom was this disturbance caused?' He saw that it was by <s>Māra</s>.

body.text: yāvad dvitīye divase bahutarako janakāyo nirgataḥ / upagupto dharmaṃ deśayati / muktāhāraṃ ca varṣopavarṣitamiti / yāvad dvitīye 'pi divase sthaviropaguptena pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyasaṃprakāśanāyāmārabdhāyāṃ māreṇa cāsya parṣadi suvarṇavarṣamutsṛṣṭaṃ / vaineyānāṃ manāṃsi saṃkṣobhotāni / ekenāpi satyadarśanaṃ na kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then on the second day, an even larger crowd came out. <s>Upagupta</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. And a rain of pearls fell. On that second day too, when the elder <s>Upagupta</s> had completed the preliminary discourse and begun the exposition of the [Four Noble] Truths, <s>Māra</s> released a shower of gold upon his assembly. The minds of those to be converted were disturbed. Not even one attained the vision of truth.

body.text: yāvat sthaviropagupto vyavalokayati, kenāyaṃ vyākṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ / paśyati māreṇa pāpīyaseti /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s> reflects: 'By whom has this disruption been caused?' He sees: 'By <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One.'

body.text: yāvat tṛtīye divase bahutarako janakāyo nirgataḥ / upagupto dharmaṃ deśayati / muktāvarṣaṃ suvarṇavarṣaṃ ca patatīti / yāvat tṛtīye 'pi divase sthaviropaguptaḥ pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyāni ārabdhaḥ saṃprakāśayituṃ / māreṇa ca nātīdūre nāṭakamārabdhaṃ / divyāni ca vādyāni saṃpravāditāni / divyāścāpsaraso nāṭayituṃ pravṛttāḥ / yāvad vītarāgo janakāyo divyāni rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā divyāṃśca śabdān śrutvā māreṇākṛṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then on the third day, an even larger crowd came out. <s>Upagupta</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. A rain of pearls and a rain of gold fell. On that third day too, the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having completed the preliminary discourse, began to reveal the [Four Noble] Truths. But <s>Māra</s> started a theatrical performance not far away. Divine instruments were played. Divine <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) began to dance. And the crowd, though free from passion, seeing the divine forms and hearing the divine sounds, was drawn away by <s>Māra</s>.

body.text: ato māreṇopaguptasya parṣad ākṛṣṭā / prītamanasā māreṇa
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Māra</s> drew away <s>Upagupta</s>'s assembly. With delighted mind, <s>Māra</s>

body.text: sthaviropaguptasya śirasi mālā baddhā / yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ samanvāharitumārabdhaḥ / ko 'yaṃ / paśyati māraḥ / tasya buddhirutpannā / ayaṃ māro bhagavacchāsane mahāntaṃ vyākṣepaṃ karoti / kimarthamayaṃ bhagavatā na vinītaḥ / paśyati mamāyaṃ vineyaḥ / tasya ca vinayāt sattvānugrahādahaṃ bhagavatā alakṣaṇako buddho nirdiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: bound a garland on the elder <s>Upagupta</s>'s head. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s> began to reflect: 'Who is this?' He sees: '<s>Māra</s>.' This thought arose in him: 'This <s>Māra</s> causes great disruption to the Blessed One's teaching. Why was he not disciplined by the Blessed One?' He sees: 'He is to be disciplined by me. And because of his discipline and the benefit it brings to beings, the Blessed One designated me as a <s>Buddha</s> without the [bodily] marks.'

body.text: yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ samanvāharati / kimasya vineyakāla upasthita āhosvin neti / paśyati vineyakāla upasthitaḥ / tataḥ sthaviropaguptena trayaḥ kuṇapā gṛhītāḥ / ahikuṇapaṃ kurkuskuṇapaṃ manuṣyakuṇapaṃ ca / ṛddhyā ca puṣpamālāmabhinirmāya mārasakāśamabhigataḥ / dṛṣṭvā ca mārasya prītirutpannā / upagupto 'pi mayākṛṣṭa iti /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s> reflects: 'Has the time for his discipline arrived, or not?' He sees: 'The time for his discipline has arrived.' Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s> took three corpses — a snake's corpse, a dog's corpse, and a human corpse. Through his supernatural power, he created a flower garland [in appearance] and approached <s>Māra</s>. Upon seeing him, <s>Māra</s> was delighted, [thinking]: '<s>Upagupta</s> too has been attracted by me.'

body.text: tato māreṇa svaśarīramupanāmitaṃ / sthaviropaguptaḥ svayameva badhnāti / tataḥ sthavireṇopaguptena ahikuṇapaṃ mārasya śirasi baddhaṃ / kurkurakuṇapaṃ grīvāyāṃ karṇāvasaktaṃ manuṣyakuṇapaṃ ca / tataḥ samālabhyovāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> offered his own body [for the garland]. The elder <s>Upagupta</s> himself binds [them]. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s> bound the snake's corpse on <s>Māra</s>'s head, the dog's corpse on his neck, and the human corpse hanging from his ears. Then, touching [them in blessing], he said:

children.text: bhikṣujanapratikūlā mālā baddhā yathaiva me bhavatā /
children.translated_text: 'Just as a garland offensive to a monk was bound on me by you,
So this corpse, offensive to a lover of pleasure, has been bound on you by me.'

body.text: yat te balaṃ bhavati tat pratidarśayasva buddhātmajena hi sahādya samāgato 'si / ugdṛttamapyanilabhinnataraṅgavaktraṃ vyāvartate malayakukṣiṣu sāgarāmbhaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Whatever power you have, display it now — for today you have encountered a son of the <s>Buddha</s>. Even the ocean waters, though swelling with wind-tossed wave-crests, turn back in the hollows of the <s>Malaya</s> [mountains].'

body.text: atha mārastaṃ kuṇapamapanetumārabdhaḥ / paramapi ca svayamanupraviśya pipīlika iva adrirājamapanetuṃ na śaśāka / sāmarṣo vaihāyasamutpatya uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> began trying to remove those corpses. But even entering into himself with all his might, like an ant trying to move the king of mountains, he could not remove them. Full of anger, he flew up into the sky and said:

children.text: yadi moktuṃ na śakyāmi kaṇṭhāt svakuṇapaṃ svayaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'If I myself cannot free this corpse from my neck,
Other gods, superior to me in splendor, will surely free me.'

body.text: sthavira uvāca /
body.translated_text: The elder said:

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ vajra śaraṇaṃ śatakratuṃ vā dīptaṃ vā praviśa hutāśamarṇavaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: 'Go to <s>Brahmā</s>, to the thunderbolt-wielder <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>), or enter the blazing fire of <s>Hutāśana</s> (<s>Agni</s>), or the ocean —

children.text: na kledaṃ na ca pariśoṣaṇaṃ na bhedaṃ kaṇṭhasthaṃ kuṇapamidaṃ tu yāsyatīha //
children.translated_text: This corpse lodged on your neck shall not be moistened, nor dried, nor split here.'

body.text: sa mahendrarudropendradraviṇeśvarayamavaruṇakuveravasavādīnāṃ devānāmabhigamya akṛtārtha eva brahmāṇamabhigataḥ /
body.translated_text: He went to <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Draviṇeśvara</s> (lord of wealth), <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kuvera</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and other gods, and having failed with all of them, he went to <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text: tena coktaṃ /
body.translated_text: And he [<s>Brahmā</s>] said:

body.text: marṣaya vatsa /
body.translated_text: 'Be patient, my child.'

children.translated_text: 'The disciple of the Tenfold-Powered One [the <s>Buddha</s>] has established a boundary through his own supernatural power;
Who could break it? — as [none can break] the shore of <s>Varuṇa</s>'s abode [the ocean].'
'One might perhaps lift <s>Himavat</s> bound with lotus-fiber threads,
But I could not lift this dog's corpse attached to your neck.'

children.text: kāmaṃ mamāpi mahadasti balaṃ tathāpi nāhaṃ tathāgatasutasya balena tulyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Though indeed I too have great power, still I am not equal in power to a son of the <s>Tathāgata</s>;

children.text: tejasvināṃ na khalu na jvalane 'sti kintu nāsau dyutirhutavahe ravimaṇḍaleyā //
children.translated_text: It is not that the brilliant ones have no splendor in fire, but the radiance of fire is not that of the sun's disk.'

body.text: māro 'bravīt / kimidānīmājñāpayasi / kaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said: 'What then do you command? To whom shall I go for refuge?'

body.text: brahmābravīt /
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: śīghraṃ tameva śaraṇaṃ vraja yaṃ sametya bhraṣṭastvamṛddhivibhavād yaśasaḥ sukhācca /
children.translated_text: 'Quickly go for refuge to that very one, encountering whom you have been stripped of your supernatural power, glory, and happiness;

children.text: bhraṣṭo hi yaḥ kṣititale bhavatīha janturuttiṣṭhati kṣitimasāvavalambya bhūyaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a being who has fallen to the earth's surface here rises again by leaning upon the earth itself.'

body.text: atha mārastathāgataśiṣyasāmarthyamupalabhya cintayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>, having realized the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciple, reflected:

children.translated_text: 'He whose disciples' authority is honored even by <s>Brahmā</s> —

children.text: tasya buddhasya sāmarthyaṃ pramātuṃ ko nu śaknuyāt //
children.translated_text: Who could measure the power of that <s>Buddha</s>?'

children.text: kartukāmo 'bhaviṣyat kāṃ śiṣṭiṃ kṣamo na suvrataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What discipline would the keeper of noble vows not have been capable of imposing?
But [that discipline] which he did not impose through patience — by that I have been protected.'

body.text: kiṃ bahunā /
body.translated_text: In short —

body.text:
adyāvaimi munermahākaruṇatāṃ tasyātimaitrātmanaḥ
sarvopadravavipramuktamanasaścāmīkarādridyutiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Today I understand the great compassion of that sage, whose nature is supreme friendliness, whose mind is free from all afflictions, whose radiance is like a golden mountain;

body.text:
mohāndhena hi tatra tatra sa mayā taistairnayaiḥ kheditaḥ
tenāhaṃ ca tathāpi nāma balinā naivāpriyaṃ śrāvitaḥ //
body.translated_text: For I, blinded by delusion, wearied him here and there with various stratagems, and yet he, the powerful one, never uttered anything unpleasant to me.'

body.text: atha kāmadhātvadhipatirmāro nāstyanyā gatir anyatra upaguptakādeveti jñātvā sarvamutsṛjya sthaviropaguptasamīpamupetya pādayornipatyovāca / bhadanta kimaviditametad bhadantasya yathā bodhimūlamupādāya mayā bhagavato vipriyaśatāni kṛtāni / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>, lord of the realm of desire, knowing that there was no other refuge except the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, abandoning everything, came to the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, fell at his feet, and said: 'Venerable sir, is it unknown to you that from the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree onward, I committed hundreds of offenses against the Blessed One? For example —'

children.translated_text: 'In the brahmin village, in the [alms-]hall, that <s>Gautama</s>, having encountered me,
Even upon being deprived of food, did not cause me displeasure.'
'Having become a bull, having stood as a serpent, having assumed the form of a carter —

children.text: sa mayāyāsito nātho na cāhaṃ tena hiṃsitaḥ //
children.translated_text: The Lord was harassed by me, and yet I was not harmed by him.'

children.text: tvayā punarahaṃ vīra tyaktvā hi sahajāṃ dayāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'But you, O hero, having abandoned your innate compassion,
Have today humiliated me before the worlds of gods and <s>asuras</s>.'

body.text: sthaviro 'bravīt / pāpīyān kathamaparīkṣyaiva tathagatamāhātmyeṣu śrāvakamupasaṃharasi /
body.translated_text: The elder said: 'O Evil One, how can you, without proper examination, compare a disciple to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s greatness?'

children.translated_text: 'Do you equate <s>Meru</s> with a mustard seed here,
The sun with a firefly, or the ocean with a handful [of water]?'

children.text: anyā hi sā daśabalasya kṛpā prajāsu
children.translated_text: 'For the compassion of the Tenfold-Powered One toward beings is one thing,
But a disciple does not possess the great compassion, O gentle one.'

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: 'The reason why the Blessed One tolerated you despite your offenses —
That very cause has been directly perceived by us.'

body.text: māra uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said:

children.text: brūhi brūhi śrīmatastasya bhāvaṃ saṅgaṃ chettuṃ kṣāntiguptavratasya /
children.translated_text: 'Tell me, tell me the intention of that glorious one, whose vow is guarded by patience, [so as] to cut my attachment;

children.text: yau'sau mohānnityamāyasito me tenāhaṃ ca prekṣito maitracittaiḥ //
children.translated_text: He whom I, out of delusion, constantly harassed — and yet he looked upon me with eyes of friendliness.'

body.text: sthavira uvāca / śṛṇu saumya tvaṃ hi bhagavatyasakṛdasakṛdavaskhalitaḥ / na ca buddhāvaropitānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanyat prakṣālanamanyatra tathāgataprasādādeva /
body.translated_text: The elder said: 'Listen, gentle one — you have stumbled again and again against the Blessed One. And there is no other means to cleanse the unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> generated against a <s>Buddha</s>, except through faith in the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone.'

children.translated_text: 'Seeing this cause, that far-sighted one

children.text: tvaṃ nāpriyamiha proktaḥ priyāṇyeva tu lambhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Did not utter anything unpleasant to you here, but rather granted you only pleasant things.'
'By this method, devotion was generated in your heart by that foremost of minds;
For even a little devotion in the wise becomes the fruit of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: saṃkṣepād yat kṛtaṃ te vṛjinamiha munermohāndhamanasā
children.translated_text: 'In short, whatever sin was committed by you against the sage, blinded by delusion in mind,
All of that has been washed away by the streams of faith-water arising in your heart.'

body.text: atha māraḥ kadambapuṣpavad āhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ sarvāṅgeṇa praṇipatyovāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>, his hair-pores bristling like <s>kadamba</s> flowers, prostrated with his whole body and said:

children.translated_text: 'Rightly was he wearied by me in many ways,
And [rightly did he] beforehand fulfill the wish for enlightenment on earth;
And all was forgiven by that best of sages,
As a father [forgives] the offense of a son, with affection.'

body.text: sa buddhaprasādāpyayitamanāḥ suciraṃ buddhaguṇānanusmṛtya sthavirasya pādayornipatyovāca /
body.translated_text: He, his mind flooded with reverence for the <s>Buddha</s>, having long contemplated the <s>Buddha</s>'s virtues, fell at the elder's feet and said:

children.text: anugraho me 'dya paraḥ kṛtastvayā niveśitaṃ yan mayi buddhagauravaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'The supreme favor has been done to me today by you — that you have established in me reverence for the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: idaṃ tu kaṇṭhavyavalambi maitryā maharṣikopābharaṇaṃ visarjaya //
children.translated_text: But this [corpse] hanging on my neck — release it with friendliness, O ornament of the great sage's wrath.'

body.text: sthavira uvāca / samayato vimokṣyāmīti / māra uvāca / kaḥ samaya iti / sthavira uvāca / adyaprabhṛti bhikṣavo na viheṭhayitavyā iti / māro 'bravīt / na viheṭhayiṣye / kimaparamājñāpayasīti / sthavira uvāca / evaṃ tāvacchāsanakāryaṃ prati mamājñā / svakāryaṃ prati vijñāpayiṣyāmi bhavantaṃ / māraḥ sasambhrama uvāca / prasīda sthavira kimājñāpayasīti / sthaviro 'bravīt / svayamavagacchasi yadahaṃ varṣaśataparinirvṛte bhagavati pravrajitaḥ / tad
body.translated_text: The elder said: 'I shall release you on a condition.' <s>Māra</s> said: 'What is the condition?' The elder said: 'From today onward, you must not harass the monks.' <s>Māra</s> said: 'I shall not harass them. What else do you command?' The elder said: 'First, this is my command regarding the affairs of the teaching. Regarding my own personal matter, I shall make a request of you.' <s>Māra</s>, agitated, said: 'Be pleased, O elder — what do you command?' The elder said: 'You yourself know that I went forth [as a monk] when the Blessed One had already passed away a hundred years ago. Therefore —'

children.translated_text: 'I have seen the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (body of doctrine) of that lord of the three worlds,
But I have not seen his <s>Rūpakāya</s> (physical body), whose radiance was like a golden mountain.'
'Therefore, as an incomparable favor to me, display here the <s>Buddha</s>'s form;

children.text: priyamadhikamato hi nāsti me daśabalarūpakutūhalo hyahaṃ //
children.translated_text: For there is nothing dearer to me than this — I am filled with curiosity about the form of the Tenfold-Powered One.'

body.text: māra uvāca / tena hi mamāpi samayaḥ śrūyatāṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said: 'Then hear my condition as well.'

children.translated_text: 'When you see me here suddenly wearing the <s>Buddha</s>'s guise,
You must not make obeisance, out of reverence for the Omniscient One's qualities.'

children.text: buddhānusmṛtipeśalena manasā pūjāṃ yadi tva mayi
children.translated_text: 'If, with a mind tender through recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, you display toward me
Even the slightest worship, O lord, I shall be burned.
What power have I to endure the act of prostration performed by one free from passion?
Castor-oil saplings cannot bear the weight of an elephant's foot-step.'

body.text: sthaviropyāha / evamastu / na bhavantaṃ praṇamiṣyāmīti / māro 'bravīt / tena muhūrtamāgamasva yāvadahaṃ vanagahanamanupraviśya
body.translated_text: The elder also said: 'So be it — I shall not bow to you.' <s>Māra</s> said: 'Then wait a moment while I enter the deep forest —'

children.translated_text: 'That <s>Buddha</s>-form, radiant as heated gold, which was once created by me
Through the inconceivable power of the <s>Buddha</s>, in order to deceive a hero —
Having assumed that same form, delightful to the eyes of living beings,
I shall come, casting [around me] a spotless halo of sun-rays.'

body.text: atha sthavira evamastu ityuktvā taṃ kuṇapamapanīya tathāgatarūpadarśanotsuko 'vasthitaḥ / māraśca vanagahanamanupraviśya buddharūpaṃ kṛtvā naṭa iva saruciranepathyastasmādvanagahanādārabdhoniṣkramituṃ / vakṣyate hi /
body.translated_text: Then the elder, having said 'So be it' and removed the corpses, stood eagerly awaiting the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s form. And <s>Māra</s>, entering the deep forest and assuming the <s>Buddha</s>'s form, began to emerge from that forest thicket like an actor in a splendid costume. For it is said:

children.translated_text: 'Displaying the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, rich in supreme marks, bringing peace to the eyes of men,
Unrolling [it] like a freshly colored painting of great value, he adorned that forest.'

body.text: atha vyāmaprabhāmaṇḍalamaṇḍitamasecanakadarśanaṃ bhagavato rūpamabhinirmāya dakṣiṇe pārśve sthaviraśāradvatīputraṃ vāmapārśve sthaviramahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ pṛṣṭhaścāyuṣmantamānandaṃ buddhapātravyagrahastaṃ sthaviramahākāśyapāniruddhasubhūtiprabhṛtīnāṃ
body.translated_text: Then, having created the Blessed One's form, adorned with a halo of light one <s>vyāma</s> (fathom) in extent, beautiful beyond description — on the right side the elder <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>), on the left side the elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, behind him the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> with the <s>Buddha</s>'s bowl in his hands, and the forms of the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, and other

body.text: ca mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ rūpāṇyabhinirmāya ardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśatairardhacandreṇānuparivṛtaṃ buddhaveśamādarśayitvā māraḥ sthaviropaguptasyāntikamājagāma / sthaviropaguptasya ca bhagavato rūpamidamidṛśamiti prāmodyamutpannaṃ /
body.translated_text: great disciples, surrounded in a half-moon formation by twelve hundred and fifty monks — having displayed this <s>Buddha</s>-guise, <s>Māra</s> came to the elder <s>Upagupta</s>. And in the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, the joyful thought arose: 'So this is what the Blessed One's form was like!'

body.text: sa pramuditamanāstvaritamāsanādutthāya nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca /
body.translated_text: He, with delighted mind, rising swiftly from his seat and gazing [at the form], said:

children.text: dhigastu tāṃ niṣkaruṇāmanityatāṃ bhinatti rūpāṇi yadīdṛśānyapi /
children.translated_text: 'Shame upon that merciless impermanence, which shatters even such forms as these!

children.text: śarīramīdṛk kila tanmahāmuner anityatāṃ prāpya vināśamāgataṃ //
children.translated_text: Such indeed was the body of that great sage — having met with impermanence, it came to destruction.'

body.text: sa buddhāvalambitayā smṛtyā tathāpyāsaktamanāḥ saṃvṛtto yathā buddhaṃ bhagavantamahaṃ paśyāmīti vyaktamupāgataḥ / sa padmamukulapratimamañjaliṃ kṛtvovāca / aho rūpaśobhāḥ bhagavataḥ / kiṃ bahunā /
body.translated_text: He, with his mind fixed on the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, became so absorbed that it was as if he clearly perceived: "I am seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One)." Joining his palms together like the bud of a lotus, he said: "Oh, the splendor of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s form! What more can be said?"

children.translated_text: With his face he surpasses the lotus, with his eyes the blue <s>utpala</s> (water lily),

children.text: kāntyā puṣpavanaṃ mana priyatayā candraṃ samāptadyutiṃ /
children.translated_text: with his radiance a garden of flowers, with his loveliness the mind, with his beauty the moon of perfect splendor,

children.text: gāmbhīryeṇa mahodadhiṃ sthiratayā meruṃ raviṃ tejasā
children.translated_text: with his depth the great ocean, with his steadfastness <s>Meru</s>, with his brilliance the sun,
with his gait the lion, with his glance the bull, and with his complexion pure gold.

body.text: sa bhūyasā mātrayā harṣeṇāpūryamāṇahṛdayo vyāpinā svareṇovāca /
body.translated_text: He, his heart overflowing with ever-increasing joy, spoke in a voice that filled all directions:

children.translated_text: "Oh, how sweet is the fruit of deeds purified through existences!
This form was created by <s>karma</s> (action), not by lordly power or by mere chance.
That which through billions of aeons, arising from speech, body, and mind,
was purified by <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), wisdom, and discipline to attain <s>arhathood</s> (worthiness),
by that was this immaculate form produced, delightful to the eyes of the people,

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā ripurapyabhipramuditaḥ syāt kiṃ punarmadvidhaḥ //
children.translated_text: upon seeing which even an enemy would be overjoyed — how much more one such as I!"

body.text: saṃbuddhālambanaiḥ saṃjñāṃ vismṛtya buddhasaṃjñāmadhiṣṭhāya mūlanikṛtta iva drūmaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa mārasya pādayornipatitaḥ / atha māraḥ sasambhramo 'bravīt / evaṃ tvaṃ bhadanta nārhasi samayaṃ vyatikramituṃ / sthavira uvāca / kaḥ samaya iti / māra uvāca / nanu pratijñātaṃ bhadantena nāhaṃ bhavantaṃ praṇamiṣyāmīti /
body.translated_text: Forgetting the perception that his support was the <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One), and establishing the perception of the <s>Buddha</s>, like a tree cut at its root he fell with his entire body at <s>Māra</s>'s feet. Then <s>Māra</s>, alarmed, said: "Venerable sir, you ought not to transgress our agreement." The elder said: "What agreement?" <s>Māra</s> said: "Did you not promise, venerable sir, 'I will not bow to you'?"

body.text: tataḥ sthavira upaguptaḥ pṛthivītalādutthāya sagadgadakaṇṭho 'bravīta / pāpīyān /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, rising from the ground, spoke with a choked voice: "O Evil One,

children.text: na khalu na viditaṃ me yat sa vādipradhāno
children.translated_text: "Indeed it is not unknown to me that that foremost of teachers,
like a fire extinguished by water, has passed into <s>nirvṛti</s> (final peace).
Yet having seen the appearance and the beauty pleasing to the eyes of that one,
I bowed to that sage — but it is not you whom I worship."

body.text: māra uvāca / kathamihāhaṃ nārcito bhavāmi yadevaṃ mā praṇamasīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said: "How is it that I am not worshipped, if you bow to me thus?"

body.text: sthaviro 'bravīt / śrūyatāṃ yathā tvaṃ naiva mayābhyarcito bhavasi na ca mayā samayātikramaḥ kṛta iti /
body.translated_text: The elder said: "Listen to how you are indeed not worshipped by me, nor have I transgressed the agreement:

children.translated_text: "Just as people, before clay images of the gods,
disregarding the perception of clay, bow with the perception of the divine,
so I, seeing you here bearing the form of the <s>Lokanātha</s> (Protector of the World),
disregarding the perception of <s>Māra</s>, bowed with the perception of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)."

body.text: atha māro buddhaveśamantardhāpayitvā sthaviropaguptamabhyarcya prakrāntaḥ / yāvac caturthe divase māraḥ svayameva mathurāyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣittumārabdhaḥ / yo yuṣmākaṃ svargāpavargasukhaṃ prārthayate sa sthaviropaguptasakāśād dharmaṃ śṛṇotu / yaiśca yuṣmābhistathāgato na dṛṣṭaste sthaviropaguptaṃ paśyantviti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>, having made the guise of the <s>Buddha</s> disappear, paid homage to the elder <s>Upagupta</s> and departed. On the fourth day, <s>Māra</s> himself began to ring bells throughout <s>Mathurā</s>, proclaiming: "Whoever among you desires the happiness of heaven and liberation, let him hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the elder <s>Upagupta</s>! And those among you who have not seen the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), let them see the elder <s>Upagupta</s>!" And he said:

children.translated_text: "Abandoning poverty, the root of misfortune, whoever desires resplendent and glorious prosperity,

children.text: svargāpavargāya ca yasya vāñchā sa śraddhayā dharmamataḥ śṛṇotu //
children.translated_text: and whoever has the wish for heaven and liberation, let him hear the <s>Dharma</s> here with faith!

children.text: dṛṣṭo na yairvā dvipadapradhānaḥ śāstā mahākāruṇikāḥ svayambhūḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have not seen the foremost of bipeds, the Teacher, the greatly compassionate, self-born one,

children.text: te śāstṛkalpaṃ sthaviropaguptaṃ paśyantu bhāsvat tribhavapradīpaṃ //
children.translated_text: let them behold the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, who is like the Teacher, a brilliant lamp of the three worlds!"

body.text: yāvan mathurāyāṃ śabdo visṛtaḥ sthaviropaguptena māro vinīta iti / śrutvā ca yabhdūyasā mathurāvāstavyo janakāyaḥ sthaviropaguptasakāśaṃ nirgataḥ / tataḥ sthaviropagupto 'nekeṣu brāhmaṇaśatasahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu siṃha iva nirbhīḥ siṃhāsanamabhirūḍho vakṣyati ca /
body.translated_text: The news spread throughout <s>Mathurā</s> that <s>Māra</s> had been tamed by the elder <s>Upagupta</s>. Upon hearing this, the greater part of the populace of <s>Mathurā</s> went forth to the elder <s>Upagupta</s>. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, when many hundreds of thousands of brahmins had assembled, fearless as a lion, ascended the lion-throne. And it is said:

children.text: māṃ prati na tena śakyaṃ siṃhāsanamaviduṣā samabhiroḍhuṃ /
children.translated_text: "It is not possible for an ignorant person to ascend the lion-throne in my presence;

children.text: yas [tu] siṃhāsanastho mṛga iva sa hi yāti saṅkocaṃ //
children.translated_text: he who sits on the lion-throne yet shrinks like a deer — he is unworthy.
But he who, fearless as a lion, roars forth to destroy the pride of rival debaters,
that lion among preachers is worthy to ascend the lion-throne."

body.text: yāvat sthaviropaguptena pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyāni saṃprakāśitāni / śrutvā cānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair mokṣabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlānyākṣiptāni / kaiścidanāgāmiphalaṃ prāptaṃ / kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ / kaiścic chrotāpattiphalaṃ / yāvadaṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi pravrajitāni / sarvaiśca yujyamānairyāvadarhattvaṃ prāptaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having first given an introductory discourse, illuminated the noble truths. Upon hearing them, many hundreds of thousands of beings planted roots of merit leading to liberation. Some attained the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner). Some attained the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner). Some attained the fruit of <s>śrotāpatti</s> (stream-entry). As many as eighteen thousand went forth into the renunciant life. And all of them, through diligent practice, attained <s>arhattva</s> (the state of the worthy one).

body.text: tatra corumuṇḍaparvate guhāṣṭādaśahastā dīrgheṇa dvādaśahastā vistareṇa / yadā tu kṛtakaraṇīyāḥ / saṃvṛttāstadā sthaviropaguptenābhihitaṃ / yo madīyenavavādena sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati tena caturaṅgulamātrā śalākā guhāyāṃ prakṣeptavyā /
body.translated_text: There on <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain was a cave eighteen cubits in length and twelve cubits in breadth. When all had completed their tasks, the elder <s>Upagupta</s> declared: "Whoever, through my instruction, directly realizes <s>arhattva</s> (the state of the worthy one) by the complete abandonment of all afflictions, let him cast a tally-stick of four finger-breadths into the cave."

body.text: yāvadekasmin divaseṣṭādaśabhirarhatsahasraiḥ śalākāḥ prakṣiptāḥ / tasya yāvadāsamudrāyāṃ śabdo visṛtaḥ / mathurāyamupaguptanāmā avavādakānāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā / tadyathā hi /
body.translated_text: On a single day, eighteen thousand <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones) cast their tally-sticks. His fame spread as far as the ocean. In <s>Mathurā</s>, the one named <s>Upagupta</s> was designated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) as foremost among instructors. Just as:

body.text: vinītakāmadhātvīśvare dvitīyaśāstṛkalpe mahātmani sthaviropagupte suramanujamahoragāsuragaruḍayakṣagandharvavidyādharārcitapādayugme [sati] pūrvabuddhākṣetrāvaropitakuśalabījasantatīnām anekeṣāṃ sattvaśatasahasrāṇāṃ saddharmasalilavarṣadhārānipātāmokṣāṅkurān abhyavardhayannurumuṇḍe śaile /
body.translated_text: When the great-souled elder <s>Upagupta</s>, like a second Teacher, who had tamed the lord of the desire realm, whose pair of feet was worshipped by <s>devas</s> (gods), humans, <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-bearers), was on <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain, he caused the sprouts of liberation to grow through showers of the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s> for many hundreds of thousands of beings whose seeds of merit had been planted in the fields of former Buddhas.

body.text: kāryānurodhāt praṇatasakalasāmantacūḍāmaṇimayūkhobhdāsitapādapīṭhasyāśokasya rājñaḥ pūrvaṃ pāṃśupradānaṃ samanusmariṣyāmaḥ / ityevamanuśrūyate /
body.translated_text: In accordance with duty, we shall now recall the prior gift of dirt by King <s>Aśoka</s>, at whose footstool the crest-jewel rays of all bowing vassal kings shone forth. Thus it is heard:

children.translated_text: The chapter called "The Gift of Dirt."

body.text: bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe / atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṅghapuraskṛto rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat / vakṣyati ca /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground). Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded by the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and preceded by the <s>bhikṣu-saṅgha</s> (monastic community), entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. And it is said:

children.translated_text: With his supreme body resembling a mountain of gold, moving with the graceful gait of the lord of elephants,
with a face as gentle as the full moon, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) went forth surrounded by the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks).

body.text: yāvad bhagavatā sābhisaṃskāraṃ nagaradvāre pādaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ / dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ sābhisaṃskāraṃ nagaradvāramindrakīle pādau vyavasthāpayanti / tadā citrāṇi adbhūtāni prādurbhavanti / andhāścakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante / badhirāḥ śrotragrahaṇasamarthā bhavanti / paṅgavo gamanasamarthā bhavanti / haḍinigaḍacārakāvabaddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ bandhanāni śithilībhavanti / janmajanmavairānubaddhāḥ sattvāstadanantaraṃ maitracittatāṃ labhante / vatsā dāmāni chittvā mātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ samāgacchanti / hastinaḥ krośanti / aśvā hreṣante / ṛṣabhā garjanti / śukaśārikakokilajīvajīvabarhiṇo madhurān nikūjanti / peḍāgatālaṅkārā madhuraśabdaṃ niścārayanti / aparāhatāni ca vāditrabhāṇḍāni madhuraṃ śabdaṃ niścārayanti / unnatonnatā pṛthivīpradeśā avanamanti / avanatāśconnamanti / apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālāścāvatiṣṭhante /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> deliberately placed his foot at the city gate. For it is a natural law that whenever the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, deliberately place their feet at the city gate, upon the threshold, then marvelous and wondrous things manifest: the blind regain their sight; the deaf become able to hear; the lame become able to walk; the bonds of beings bound in fetters, chains, and prisons become loose; beings bound by enmity through birth after birth thereupon attain a state of loving-kindness; calves break their tethers and come together with their mothers; elephants trumpet; horses whinny; bulls bellow; parrots, <s>śārikā</s> (mynas), cuckoos, <s>jīvajīva</s> birds, and peacocks sing sweetly; ornaments placed in boxes emit sweet sounds; and unplayed musical instruments produce sweet sounds; elevated areas of the earth sink down; depressed areas rise up; and the ground becomes free of stones, gravel, and potsherds.

body.text: iyaṃ ca tasmin samaye pṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampyate / tadyathā pūrvo digbhāga unnamati / paścimo 'vanamati / anto 'vanamati / madhya
body.translated_text: And at that time, this earth trembles with six kinds of quaking: the eastern quarter rises up, the western quarter sinks down, the outer parts sink down, and the middle

body.text: unnamati / calitaḥ pracalito vedhitaḥ pravedhita itīme cānye cādbhutadharmāḥ prādurbhavanti / bhagavato nagarapraveśe vakṣyati /
body.translated_text: rises up; it shakes, it quakes, it trembles, it greatly trembles — these and other wondrous phenomena manifest. Regarding the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s entry into the city, it is said:

children.translated_text: "Like the sea with its inhabitants, or like a region adorned with towns and villages and mountains,

children.text: municaraṇanipīḍitā ca bhūmī pavanabalahataṃ hi yānapātraṃ //
children.translated_text: so the earth pressed by the sage's feet is like a vessel struck by the force of the wind."

body.text: atha buddhapraveśakālaniyataiḥ prātihāryairāvarjitāḥ strīmanuṣyās, tannagaram anibalacalitabhinnavicitaraṅgakṣubhitamiva mahāsamudraṃ vimuktoccanādaṃ babhūva / na hi buddhapraveśatulyaṃ nāma jagatyadbhutamupalabhyate / purapraveśasamaye hi bhagavataś citrāṇyadbhūtāni dṛśyante / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: Then the women and men, drawn by the miracles that invariably accompany the <s>Buddha</s>'s entry, that city became like a great ocean with waves broken, varied, and surging from an unleashed whirlwind, and it resounded with loud cries. For in the world there is no marvel equal to the entry of a <s>Buddha</s>. At the time of entering the city, wondrous and marvelous things are seen of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. For it is said:

children.translated_text: "The low ground rises up and the sunken ground levels out by the <s>Buddha</s>'s power — the great earth,
the pillars become free of gravel and thorns and attain a flawless state,
the blind, mute, and dull-sensed men instantly become clear in their faculties,
and unplayed instruments in the city sound forth and rejoice!"

body.text: sarvaṃ ca tannagaraṃ sūryasahasrātirekayā kanakamarīcivarṇayā buddhaprabhayā sphuṭaṃ babhūva / āha ca /
body.translated_text: And that entire city became radiant with the <s>Buddha</s>'s splendor, golden in hue like golden rays, surpassing a thousand suns. And it is said:

body.text: sūryaprabhāṃ samavabhartsya hi tasya bhābhir vyāptaṃ jagat sakalameva sakānanasthaṃ /
body.translated_text: "Outshining the light of the sun with his radiance, the entire world, including forests, was pervaded.

body.text: saṃprāpa ca pravaradharmakathābhirāmo lokaṃ surāsuranaraṃ hi samuktabhāvaṃ //
body.translated_text: And he who delights in teaching the supreme <s>Dharma</s> brought the world of <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>asuras</s> (demons), and humans to a state of liberation."

body.text: yāvad bhagavān rājamārgaṃ pratipannaḥ / tatra dvau bāladārakau / eko 'grakulikaputro dvitīyaḥ kulikaputraśca / pāṃśvāgāraiḥ krīḍataḥ / ekasya jayo nāma dvitīyasya vijayaḥ / tābhyāṃ bhagavān dṛṣṭo dvātriṃśamahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṅkṛtaśarīro 'secanakadarśanaśca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> proceeded along the royal highway. There were two young boys — the first, a son of a leading family, and the second, a son of a good family — playing with toy houses of dirt. One was named <s>Jaya</s> and the second <s>Vijaya</s>. The two of them saw the <s>Bhagavān</s>, whose body was adorned with the thirty-two marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being), and who was pleasing to behold.

body.text: yāvaj jayena dārakeṇa śaktuṃ dāsyāmīti pāṃśvañjalirbhagavataḥ pātre prakṣiptaḥ / vijayena ca kṛtāñjalinābhyanumoditaṃ / vakṣyati ca /
body.translated_text: Then the boy <s>Jaya</s>, thinking "I will give barley-meal," cast a handful of dirt into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s bowl. And <s>Vijaya</s>, with palms joined together, gave his approval. And it is said:

children.translated_text: "Having seen the greatly compassionate, self-born one, whose entire body was illuminated by the splendor of his arm-span radiance,

children.text: dhīreṇa vaktreṇa kṛtaprasādaḥ pāṃśuṃ dadau jātijarāntakāya //
children.translated_text: with a steadfast countenance and faith inspired, he gave dirt to the one who ends birth and old age."

body.text: sa bhagavate pratipādayitvā praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ / anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena ekacchatrāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ rājā syām / atraiva ca buddhe bhagavati kārāṃ kuryāmiti /
body.translated_text: Having offered it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he began to make a vow: "By this root of merit, may I become king of the entire earth under a single parasol, and may I render service to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>."

children.text: tato munistasya niśāmya bhāvaṃ bālasya samyak praṇidhiṃ ca buddhvā /
children.translated_text: Then the sage, perceiving his intention and understanding the boy's proper aspiration,

children.text: iṣṭaṃ phalaṃ kṣetravaśena dṛṣṭvā jagrāha pāṃśuṃ karuṇāyamānaḥ //
children.translated_text: seeing the desired fruit arising from the excellence of the field of merit, accepted the dirt with compassion.

body.text: tena yāvad rājyavaipākyaṃ kuśalamākṣiptaṃ / tato bhagavatā smitaṃ vidarśitaṃ /
body.translated_text: By that he planted the merit whose fruit would ripen as kingship. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile.

body.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ vidarśayanti /
body.translated_text: For it is a natural law that whenever the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, display a smile,

body.text: tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātamañjiṣṭhasphaṭikarajatavarṇā arciṣo mukhān niścaranti / kecidūrdhvato gacchanti kecidadhastād gacchanti / ye 'dho gacchanti te sañjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīciparyanteṣu gatvā ye śītanarakāsteṣūṣṇībhūtvā nipatanti / ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtvā nipatanti /
body.translated_text: at that time rays of blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, crystal, and silver color issue from their mouths. Some go upward and some go downward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells of <s>Sañjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, and as far as <s>Avīci</s> — in the cold hells they fall as warmth, and in the hot hells they fall as coolness.
