body.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇaviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante / teṣāmevaṃ bhavati / kiṃ nu bhavanto vayamitaścyutā āhosvidanyatropapannā iti / yenāsmākaṃ kāraṇaviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhāḥ / teṣāṃ bhagavān prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ nirmitaṃ visarjayati / teṣāmevaṃ bhavati / na vayaṃ cyutā nāpyanyatropapannāḥ / api tu ayamapūrvadarśano 'syānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇaviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti / te nirmite cittāni prasādayitvā narakavedanīyāni karmāṇi kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti / yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti / ye ūrdhvato gacchanti te caturmahārājikān devāṃstrayastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmān parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhān śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhaparyanteṣu deveṣu gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmeti udghoṣayanti / gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante /
body.translated_text: By that, the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think thus: 'Have we passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere, that our particular sufferings have been alleviated?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) sends forth an emanation for the purpose of generating faith in them. They think thus: 'We have not passed away, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is an unprecedented sight, and by its power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having generated faith in the emanation and having exhausted the <s>karmas</s> (actions) that would lead to hellish experience, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those who go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> (Four Great Kings), <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three), <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s> (Contented), <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> (Delighting in Creation), <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> (Controlling Others' Creations), <s>Brahmakāyika</s> (Brahmā's Retinue), <s>Brahmapurohita</s> (Brahmā's Ministers), <s>Mahābrahmā</s> (Great Brahmā), <s>Parīttābha</s> (Limited Radiance), <s>Apramāṇābha</s> (Immeasurable Radiance), <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Streaming Radiance), <s>Parīttaśubha</s> (Limited Beauty), <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> (Immeasurable Beauty), <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (Total Beauty), <s>Anabhraka</s> (Cloudless), <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> (Merit-born), <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (Great Fruit), <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s> (Without Heat), <s>Sudṛśa</s> (Fair-seeing), <s>Sudarśana</s> (Fair-appearing), up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (Highest) gods, they proclaim: 'All is impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self.' And they speak two verses:

children.translated_text: Strive, renounce, apply yourselves to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!
Crush the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant crushes a reed hut.
Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline) shall dwell heedfully,
Having abandoned the cycle of birth and <s>saṃsāra</s> (rebirth), shall make an end of suffering.

body.text: atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantamevānugacchanti / yadi bhagavānatītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante 'nāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purato 'ntardhīyante / narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante / tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyāmantardhīyante / pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṃguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante / manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānuno[ra]ntardhīyante / balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante / cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante / devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyāmantardhīyante / śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante / pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyāmantardhīyante / anuttarāṃ smayaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe 'ntardhīyante /
body.translated_text: Then those rays, having wandered through the great trichiliocosm, follow the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to declare a past <s>karma</s> (deed), they vanish behind him; if he wishes to declare a future one, they vanish in front. If he wishes to declare rebirth in a hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet; if he wishes to declare rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels; if he wishes to declare rebirth as a hungry ghost, they vanish at his big toe; if he wishes to declare rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees; if he wishes to declare a kingdom of a <s>balacakravartin</s> (minor universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm; if he wishes to declare a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) kingdom, they vanish in his right palm; if he wishes to declare rebirth as a god, they vanish at his navel; if he wishes to declare the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they vanish at his mouth; if he wishes to declare the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha), they vanish at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the brows); if he wishes to declare supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they vanish at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

body.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato vāme karatale 'ntarhitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s left palm.

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo gāthāṃ bhāṣate / nāhetvapratyayaḥ /

children.translated_text: Free from agitation, rid of wretchedness and pride, the <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme cause in the world.

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitaṃ vidarśenti jinā jitārayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), who have conquered their foes, display a smile white as a conch shell and lotus fiber.

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, spoke a verse — not without cause or condition:

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṛṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṃkṣitānāṃ /
children.translated_text: At this moment, O Hero, having understood by your own wisdom, for the sake of listeners eager to know, O <s>Śramaṇa</s> (Ascetic), O Lord of Victors,
with your firm, supreme, and auspicious words, O Bull among Sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen.
O you whose voice is like the thunder of clouds, whose eyes are like those of a lordly bull,
declare the fruit of the gift of dust, O Best of Men.

body.text: bhagavānāha / etadānanda evametad ānanda nāhetvapratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti / api tu sahetu sapratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is, <s>Ānanda</s>. Not without cause or condition do the <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-gone Ones), <s>Arhats</s> (Worthy Ones), Perfectly Awakened Ones display a smile. Rather, with cause and with condition do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones display a smile.'

body.text: paśyasi tvamānanda dārakaṃ yena tathāgatasya pātre pāṃśvañjaliḥ prakṣiptaḥ / evaṃ bhadanta / ayamānanda dārakaḥ anena kuśalamūlena varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya pāṭaliputre nagare 'śoko nāmnā rājā bhaviṣyati / caturbhāgacakravartī dhārmiko dharmarājā / yo me śarīradhātūn vaistārikān kariṣyati / caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati / bahujanahitāya pratipatsyate / iti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: 'Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, the boy who threw a handful of dust into the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s bowl?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, this boy, by this root of merit, one hundred years after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), shall become a king named <s>Aśoka</s> in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, a <s>caturbhāgacakravartin</s> (ruler of one of the four continents), a righteous <s>Dharma</s>-king. He shall distribute my bodily relics far and wide, shall establish eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> (Dharma-king shrines), and shall act for the benefit of many people.' And he spoke:

children.text: astaṃgate mayi bhaviṣyati saikarājā yo 'sau hyaśoka iti nāma viśālakīrtiḥ /
children.translated_text: After I have passed away, there shall be a king who will be known by the name <s>Aśoka</s>, of widespread fame,
He shall make this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (Rose-apple Continent) adorned with shrines containing my relics, worshipped by men and gods.

body.text: ayamasya deyadharmo yat tathāgatasya pāṃśvañjaliḥ pātre prakṣiptaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This is his meritorious gift — that a handful of dust was thrown into the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s bowl.'

body.text: yāvad bhagavatā teṣāṃ sarva āyuṣmata ānandāya dattāḥ / gomayena miśrayitvā yatra caṃkrame tathāgataścaṃkramyate tatra gomayakārṣī prayaccheti / yāvadāyuṣmatānandena teṣāṃ sagomayena miśrayitvā yatra caṃkramati bhagavān tatra gomayakārṣī dattā /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave all of them to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, saying: 'Mix them with cow dung, and wherever the <s>Tathāgata</s> walks on his walking path, apply the cow-dung plaster there.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having mixed them with cow dung, applied the cow-dung plaster wherever the <s>Bhagavān</s> walked.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena rājagṛhe nagare bimbisāro rājā rājyaṃ kārayati / rājño bimbisārasya ajātaśatruḥ putraḥ / ajātaśatrorudāyī /
body.translated_text: At that time, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was ruling the kingdom. King <s>Bimbisāra</s>'s son was <s>Ajātaśatru</s>. <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s son was <s>Udāyin</s>.

body.text: udāyibhadrasya muṇḍaḥ / muṇḍasya kākavarṇī / kākavarṇinaḥ sahalī / sahalinastulakuciḥ / tulakucermahāmaṇḍalaḥ / mahāmaṇḍalasya prasenajit / prasenajito nandaḥ / nandasya bindusāraḥ / pāṭaliputre nagare bindusāro nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati / bindusārasya rājñaḥ putro jātaḥ / tasya susīma iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Udāyibhadra</s>'s son was <s>Muṇḍa</s>. <s>Muṇḍa</s>'s son was <s>Kākavarṇin</s>. <s>Kākavarṇin</s>'s son was <s>Sahali</s>. <s>Sahali</s>'s son was <s>Tulakuci</s>. <s>Tulakuci</s>'s son was <s>Mahāmaṇḍala</s>. <s>Mahāmaṇḍala</s>'s son was <s>Prasenajit</s>. <s>Prasenajit</s>'s son was <s>Nanda</s>. <s>Nanda</s>'s son was <s>Bindusāra</s>. In the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, a king named <s>Bindusāra</s> was ruling the kingdom. A son was born to King <s>Bindusāra</s>. He was given the name <s>Susīma</s>.

body.text: tena ca samayena campāyāṃ nagaryāmanyatamo brāhmaṇaḥ / tasya duhitā jātā / abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā janapadakalyāṇī / sā naimittikairvyākṛtā / asyā dārikāyā rājā bhartā bhaviṣyati / dve putraratne janayiṣyati / ekaścaturbhāgacakravartī bhaviṣyati / dvitīyaḥ pravrajitvā siddhavrato bhaviṣyati / śrutvā ca brāhmaṇasya romaharṣo jātaḥ / sampattikāmo lokaḥ /
body.translated_text: At that time, in the city of <s>Campā</s>, there was a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (brahmin). A daughter was born to him — beautiful, lovely, charming, the fairest in the land. Soothsayers declared of her: 'This girl's husband shall be a king. She will bear two jewel-like sons. One shall become a <s>caturbhāgacakravartin</s> (ruler of one of the four continents). The second, having gone forth as a renunciant, shall become one who has fulfilled his vows.' Upon hearing this, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s hair stood on end with joy. People desire good fortune.

body.text: sa tāṃ duhitaraṃ grahāya pāṭaliputraṃ gataḥ / tena sā sarvālaṅkārairvibhūṣayitvā rājño bindusārasya bhāryārthamanupradattā / iyaṃ hi devakanyādhanyā praśastā ceti /
body.translated_text: He took his daughter and went to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. Having adorned her with all ornaments, he offered her to King <s>Bindusāra</s> as a wife, saying: 'This one is blessed and auspicious like a divine maiden.'

body.text: yāvadrājñā bindusāreṇāntaḥpuraṃ praveśitā / antaḥpurikāṇāṃ buddhirutpannā / iyamabhirūpā prāsādikā janapadakalyāṇī / yadi rājānayā sārdhaṃ paricārayiṣyati asmākaṃ bhūyaścakṣuḥsaṃpreṣaṇamapi na kariṣyati /
body.translated_text: When she was brought into the inner quarters by King <s>Bindusāra</s>, the women of the harem thought: 'She is beautiful, charming, the fairest in the land. If the king consorts with her, he will not even cast a glance at us anymore.'

body.text: tābhiḥ sā nāpitakarma śikṣāpitā / sā rājñaḥ keśaśmaśru prasādhayati / yāvat suśikṣitā saṃvṛttā / yadārabhate rājñaḥ keśaśmaśru prasādhayituṃ tadā rājā śete / yāvadrājñā prītena vareṇa pravāritā / kiṃ tvaṃ varamicchasīti / tayābhihitaṃ / devena me saha samāgamaḥ syāt / rājāha / tvaṃ nāpinī ahaṃ rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ / kathaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ samāgamo bhaviṣyati / sā kathayati / deva nāhaṃ nāpinī / api brāhmaṇasyāhaṃ duhitā / tena devasya patnyarthaṃ dattā / rājā kathayati / kena tvaṃ nāpitakarma śikṣāpitā / sā kathayati / antaḥpurikābhiḥ / rājāha / na bhūyastvayā nāpitakarma kartavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: They had her trained in the barber's craft. She would groom the king's hair and beard. When she became well-trained, whenever she began to groom the king's hair and beard, the king would fall asleep. Then the king, pleased, offered her a boon: 'What boon do you wish?' She said: 'May I have union with Your Majesty.' The king replied: 'You are a barber-woman and I am a king, a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior) anointed on the head. How can there be union with me?' She said: 'Your Majesty, I am not a barber-woman. I am a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s daughter, given to Your Majesty as a wife.' The king asked: 'Who trained you in the barber's craft?' She said: 'The women of the harem.' The king said: 'You shall no longer perform the barber's work.'

body.text: yāvadrājāgramahiṣī sthāpitā / tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati / sā apannasattvā saṃvṛttā / yāvadaṣṭānāṃ navānāṃ māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā / tasyāḥ putro jātaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then she was installed as chief queen. He sported, delighted, and consorted with her. She became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A son was born to her.

body.text: tasya vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvā [pṛcchati] kiṃ kumārasyabhavatu nāma / sā kathayati / asya dārakasya jātasya aśokāsmi saṃvṛttā / tasyāśoka iti nāma kṛtam /
body.translated_text: Having performed the birth celebration for him in full, he asked: 'What shall be the boy's name?' She said: 'When this child was born, I became free from sorrow (<s>aśoka</s>).' So he was given the name <s>Aśoka</s>.

body.text: yāvad dvitīyaḥ putro jātaḥ / vigate śoke jātas tasya vītaśoka iti nāma kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then a second son was born. Since he was born after the sorrow had departed, he was given the name <s>Vītaśoka</s> (Free from Sorrow).

body.text: aśoko duḥsparśagātraḥ / rājño bindusārasyānabhipretaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Aśoka</s>'s body was rough to the touch. He was not pleasing to King <s>Bindusāra</s>.

body.text: atha rājā bindusāraḥ kumāraṃ parīkṣitukāmaḥ piṅgalavatsājīvaṃ parivrājakamāmantrayate / upādhyāya kumārāṃstāvat parīkṣayāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Bindusāra</s>, wishing to test the princes, addressed the wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s>: 'Teacher, let us test the princes.

body.text: kaḥ śakyate mamātyayād rājyaṃ kārayituṃ / piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājakaḥ kathayati / tena hi deva kumārānādāya suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ nirgaccha, parīkṣayāmaḥ / yāvadrājā kumārānādāya suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ nirgataḥ /
body.translated_text: Who is able to rule the kingdom after my passing?' The wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s> said: 'Then, Your Majesty, take the princes and go out to the Golden Pavilion Garden; we shall test them.' Then the king, taking the princes, went out to the Golden Pavilion Garden.

body.text:
yāvadaśokaḥ kumāro mātrā cocyate / vatsa rājā kumārān parīkṣitukāmaḥ suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ gataḥ / tvamapi tatra gaccheti / aśokaḥ kathayati / rājño 'hamanabhipreto darśanenāpi / kimahaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi / sā kathayati / tathāpi gaccheti / aśoka uvāca / āhāraṃ preṣaya /
yāvadaśokaḥ pāṭaliputrannirgacchati / rādhaguptena cāgrāmātyaputreṇoktaḥ / aśoka kva gamiṣyasīti / aśokaḥ kathayati / rājādya suvarṇamaṇḍape udyāne kumārān parīkṣayati / tatra rājño mahallako hastināgastiṣṭhati / yāvadaśokastasmin mahallake 'bhiruhya suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ gatvā kumārāṇāṃ madhye 'tra pṛthivyāṃ prastīrya niṣasāda /
body.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Aśoka</s> was told by his mother: 'Son, the king has gone to the Golden Pavilion Garden wishing to test the princes. You too should go there.' <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'The king finds me displeasing even to look at. Why should I go there?' She said: 'Go nevertheless.' <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'Send food for me.' Then <s>Aśoka</s> set out from <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. And <s>Rādhagupta</s>, the son of the chief minister, said to him: '<s>Aśoka</s>, where are you going?' <s>Aśoka</s> replied: 'The king is testing the princes today at the Golden Pavilion Garden.' There stood the king's old elephant. <s>Aśoka</s> mounted that old elephant, went to the Golden Pavilion Garden, and in the midst of the princes, sat down on the bare ground.

body.text: yāvat kumārāṇāmāhāra upanāmitaḥ / aśokasyāpi mātrā śālyodanaṃ dadhisaṃmiśraṃ mṛdbhājane preṣitaṃ / tato rājñā bindusāreṇa piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājako 'bhihitaḥ / upādhyāya parīkṣasva kumārān / kaḥ śakyate mamātyayād rājyaṃ kartumiti / paśyati piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājakaḥ / cintayati ca / aśoko rājā bhaviṣyati / ayaṃ ca rājño nābhipretaḥ / yadi kathayiṣyāmi aśoko rājā bhaviṣyatīti, nāsti me jīvitaṃ / sa kathayati / devābhedena
body.translated_text: Then food was brought for the princes. For <s>Aśoka</s> too, his mother had sent rice cooked with milk and mixed with curds in an earthen vessel. Then King <s>Bindusāra</s> said to the wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s>: 'Teacher, examine the princes. Who is able to rule the kingdom after my passing?' The wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s> looked and reflected: '<s>Aśoka</s> will become king. But this one is not pleasing to the king. If I say that <s>Aśoka</s> will become king, my life will be at risk.' He said: 'Your Majesty, I shall declare it in a veiled manner.'

body.text: vyākariṣyāmi / rājāha / abhedena vyākuruṣva / āha / yasya yānaṃ śobhanaṃ sa rājā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Declare it in a veiled manner.' He said: 'He whose vehicle is the finest shall become king.'

body.text: teṣāmekaikasya buddhirutpannā / mama yānaṃ śobhanamahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmi / aśokaścintayati / ahaṃ hastiskandhenāgato mama yānaṃ śobhanamahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmīti / rājāha / bhūyastāvad upādhyāya parīkṣasva / piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājakaḥ kathayati / deva yasyāsanamagraṃ sa rājā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Each one of them thought: 'My vehicle is the finest; I shall become king.' <s>Aśoka</s> thought: 'I came on the back of an elephant; my vehicle is the finest; I shall become king.' The king said: 'Teacher, test them further.' The wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s> said: 'Your Majesty, he whose seat is foremost shall become king.'

body.text: teṣāmekaikasya buddhirutpannā / mamāsanamagraṃ / aśokaścintayati / mama pṛthivī āsanamahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmi / evaṃ bhājanaṃ bhojanaṃ pānaṃ vistareṇa kumārāṇāṃ parīkṣya [pāṭaliputraṃ] praviṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: Each one of them thought: 'My seat is foremost.' <s>Aśoka</s> thought: 'The earth is my seat; I shall become king.' Thus, having tested the princes extensively regarding their vessels, food, and drink, they returned to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.

body.text: yāvadaśoko mātrocyate / ko vyākṛto rājā bhaviṣyatīti / aśokaḥ kathayati / abhedena vyākṛtaṃ / yasya yānamagramāsanaṃ pānaṃ bhājanaṃ bhojanaṃ ceti sa rājā bhaviṣyatīti / yathā paśyāmi ahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmi / mama hastiskandhaṃ yānaṃ pṛthivī āsanaṃ mṛnmayaṃ bhājanaṃ śālyodanaṃ dadhivyañjanaṃ bhojanaṃ pānīyaṃ pānamiti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Aśoka</s> was asked by his mother, "Who has been prophesied to become king?" <s>Aśoka</s> replied, "It was prophesied without distinction: 'He whose vehicle, food, seat, drink, vessel, and meal are foremost—he shall become king.' As I see it, I shall become king, for my vehicle is an elephant's back, my seat is the earth, my vessel is made of clay, my meal is rice with curd as a side dish, and my drink is water."

body.text: tataḥ piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājako 'śoko rājā bhaviṣyatīti tasya mātaramārabdha sevituṃ / yāvat tayocyate / upādhyāya kataraḥ kumāro rājño bindusārasyātyayād rājā bhaviṣyatīti / āha / aśokaḥ / tayocyate / kadācit tvāṃ rājā nirbandhena pṛccheta /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s>, a <s>parivrājaka</s> (wandering ascetic), knowing that <s>Aśoka</s> would become king, began to serve his mother. She asked him, "Teacher, which prince will become king after King <s>Bindusāra</s>'s passing?" He said, "<s>Aśoka</s>." She then said to him, "Should the king ever press you insistently with questions—"

body.text: gaccha tvaṃ pratyantaṃ samāśraya / yadā śrṛṇoṣi aśoko rājā saṃvṛttastadāgantavyaṃ / yāvatsa prayanteṣu janapadeṣu saṃśritaḥ /
body.translated_text: "—go and take refuge in the borderlands. When you hear that <s>Aśoka</s> has become king, then you should return." Thereupon he took shelter in the outlying provinces.

body.text: atha rājño bindusārasya takṣaśilā nāma nagaraṃ viruddhaṃ / tatra rājñā bindusāreṇa aśoko visarjitaḥ / gaccha kumāra takṣiśīlānagaraṃ / saṃnāhaya / caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ dattaṃ / yānaṃ praharaṇaṃ ca pratiṣiddhaṃ /
body.translated_text: Now the city called <s>Takṣaśilā</s> had revolted against King <s>Bindusāra</s>. King <s>Bindusāra</s> dispatched <s>Aśoka</s> there: "Go, prince, to the city of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>. Subdue it." A fourfold army was given to him, but vehicles and weapons were withheld.

body.text: yāvadaśokaḥ kumāraḥ pāṭaliputrānnirgacchan bhṛtyairvijñaptaḥ / kumāra naivāsmākaṃ sainyapraharaṇaṃ kena vayaṃ kaṃ yodhayāmaḥ / tato 'śokenābhihitaṃ /
body.translated_text: As Prince <s>Aśoka</s> was departing from <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, his servants informed him, "Prince, we have neither an army nor weapons—with what shall we fight, and against whom?" Then <s>Aśoka</s> declared,

body.text: yadi mama rājyavaipākyaṃ kuśalamasti sainyapraharaṇaṃ prādurbhavatu / evamukte kumāreṇa pṛthivyāmavakāśo datto devatābhiḥ sainyapraharaṇāni copanītāni / yāvat kumāraścaturaṅgeṇa balakāyena takṣaśilāṃ gataḥ /
body.translated_text: "If I possess meritorious <s>karma</s> (action) that will ripen into kingship, let an army and weapons appear!" When the prince spoke thus, the earth made room, and the <s>devatās</s> (deities) brought forth an army and weapons. Then the prince marched to <s>Takṣaśilā</s> with a fourfold army.

body.text: śrutvā takṣaśilānivāsinaḥ paurā ardhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārge śobhāṃ kṛtvā pūrṇaghaṭamādāya pratyudgatāḥ / pratyudgamya ca kathayanti / na vayaṃ kumārasya viruddhā nāpi rājño bindusārasya / api tu duṣṭāmātyā asmākaṃ paribhavaṃ kurvanti / mahatā ca satkāreṇa takṣaśilāṃ praveśitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> adorned the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) and came forth to meet him carrying full water-pots. Having come out to meet him, they said, "We are not in revolt against the prince, nor against King <s>Bindusāra</s>. Rather, it is the corrupt ministers who oppress us." And he was received into <s>Takṣaśilā</s> with great honor.

body.text: evaṃ vistareṇa aśokaḥ khaśarājyaṃ praveśitaḥ / tasya dvau mahānagnau saṃśritau / tena tau vṛttyā saṃvibhaktau / tasyāgrataḥ parvatān saṃchindantau saṃprasthitau / devatābhiścoktaṃ / aśokaścaturbhāgacakravartī bhaviṣyati / na kenacid virodhitavyamiti / vistareṇa yāvadāsamudrā pṛthivī ājñāpitā /
body.translated_text: Thus, in detail, <s>Aśoka</s> was established in the kingdom of the <s>Khaśas</s>. Two great <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent beings) had taken refuge with him. He shared his provisions with those two. They went before him, cleaving through mountains. And the <s>devatās</s> (deities) declared, "<s>Aśoka</s> shall become a <s>caturbhāgacakravartin</s> (sovereign of the four quarters). No one should oppose him." In detail, the earth up to the ocean was brought under his command.

body.text: yāvat susīmaḥ kumāra udyānāt pāṭaliputraṃ praviśati / rājño bindusārasyāgrāmātyaḥ khalvāṭakaḥ pāṭaliputrānnirgacchati / tasya susīmena kumāreṇa krīḍābhiprāyatayā khaṭakā murdhni pātitā / yāvadamātyaścintayati / idānīṃ khaṭakāṃ nipātayati / yadā rājā bhaviṣyati tadā śasraṃ pātayiṣyati / tathā kariṣyāmi yathā rājaiva na bhaviṣyati / tena pañcāmātyaśatāni bhinnāni / aśokaścaturbhāgacakravartī nirdiṣṭaḥ / etaṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmaḥ / takṣaśilāśca punar virodhitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Susīma</s> was entering <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> from the pleasure garden. <s>Khalvāṭaka</s>, the chief minister of King <s>Bindusāra</s>, was leaving <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. Prince <s>Susīma</s>, in a playful mood, struck him on the head with his fist. The minister then thought, "Now he strikes with his fist; when he becomes king, he will strike with a sword. I shall act so that he never becomes king." He then won over five hundred ministers, declaring, "<s>Aśoka</s> has been designated a <s>caturbhāgacakravartin</s> (sovereign of the four quarters). We shall establish him on the throne." And <s>Takṣaśilā</s> was made to revolt again.

body.text: yāvadrājñā susīmaḥ kumārastakṣaśilāmanupreṣitaḥ / na ca śakyate saṃnāmayituṃ / bindusāraśca rājā glānībhūtaḥ / tenābhihitaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Bindusāra</s> sent Prince <s>Susīma</s> to <s>Takṣaśilā</s>. But it could not be pacified. And King <s>Bindusāra</s> fell ill. He said,

body.text: susīmaṃ kumāramānayata / rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti / aśokaṃ takṣaśilāṃ praveśayata /
body.translated_text: "Bring Prince <s>Susīma</s>. I shall establish him on the throne." And, "Send <s>Aśoka</s> to <s>Takṣaśilā</s>."

body.text: yāvadamātyairaśokaḥ kumāro haridrayā praliptaḥ / lākṣāṃ ca lohapātre kvāthayitvā kvathitena rasena lohapātrāṇi mrakṣayitvā chorayanti / aśokaḥ kumāro glānībhūta iti / yadā bindusāraḥ svalpāvaśeṣaprāṇaḥ saṃvṛttastadāmātyairaśokaḥ kumāraḥ sarvālaṅkārairbhūṣayitvā rājño bindusārasyopanītaḥ / imaṃ tāvad rājye pratiṣṭhāpaya / yadā susīma āgato bhaviṣyati tadā taṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the ministers smeared Prince <s>Aśoka</s> with turmeric. They boiled lac in iron vessels and, having anointed iron vessels with the boiled extract, they concealed them, announcing, "Prince <s>Aśoka</s> has fallen ill." When <s>Bindusāra</s> had but little life remaining, the ministers adorned Prince <s>Aśoka</s> with all ornaments and brought him before King <s>Bindusāra</s>, saying, "Establish this one on the throne for now. When <s>Susīma</s> arrives, we shall establish him on the throne."

body.text: tato rājā ruṣitaḥ / aśokena cābhihitaṃ / yadi mama dharmeṇa rājyaṃ bhavati devatā mama paṭṭaṃ badhnantu / yāvad devatābhiḥ paṭṭo baddhaḥ / taṃ dṛṣṭvā bindusārasya rājña uṣṇaṃ śoṇitiaṃ mukhādāgataṃ / yāvat kālagataḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king was angered. And <s>Aśoka</s> declared, "If the kingdom is mine by <s>dharma</s> (righteous destiny), let the <s>devatās</s> (deities) bind the royal diadem upon me." Thereupon the <s>devatās</s> bound the diadem. Seeing this, hot blood came from the mouth of King <s>Bindusāra</s>, and he passed away.

body.text: yadāśoko rājye pratiṣṭhitas tasyordhva yojanaṃ yakṣāḥ [ādeśaṃ] śrṛṇvanti / adho yojanaṃ nāgāḥ / tena rādhagupto 'grāmātyaḥ sthāpitaḥ /
body.translated_text: When <s>Aśoka</s> was established on the throne, the <s>Yakṣas</s> (nature spirits) heard his commands up to a <s>yojana</s> (league) above, and the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent beings) up to a <s>yojana</s> below. He appointed <s>Rādhagupta</s> as chief minister.

body.text: susīmenāpi śrutaṃ bindusāro rājā kālagato 'śoko rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ / iti śrutvā ca rūṣitamabhyāgataḥ / tvaritaṃ ca tasmād deśād āgataḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Susīma</s> also heard that King <s>Bindusāra</s> had passed away and that <s>Aśoka</s> had been established on the throne. Having heard this, he came back in anger, returning swiftly from that region.

body.text: aśokenāpi pāṭaliputre nagare ekasmin dvāre eko nagnaḥ sthāpitaḥ / dvitīye dvitīyastṛtīye rādhaguptaḥ pūrvadvāre svayameva rājāśoko 'vasthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Aśoka</s> then stationed one <s>Nāga</s> (serpent being) at one gate of the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, a second at the second gate, <s>Rādhagupta</s> at the third, and King <s>Aśoka</s> himself stood at the eastern gate.

body.text: rādhaguptena ca pūrvasmin dvāre yantramayo hastī sthāpitaḥ / tasyopari aśokasya ca pratimā nirmitā / paritaśca parikhāṃ khanayitvā khadirāṅgāraiśca pūrayitvā tṛṇenācchādya [sā] pāṃśunākīrṇā / susīmaścābhihito yadi śakyase 'śokaṃ ghātayituṃ rājeti /
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhagupta</s> stationed a mechanical elephant at the eastern gate, and upon it was fashioned an image of <s>Aśoka</s>. Around it he had a moat dug, filled it with <s>khadira</s> (acacia) charcoal, covered it with grass, and strewed it with dust. And <s>Susīma</s> was told, "If you can slay <s>Aśoka</s>, the kingdom is yours."

body.text: sa yāvat pūrvadvāraṃ gataḥ / aśokena saha yotsyāmīti / aṅgārapūrṇāyāṃ parikhāyāṃ patitaḥ / tatraiva cānayena vyasanamāpannaḥ / yadā ca susīmaḥ praghātitas tasyāpi mahānagno bhadrāyudho nāmnānekasahasraparivāraḥ / sa bhagavacchāsane pravrajito 'rhan saṃvṛttaḥ /
body.translated_text: He went to the eastern gate, intending to fight <s>Aśoka</s>, and fell into the moat filled with burning coals. There, by this stratagem, he met his destruction. When <s>Susīma</s> was slain, his great <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Bhadrāyudha</s>, attended by many thousands, went forth into the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s (the Blessed One's) teaching and became an <s>Arhat</s> (enlightened one).

body.text: yadāśoko rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ sa tairamātyairavajñādṛśyate / tenāmātyānāṃ śāsanārthamabhihitaṃ / bhavantaḥ puṣpavṛkṣān phalavṛkṣāṃśca chittvā kaṇṭakavṛkṣān paripālayantu / amātyā āhuḥ / devena kutra dṛṣṭaṃ / api tu kaṇṭakavṛkṣān chittvā puṣpavṛkṣāḥ phalavṛṃkṣāśca paripālayitavyāḥ / tairyāvat trirapi rājña ājñā pratikalitā / tato
body.translated_text: When <s>Aśoka</s> was established on the throne, those ministers looked upon him with contempt. To discipline the ministers, he commanded, "Sirs, cut down the flower trees and fruit trees, and tend the thorn trees." The ministers replied, "Where has Your Majesty seen such a thing? Rather, one should cut down the thorn trees and tend the flower trees and fruit trees." Three times they defied the king's order. Then

body.text: rājñā ruṣitena asiṃ niṣkośaṃ kṛtvā pañcānāmamātyaśatānāṃ śirāṃsi chinnāni /
body.translated_text: the king, enraged, drew his sword from its sheath and cut off the heads of five hundred ministers.

body.text: yāvad rājāśoko 'pareṇa samayenāntaḥ puraparivṛto vasantakāle samaye puṣpitaphaliteṣu pādapeṣu pūrvanagarasya udyānaṃ gataḥ / tatra ca paribhramatāśokavṛkṣaḥ supuṣpito dṛṣṭaḥ / tato rājño mamāyaṃ sahanāmā ityanunayo jātaḥ / sa ca rājāśoko duḥsparśagātraḥ / tā yuvatayastaṃ necchanti spraṣṭuṃ / yāvad rājā śayitastasyāntaḥpureṇa roṣeṇa tasmādaśokavṛkṣāt puṣpāṇi śākhāśca chinnāḥ /
body.translated_text: On another occasion, King <s>Aśoka</s>, surrounded by the women of the inner palace, went to the garden east of the city during the spring season, when the trees were in flower and fruit. While wandering there, he saw a beautifully blossoming <s>aśoka</s> tree. Then the king felt affection, thinking, "This tree shares my name." Now King <s>Aśoka</s> had rough skin. Those young women did not wish to touch him. While the king slept, the women of the inner palace, out of spite, cut the flowers and branches from that <s>aśoka</s> tree.

body.text: yāvad rājñā pratibuddhena so 'śokavṛkṣo dṛṣṭaḥ / puṣṭāśca tatrasthāḥ kena sa chinnaḥ / te kathayanti devāntaḥpurikābhiriti / śrutvā ca rājñāmarṣajātena pañcastrīśatāni kiṭikaiḥ saṃveṣṭaya dagdhāni /
body.translated_text: When the king awoke and saw that <s>aśoka</s> tree, he asked those standing nearby, "Who cut it down?" They replied, "Your Majesty, the women of the inner palace." Hearing this, the king, filled with fury, had five hundred women wrapped in bark and burned.

body.text: tasyemāni aśubhāni ālokya caṇḍo rājā caṇḍāśoka iti vyavasthāpitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Seeing these cruel deeds of his, the king was designated "<s>Caṇḍāśoka</s>" (<s>Aśoka</s> the Fierce).

body.text: yāvad rādhaguptenāgrāmātyenābhihitaḥ / deva na sadṛśaṃ svayamevedṛśamakāryaṃ kartuṃ / api tu devasya vadhyaghātakāḥ puruṣāḥ sthāpayitavyā ye devasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ śodhayiṣyanti / yāvadrājñā rājapuruṣāḥ pratyuktā vadhyaghātaṃ me mārgadhvamiti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Rādhagupta</s>, the chief minister, said to him, "Your Majesty, it is not fitting to carry out such deeds yourself. Rather, Your Majesty should appoint executioners who will carry out the punishments on Your Majesty's behalf." Then the king instructed the royal servants, "Find me an executioner."

body.text: yāvat tatra nātidūre parvatapādamūle karvaṭakaṃ / tatra tantravāyaḥ prativasati / tasya putro jātaḥ / girika iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtaṃ / caṇḍo duṣṭātmā mātaraṃ pitaraṃ ca paribhāṣate /
body.translated_text: Now not far from there, at the foot of a mountain, was a small settlement. A weaver lived there. A son was born to him, and he was given the name <s>Girika</s>. He was cruel and wicked, abusing his mother and father,

body.text: dārakadārikāśca tāḍayati / pipīlikān makṣikān mūṣikān matsyāṃśca jālena baḍiśena praghātayati / caṇḍo dārakastasya caṇḍagirika iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: beating other boys and girls, and killing ants, flies, mice, and fish with nets and hooks. Because the boy was so cruel, he was given the name <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> (Fierce <s>Girika</s>).

body.text: yāvad rājapuruṣairdṛṣṭaḥ pāpe karmaṇi pravṛttaḥ / sa tairabhihitaḥ / śakyase rājño 'śokasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ kartuṃ / sa āha / kṛtsnasya jambudvīpasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ sādhayiṣyāmīti /
body.translated_text: The royal servants saw him engaged in evil deeds. They said to him, "Can you serve as King <s>Aśoka</s>'s executioner?" He replied, "I can carry out the executions for the whole of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (the Rose-Apple Continent)."

body.text: yāvad rājño niveditaṃ / rājñābhihitamānīyatāmiti / sa ca rājapuruṣairabhihitaḥ / āgaccha rājā tvāmāhvayatīti / tenābhihitam / āgamayata / yāvadahaṃ mātāpitarāvavalokayāmīti / yāvan mātāpitarāvuvāca / amba, tātānujānīdhvaṃ yāsyāmyahaṃ rājño 'śokasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ sādhayituṃ / tābhyāṃ ca sa nivāritaḥ / tena tau jīvitād vyaparopitau / evaṃ yāvad rājapuruṣairabhihitaḥ / kimarthaṃ cireṇābhyāgato 'si / tena caitat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocitaṃ /
body.translated_text: This was reported to the king. The king said, "Bring him." The royal servants told him, "Come, the king summons you." He replied, "Wait. Let me first see my mother and father." Then he said to his mother and father, "Mother, father, give me your leave. I shall go to serve as King <s>Aśoka</s>'s executioner." They both tried to dissuade him. So he killed them both. Then the royal servants asked him, "Why have you taken so long?" He then related the whole matter to them in detail.

body.text: sa tairyāvad rājño 'śokasyopanāmitaḥ / tena rājño 'bhihitaṃ /
body.translated_text: They brought him before King <s>Aśoka</s>. He said to the king,

body.text: mamārthāya gṛhaṃ kārayasveti / yāvad rājñā gṛhaṃ kārāpitaṃ / paramadāruṇaṃ dvāramātraramaṇīyaṃ / tasya ramaṇīyakaṃ bandhanamiti saṃjñā vyavasthāpitā / sa āha / deva varaṃ me prayaccha / yastatra praviśet tasya na bhūyo nirgama iti / yāvad rājñābhihitam / evamastviti /
body.translated_text: "Build a house for my work." Then the king had a house built—exceedingly terrible, yet pleasing only at its entrance. It was given the name "The Beautiful Prison." He said, "Your Majesty, grant me a boon: whoever enters there shall never come out again." The king said, "So be it."

body.text: tataḥ sa caṇḍagirikaḥ kukkuṭārāmaṃ gataḥ / bhikṣuśca / bālapaṇḍitasūtraṃ paṭhati / sattvā narakeṣūpapannāḥ / yāvan narakapālā gṛhītvāyomayyāṃ bhūmāvādīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyām ekajvālībhūtāyām uttānakān pratiṣṭhāpya ayomayena viṣkambhaṇena mukhadvāraṃ viṣkambhya ayoguḍān ādīptān pradīptān saṃprajvalitān ekajvālībhūtān āsye prakṣipanti / ye teṣāṃ sattvānām oṣṭhāvapi dahanti jihvāmapi kaṇṭhamapi kaṇṭhanāḍamapi hṛdayamapi hṛdayasāmantamapi antrāṇi antraguṇānapi dagdhvā adhaḥ pragharanti / iyadduḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> went to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock's Monastery). A <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) was reciting the <s>Bālapaṇḍitasūtra</s> (Discourse on Fools and the Wise): "Beings are reborn in the hells. The hell-wardens seize them and lay them face-up on the iron ground that is blazing, burning, and utterly aflame. They prop open their mouths with an iron clamp and pour in molten iron balls that are blazing, burning, and utterly aflame. These burn their lips, burn their tongue, burn their throat, burn their gullet, burn their heart, burn the region around the heart, burn their entrails and intestines, and pass through below. So great, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), is the suffering of the hells."

body.text: sattvā narakeṣūpapannāḥ / yāvan narakapālā gṛhītvā ayomayyāṃ bhūmāvādīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyām ekajvālībhūtāyām uttānakān pratiṣṭhāpya ayomayena viṣkambhaṇena mūkhadvāraṃ viṣkambhya kvathitaṃ tāmram āsye prakṣipanti / yat teṣāṃ sattvānām oṣṭhau api dahanti jihvāmapi tālu api kaṇṭhamapi kaṇṭhanāḍamapi antrāṇi antraguṇānāpi dagdhvā adhaḥ pragharanti / iyadduḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ /
body.translated_text: "Beings are reborn in the hells. The hell-wardens seize them and lay them face-up on the iron ground that is blazing, burning, and utterly aflame. They prop open their mouths with an iron clamp and pour in molten copper. It burns their lips, burns their tongue, burns their palate, burns their throat, burns their gullet, burns their entrails and intestines, and passes through below. So great, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), is the suffering of the hells."

body.text: santi sattvā narakeṣūpapannāḥ / yān narakapālā gṛhītvāyomayyāṃ bhūmāvādīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālībhūtāyām avāṅmukhān pratiṣṭhāpyāyomayena sūtreṇa ādīptena saṃprajvalitena ekajvālībhūtena āsphāṭya ayomayena kuṭhāreṇa ādīptena saṃpradīptena saṃprajvalitena ekajvālībhūtena takṣṇuvanti saṃtakṣṇuvanti saṃpratakṣṇuvanti aṣṭāṃśamapi ṣaḍaṃśamapi caturasramapi vṛttamapi maṇḍalamapi unnatamapi avanatamapi śāntamapi viśāntamapi takṣṇuvanti / iyadduḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ /
body.translated_text: There are beings reborn in the hells. The hell-wardens seize them, place them face-down on an iron ground that is blazing, burning, and flaming as one mass of fire, mark them with an iron cord that is blazing, burning, and flaming as one mass of fire, and with an iron axe that is blazing, burning, and flaming as one mass of fire, they hew them, chop them, and cut them into eight-sided, six-sided, square, round, circular, raised, lowered, smooth, and very smooth [shapes]. So great indeed, O monks, is the suffering of the hells.

body.text: santi sattvā narakeṣūpapannāḥ / yān narakapālā gṛhītvā ayomayyāṃ bhūmāvādīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālībhūtāyāmavāṅmukhān pratiṣṭhāpyāyomayena sūtreṇādīptena pradīptena saṃprajvalitenaikajvālībhūtenāsphāṭyāyomayyāṃ bhūmyāmādīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāṃ naikajvālībhūtāyāṃ takṣṇuvanti saṃtakṣṇuvanti saṃparitakṣṇuvanti aṣṭāṃśamapi ṣaḍaṃśamapi caturasramapi maṇḍalamapi unnatamapi anavatamapi śāntamapi viśāntamapi takṣṇuvanti / iyadduḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ /
body.translated_text: There are beings reborn in the hells. The hell-wardens seize them, place them face-down on an iron ground that is blazing, burning, and flaming as one mass of fire, mark them with an iron cord that is blazing, burning, and flaming as one mass of fire, and on an iron ground that is blazing, burning, and flaming as one mass of fire, they hew them, chop them, and cut them into eight-sided, six-sided, square, circular, raised, lowered, smooth, and very smooth [shapes]. So great indeed, O monks, is the suffering of the hells.

body.text: santi sattvā narakeṣūpapannāḥ / yān narakapālā gṛhītvāyomayyāṃ bhūmāvādīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālībhūtāyāmuttānakān pratiṣṭhāpya pañcavidhabandhanakāraṇāṃ kārayanti / ubhayorhastayorāyasau kīlau krāmanti / ubhayoḥ pādayorāyasau kīlau krāmanti / madhye hṛdayasyāyasaṃ kīlaṃ krāmanti / suduḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ /
body.translated_text: There are beings reborn in the hells. The hell-wardens seize them, place them face-up on an iron ground that is blazing, burning, and flaming as one mass of fire, and inflict the five-fold punishment upon them: they drive iron stakes into both hands, iron stakes into both feet, and an iron stake into the middle of the heart. So extremely painful indeed, O monks, are the hells.

body.text: evaṃ pañca vedanā iti so 'pi (caṇḍagirikaḥ) kurute / tatsadṛśāśca kāraṇāḥ sattvānāmārabdhaḥ kārayituṃ [so 'pi taccārake] /
body.translated_text: Thus the five torments—that <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> also performs them. And he has begun to inflict similar punishments upon beings [in that place of execution].

body.text: yāvacchrāvastyāmanyatamaḥ sārthavāhaḥ patnyā saha mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ / tasya sā patnī mahāsamudre prasūtā / dārako jātastasya samudra iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: Now, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a certain caravan-leader descended into the great ocean together with his wife. His wife gave birth on the great ocean. A boy was born, and he was given the name <s>Samudra</s> ('Ocean').

body.text: yāvat vistareṇa dvādaśabhirvaṣairmahāsamudrāduttīrṇaḥ / sa ca sārthavāhaḥ pañcabhirdhūrtaśatairmuṣitaḥ / sārthavāhaḥ sa praghātitaḥ / sa ca samudraḥ sārthavāhaputro bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ / sa janapadacārikāṃ caran pāṭaliputramanuprāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: In full detail—after twelve years he crossed back from the great ocean. That caravan-leader was robbed by five hundred rogues. The caravan-leader was killed. And <s>Samudra</s>, the caravan-leader's son, went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Wandering on a tour of the countryside, he arrived at <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.

body.text: sa pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya pāṭaliputraṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ / so 'nabhijñayā ca ramaṇīyakaṃ bhavanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ / tacca dvāramātraramaṇīyamabhyantaraṃ narakabhavanasadṛśaṃ pratibhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punarnirgantukāmaścaṇḍagirikeṇāvalokitaḥ / gṛhītvā coktaḥ / iha te nidhanamupasaṃgantavyamiti / vistareṇa kāryaṃ /
body.translated_text: In the forenoon, having put on his robe and taken his bowl, he entered <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> for alms. Not knowing the place, he entered a pleasant-looking building. But it was pleasant only at the entrance—the interior, resembling a hell-palace, was terrifying. Wishing to leave, he was spotted by <s>Caṇḍagirika</s>, who seized him and said: 'Here you must meet your end.' In full detail.

body.text: tato bhikṣuḥ śokārto vāṣpakaṇṭhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / tenocyate / kimidaṃ bāladāraka iva rudasīti / sa bhikṣuḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: Then the monk became grief-stricken, his voice choked with tears. He (<s>Caṇḍagirika</s>) said to him: 'Why do you weep like a young child?' The monk said:

children.text: na śarīravināśaṃ hi bhadra śocāmi sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: I do not grieve at all for the destruction of my body, O good sir;
but I grieve deeply for myself because of the obstruction to the <s>dharma</s> of liberation.

children.text: durlabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ pravrajyāṃ ca sukhodayāṃ /
children.translated_text: Having obtained the rare human birth and the going-forth that gives rise to happiness,
and the Teacher, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>—I, the fool, shall have to abandon them again.

body.text: tenocyate / dattavaro 'haṃ nṛpatinā / dhīro bhava / nāsti te mokṣa iti / tataḥ sakaruṇairvacanaistaṃ bhikṣuḥ kramaṃ yācati sma / māsaṃ yāvat / saptarātramanujñātaḥ /
body.translated_text: He (<s>Caṇḍagirika</s>) said: 'I have been granted a boon by the king. Be brave! There is no escape for you.' Then with piteous words the monk entreated him step by step for a month's respite. He was granted seven nights.

body.text: sa khalu maraṇabhayodvignahṛdayaḥ saptarātreṇa me na bhavitavyamiti vyāyamamatiḥ saṃvṛttaḥ /
body.translated_text: With his heart trembling from the fear of death, he resolved to strive with utmost effort, thinking: 'I have only seven nights.'

body.text: atha saptame divase aśokasya rājño 'ntaḥpurikā kumāreṇa saha saṃraktāṃ nirīkṣyamāṇāṃ saṃlapantīṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sahadarśanādeva ruṣitena
body.translated_text: Then, on the seventh day, one of King <s>Aśoka's</s> harem women was seen looking lovingly at a prince and conversing with him. The king, enraged at the very sight,

body.text: rājñā tau dvāvapi taṃ cārakamanupreṣitau / tatra mūśalairayodroṇyāmasthyavaśeṣau kṛtau / tato bhikṣustau dṛṣṭvā saṃvignaḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: sent both of them to that place of execution. There they were reduced to bone-remains in an iron trough with pestles. Then the monk, seeing them, was deeply stirred and said:

children.translated_text: Ah, compassionate is the Teacher! Rightly did the Great Sage speak:
Form is like a ball of foam—without essence, without stability.

children.text: kva tad vadanakāntitvaṃ gātraśobhā kva sā gātā /
children.translated_text: Where is that beauty of the face? Where has that loveliness of the limbs gone?
Shame on this unjust <s>saṃsāra</s>, in which fools take delight!
This support I have obtained, dwelling in this place of execution—
relying upon which, I shall today cross to the far shore of the ocean of existence.

children.text: tena tāṃ rajanīṃ kṛtsnāṃ yujyatā buddhaśāsane /
children.translated_text: By him, that entire night, striving in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching,
having cut all fetters, the supreme state of <s>arhatship</s> was attained.

body.text: tatastasmiṃn rajanikṣaye sa bhikṣuścaṇḍagirikeṇocyate / bhikṣo nirgatā rātrir udita ādityaḥ kāraṇākālastaveti / tato bhikṣurāha / dīrghāyurmamāpi nirgatā rātrir udita ādityaḥ parānugrahakāla iti / yatheṣṭaṃ vartatāmiti /
body.translated_text: Then, at the end of that night, the monk was told by <s>Caṇḍagirika</s>: 'Monk, the night has passed, the sun has risen—it is time for your punishment.' Then the monk said: 'Long-lived one, for me too the night has passed and the sun has risen—it is time for benefiting others. Do as you wish.'

body.text: caṇḍagirikaḥ prāha / nāvagacchāmi vistīryatāṃ vacanametaditi / tato bhikṣurāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> said: 'I do not understand; explain this statement.' Then the monk said:

children.translated_text: For me too, from my heart, the terrible night of delusion has departed,
covered by the five hindrances, haunted by the thieves of the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>).
And the auspicious sun of knowledge has risen in the sky of my mind—
by whose radiance I see the triple world here in its true nature.
It is time for me to benefit others, as one who follows the ways of the Teacher.
This body, O long-lived one—do with it as you wish.

body.text: tatastena nirghṛṇena dāruṇahṛdayena paralokanirapekṣeṇa roṣāviṣṭena bahūdakāyāṃ sthālyāṃ nararudhiravasāmūtrapūrīṣasaṃkulāyāṃ mahālohyāṃ prakṣiptaḥ / prabhūtendhanaiścāgniḥ prajvālitaḥ / sa ca bahunāpīndhanakṣayeṇa na saṃtapyate / tataḥ punaḥ prajvālayituṃ ceṣṭate / yadā tasyāpi na prajvalati tato vicārya tāṃ lohīṃ paśyati / taṃ bhikṣuṃ padmasyopari paryaṅkeṇopaviṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca tato rājñe nivedayāmāsa / atha rājani samāgate prāṇisahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu sa bhikṣurvaineyakālamavekṣamāṇaḥ
body.translated_text: Then that merciless one, of cruel heart, heedless of the next world, seized by rage, cast him into a large cauldron of great iron, filled with human blood, fat, urine, and excrement. He lit a fire with abundant fuel. But even with much fuel being consumed, the monk was not burned. Then he tried again to kindle the fire. When that too would not blaze, he examined the iron cauldron and saw the monk seated cross-legged upon a lotus. He then informed the king. When the king arrived and thousands of beings had assembled, that monk, observing the time for converting those fit to be trained—

children.text: ṛddhiṃ samutpādya sa tanmuhūrtaṃ lohyantarasthaḥ salilādragātraḥ /
children.translated_text: producing supernatural power at that moment, standing within the cauldron, his body fresh as if emerging from water,

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇasya janasya madhye nabhastalaṃ haṃsa ivotpapāta //
children.translated_text: while the people watched, he flew up into the expanse of sky like a swan.

body.text: vicitrāṇi ca prātihāryāṇi darśayitumārabdhaḥ / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: He began to display various miraculous feats. For it will be said:

children.text: ardhena gātreṇa vavarṣa toyamardhena jajvāla hutāśanaśca /
children.translated_text: With one half of his body he rained water, and with the other half blazed like fire;

children.text: varṣañ jvalaṃścaiva rarāja yaḥ khe dīptauṣadhiprasravaṇeva śailaḥ //
children.translated_text: raining and blazing, he shone in the sky like a mountain with glowing herbs and waterfalls.
Seeing him risen in the sky, the king, with palms joined and face blooming with wonder,

children.text: udvīkṣamāṇas tamuvāca dhīraṃ kautuhalāt kiṃcidahaṃ vivakṣuḥ //
children.translated_text: gazing up at that steadfast one, spoke, wishing to say something out of curiosity:
Your form, O gentle one, is like a human's, but your power of miraculous ability surpasses mortals.

children.text: na niścayaṃ tena vibho vrajāmi ko nāma bhāvastava śuddhabhāva //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Lord, I cannot determine—what indeed is your nature, O pure-natured one?

children.text: tat sāmprataṃ brūhi mamedamarthaṃ yathā prajānāmi tava prabhāvaṃ /
children.translated_text: Tell me now this matter, so that I may know your power.

children.text: jñātvā ca te dharmaguṇaprabhāvān yathābalaṃ śiṣyavadācarema //
children.translated_text: And having learned of your qualities of <s>dharma</s> and power, we shall practice accordingly, like disciples.

body.text: tato bhikṣuḥ pravacanaparigrāhako 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati bhagavaddhātuṃ ca vistarīkariṣyati mahājanahitārthaṃ ca pratipatsyata iti matvā svaguṇamudbhāvayaṃstam uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the monk, thinking 'This one will become a supporter of the Teaching, will widely distribute the relics of the Blessed One, and will act for the welfare of the many,' displaying his own qualities, said to him:

children.translated_text: I, O King, am the son of the greatly compassionate <s>Buddha</s>, who has destroyed all bonds of defilement (<s>āsrava</s>),

children.text: buddhasya putro vadatāṃ varasya dharmānvayaḥ sarvabhaveṣvasaktaḥ //
children.translated_text: the best of speakers—born of the <s>Dharma</s>, unattached in all existences.

children.text: dāntena dāntaḥ puruṣarṣabhena śāntiṃ gatenāpi śamaṃ praṇītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Tamed by that tamed one, the bull among men; led to peace by him who has attained peace;
liberated from the great terrors of <s>saṃsāra</s> by him who is liberated—I have been freed from the bonds of existence.

body.text: api ca mahārāja tvaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛtaḥ / varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mama pāṭaliputre nagare 'śoko nāma rājā bhaviṣyati / caturbhāgacakravartī dharmarājo yo me śarīradhātūn vaistārikān kariṣyati / caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati / idaṃ ca devena narakasadṛśaṃ sthānameva sthāpitaṃ yatra prāṇisahasrāṇi nipātyante / tadarhasi deva sarvasattvebhyo 'bhayapradānaṃ dātuṃ bhagavataśca manorathaṃ paripūrayitum / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover, O Great King, you were prophesied by the Blessed One: 'A hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, there will be a king named <s>Aśoka</s>, a quarter-<s>cakravartin</s>, a <s>dharma</s>-king, who will distribute my bodily relics widely and will establish eighty-four thousand <s>dharma-rājikā</s> stūpas.' And this hell-like place has been established by Your Majesty, where thousands of beings are destroyed. Therefore, may Your Majesty grant the gift of fearlessness to all beings and fulfill the aspiration of the Blessed One. And he said:

children.text: tasmān narendra abhayaṃ prayaccha sattveṣu kāruṇyapurojaveṣu /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O King, grant fearlessness, with compassion foremost toward beings.

children.text: nāthasya saṃpūrya manorathaṃ ca vaistārikān dharmadharān kuruṣva //
children.translated_text: Fulfilling the aspiration of the Protector, make the <s>dharma</s>-bearing [stūpas] to distribute the relics widely.

body.text: atha sa rājā buddhe samupajātaprasādaḥ kṛtakarasaṃpuṭastaṃ bhikṣuṃ kṣamayannuvāca /
body.translated_text: Then that king, having gained faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, with palms joined, asking forgiveness of the monk, said:

children.text: daśabalasuta kṣantumarhasīmaṃ kukṛtamidaṃ ca tavādya deśayāmi /
children.translated_text: O son of the Ten-powered One, deign to forgive this misdeed of mine, which I confess to you today.

children.text: śaraṇamṛṣimupaimi taṃ ca buddhaṃ gaṇavaramāryaniveditaṃ ca dharmaṃ //
children.translated_text: I take refuge in that sage, the <s>Buddha</s>, and in the <s>Dharma</s> taught by the noble community (<s>Saṅgha</s>).

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: And furthermore:

children.translated_text: And I make this resolve today, out of reverence for him and faith inclined toward him:
I shall adorn the earth with shrines to the Conqueror-Lord, resembling swans, sun-rays, conch-shells, moons, and cranes.

body.text: yāvat sa bhikṣustadaiva ṛddhyā prakrāntaḥ / atha rājārabdho niṣkrāmituṃ / tataścaṇḍagirikaḥ kṛtāñjalir uvāca / deva labdhavaro 'haṃ naikasya vinirgama iti / rājāha / mā tāvan / māmapīcchasi ghātayituṃ /
body.translated_text: Then that monk immediately departed by supernatural power. When the king began to leave, <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> said with joined palms: 'O Your Majesty, I was granted the boon that no one should leave.' The king said: 'Stop! Do you wish to kill me too?'

body.text: sa uvāca / evameva /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Indeed so.'

body.text: rājāha / ko 'smākaṃ prathamataraṃ praviṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Who entered here first?'

body.text: caṇḍagirika uvāca / ahaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> said: 'I did.'

body.text: tato rājñābhihitaṃ / ko 'treti /
body.translated_text: Then the king pronounced the verdict: 'Who is it then [that must die first]?'

body.text: yāvad vadhyaghātairgṛhītaḥ / gṛhitvā ca yantragṛhaṃ praveśitaḥ / praveśayitvā dagdhaḥ / tacca ramaṇīyakaṃ bandhanamapanītaṃ / sarvasattvebhyaścābhayapradānamanupradattaṃ //
body.translated_text: Thereupon he was seized by the executioners. Having seized him, he was led into the machine-house. Having been led in, he was burned. That pleasant-seeming prison was demolished. And the gift of fearlessness was bestowed upon all beings.

body.text: tato rājā bhagavaccharīradhātuṃ vistariṣyāmīti caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena gatvājātaśatrupratiṣṭhāpitaṃ droṇastūpamutpāṭya śarīradhātuṃ gṛhītavān / yatra uddhāraṇaṃ ca vistareṇa kṛtvā dhātupratyaṃśaṃ dattvā stūpaṃ pratyasthāpayat / evaṃ dvitīyaṃ stūpaṃ vistareṇa / bhaktimato yāvat saptadroṇād grahāya stūpāṃśca pratiṣṭhāpya rāmagrāmaṃ gataḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king, thinking 'I shall distribute the bodily relics of the Blessed One,' went with a fourfold army, uprooted the <s>Droṇa-stūpa</s> established by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, and took the bodily relics. Having performed the extraction ceremony in full detail, he distributed shares of the relics and re-established the <s>stūpa</s>. Likewise with the second <s>stūpa</s>, in full. The devout king, having thus taken relics from seven <s>Droṇa</s>-stūpas and re-established those stūpas, went to <s>Rāmagrāma</s>.

body.text: tato rājā nāgairnāgabhavanamavatāritaḥ / vijñaptaśca / vayamasya [śarīradhātoḥ] atraiva pūjāṃ kariṣyāma iti / yāvad rājñābhyanujñātaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the king was taken down into the <s>Nāga</s>-realm by the <s>Nāgas</s>. And they said: 'We ourselves shall worship this bodily relic here.' And the king granted permission.

body.text: tato nāgarājena punarapi nāgabhavanāduttāritaḥ / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: Then he was brought back up from the <s>Nāga</s>-realm by the <s>Nāga</s>-king. For it will be said:

children.text: rāmagrāme 'sti tvaṣṭamaṃ stūpamadya nāgāstatkālaṃ bhaktimanto rarakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: At <s>Rāmagrāma</s> stands the eighth <s>stūpa</s>; the devout <s>Nāgas</s> guarded it at that time.

children.text: dhātūnetasmān nopalebhe sa rājā śraddhālū rājā yastvakṛtvā jagāma //
children.translated_text: Therefore the king did not obtain the relics from this one; the faithful king departed without taking them.

body.text: yāvad rājā caturaśītikaraṇḍasahasraṃ kārayitvā sauvarṇarūpyasphaṭikavaidūryamayāṇāṃ teṣu dhātavaḥ prakṣiptāḥ / evaṃ vistareṇa caturaśītikumbhasahasraṃ
body.translated_text: Then the king had eighty-four thousand caskets made—of gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli—and the relics were placed in them. Thus in full, eighty-four thousand urns—

body.text: paṭṭasahasraṃ ca yakṣāṇāṃ haste dattvā visarjitam / āsamudrāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ hinotkṛṣṭamadhyameṣu nagareṣu yatra koṭiḥ paripūryate tatra dharmarājikā pratiṣṭhāpayitavyā /
body.translated_text: —and a thousand silk-banners were given into the hands of <s>Yakṣas</s> and dispatched. On the earth extending to the ocean, in cities of low, high, and middle rank, wherever the population reaches a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million), there a <s>dharma-rājikā</s> [stūpa] was to be established.

body.text: tasmin samaye takṣaśilāyāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśat koṭyaḥ / tairabhihitaṃ / ṣaṭtriṃśat karaṇḍakānanuprayaccheti / rājā cintayati / na yadi vaistārikā dhātavo bhaviṣyanti / upāyajño rājā / tenābhihitaṃ / pañcatriṃśat koṭyaḥ śodhayitavyāḥ / vistareṇa yāvad rājñābhihitaṃ / yatrādhikatarā bhavanti yatra ca nyūnatarā tatra na dātavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: At that time, in <s>Takṣaśilā</s> there were thirty-six <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions). They said: 'Give us thirty-six baskets.' The king reflected: 'The relics will not be sufficient in such quantity.' The king, skilled in stratagems, said: 'Thirty-five <s>koṭis</s> must be satisfied.' In detail, the king declared: 'Where there are more [people], and where there are fewer, there [the relics] should not be distributed [unequally].'

body.text: yāvad rājā kukkuṭārāmaṃ gatvā sthavirayaśasamabhigamya uvāca / ayaṃ me manorathaḥ / ekasmin divase ekasmin mūhūrte caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyamiti / sthavireṇābhihitam / evamastu / ahaṃ tasmin samaye pāṇinā sūryamaṇḍalaṃ praticchādayiṣyāmīti /
body.translated_text: Then the king went to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery) and approached the elder <s>Yaśas</s> and said: 'This is my heart's wish: in a single day, in a single moment, I would establish eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s> (dharma-king monuments).' The elder said: 'So be it. At that time, I shall cover the disc of the sun with my hand.'

body.text: yāvat tasmin divase sthavirayaśasā pāṇinā sūryamaṇḍalaṃ praticchāditaṃ / ekasmin divase ekamuhūrte caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ / vakṣyati ca /
body.translated_text: Then on that day, the elder <s>Yaśas</s> covered the disc of the sun with his hand. In a single day, in a single moment, eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s> were established. And it will be declared:

children.text: tābhyaḥ saptabhyaḥ pūrvikābhyaḥ kṛtibhyo dhātuṃ tasyarṣeḥ sa hyupādāya mauryaḥ /
children.translated_text: From those seven previous constructions, taking the relics of that Sage, the <s>Maurya</s> [king]

children.text: cakre stūpānāṃ śāradābhraprabhāṇāṃ loke sāśīti hyahni cātuḥsahasraṃ //
children.translated_text: made in the world <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary mounds) radiant as autumn clouds — eighty-four thousand in a single day.

body.text: yāvacca rājñāśokena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ dhārmiko dharmarājā saṃvṛttastasya dharmāśoka iti saṃjñā jātā / vakṣyati ca /
body.translated_text: And when King <s>Aśoka</s> had established the eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s>, the righteous <s>dharmarāja</s> (king of dharma) came to be known by the name <s>Dharmāśoka</s>. And it will be declared:

children.text: āryo mauryaśrīḥ sa prajānāṃ hitārthaṃ kṛtsne stūpān yaḥ kārayāmāsa loke /
children.translated_text: The noble <s>Mauryaśrī</s> (Glory of the Mauryas), who for the welfare of his subjects caused <s>stūpas</s> to be built throughout the entire world —

children.text: caṇḍāśokatvaṃ prāpya pūrvaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dharmāśokatvaṃ karmaṇā tena lebhe //
children.translated_text: having first attained the state of <s>Caṇḍāśoka</s> (Fierce Aśoka) on earth, by that deed he obtained the state of <s>Dharmāśoka</s> (Righteous Aśoka).

body.text: pāṃśupradānāvadānaṃ ṣaḍviṃśatimaṃ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Pāṃśupradānāvadāna</s> (Legend of the Gift of Dust) — the twenty-sixth.

children.translated_text: The <s>Vītaśokāvadāna</s> (Legend of Vītaśoka)

body.text: yadā rājñāśokena bhagavacchāsane śraddhā pratilabdhā tena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ / pañcavārṣikaṃ ca kṛtaṃ / trīṇī śatasahasrāṇi bhikṣūṇāṃ bhojitāni / yatraikam arhatāṃ dve śaikṣāṇāṃ pṛthagjanakalyāṇakānāṃ ca / āsamudrāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ janakāyā yabhdūyasā bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasannāḥ /
body.translated_text: When King <s>Aśoka</s> had gained faith in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), he established eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s>. He held a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival). Three hundred thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) were fed — of whom one [hundred thousand] were <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones), two [hundred thousand] were <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners), and [the rest were] ordinary persons of good conduct. Throughout the earth as far as the ocean, the multitude of people was abundantly devoted to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: tasya bhrātā vītaśoko nāma tīrthyābhiprasannaḥ / sa tīrthyairvigrāhitaḥ / nāsti śramaṇaśākyaputrīyāṇāṃ mokṣa iti / ete hi sukhābhiratāḥ parikhedabhīravaśceti /
body.translated_text: His brother, named <s>Vītaśoka</s>, was devoted to the <s>tīrthyas</s> (heterodox teachers). He was persuaded by the <s>tīrthyas</s> [to believe]: 'There is no liberation for the <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) who are followers of the <s>Śākya</s> son [the Buddha]. For they delight in comfort and are afraid of hardship.'

body.text: yāvadrājñāśokenocyate / vītaśoka mā tvaṃ hīnāyatane prasādamutpādaya / api tu buddhadharmasaṅghe prasādamutpādaya / eṣa āyatanagataḥ prasāda iti /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s> said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, do not generate faith in a low abode [of doctrine]. Rather, generate faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>. That is faith directed to the [proper] abode.'

body.text: atha rājāśoko 'pareṇa samayena mṛgavadhāya nirgataḥ / tatra vītaśokenāraṇye ṛṣirdṛṣṭaḥ / pañcātapenāvasthitaḥ / sa ca kaṣṭatapaḥsārasaṃjñī / tenābhigamya pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā sa ṛṣiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ / bhagavan kiyacciraṃ te ihāraṇye prativasataḥ / sa uvāca / dvādaśavarṣāṇīti / vītaśokaḥ kathayati / kastavāhāraḥ / ṛṣiruvāca / phalamūlāni / kiṃ prāvaraṇaṃ / darbhacīvarāṇi / kā śayyā / tṛṇasaṃstaraḥ / vītaśoka uvāca / bhagavan kiṃ duḥkhaṃ bādhate / ṛṣīruvāca / ime
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s> on another occasion went out for a deer hunt. There, <s>Vītaśoka</s> saw a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) in the forest, standing in the posture of the five fires (<s>pañcātapena</s>). Regarding him as one who had attained the essence of severe austerity, he approached, paid obeisance at his feet, and asked the <s>ṛṣi</s>: 'Venerable one, how long have you been dwelling here in the forest?' He replied: 'Twelve years.' <s>Vītaśoka</s> asked: 'What is your food?' The <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'Fruits and roots.' 'What is your covering?' 'Garments of <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass).' 'What is your bed?' 'A mat of grass.' <s>Vītaśoka</s> said: 'Venerable one, what suffering afflicts you?' The <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'These

body.text: mṛgā ṛtukāle saṃvasanti / yadā mṛgāṇāṃ saṃvāso dṛṣṭo bhavati tasmin samaye rāgeṇa paridahyāmi /
body.translated_text: deer mate during the rutting season. When the mating of deer is seen, at that time I am consumed by passion.'

body.text: vītaśoka uvāca / asya kaṣṭena tapasā [vartamānasya] rāgo 'dyāpi bādhate prāgeva / śramaṇāḥ śākyaputrīyāḥ svāstīrṇāsanaśayanopasevinaḥ / kuta eṣāṃ rāgaprahāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / āha ca /
body.translated_text: <s>Vītaśoka</s> said: 'If passion still afflicts this one who practices such severe austerity — how much more so the <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) who are followers of the <s>Śākya</s> son, who enjoy well-spread seats and couches! How will there be abandonment of passion for them?' And he said:

children.translated_text: 'Living in this dreadful, desolate forest, subsisting on wind, water, and roots,

children.text: rāgo naiva jito yadīha ṛṣiṇā kālaprakarṣeṇa hi /
children.translated_text: if passion has not been conquered here by this <s>ṛṣi</s> even over a long time,
then — eating food rich with ghee, abundant meat, and curds with the finest ornaments —

children.text: śākyeṣvindriyanigraho yadi bhaved vindhyaḥ plavet sāgare //
children.translated_text: if there were to be sense-restraint among the <s>Śākyas</s>, then the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain would float in the ocean!'

body.text: sarvathā vañcito rājāśoko yacchramaṇeṣu śākyaputrīyeṣu kārāṃ karoti /
body.translated_text: 'In every way, King <s>Aśoka</s> is deceived in showing honor to the <s>śramaṇas</s> who are followers of the <s>Śākya</s> son.'

body.text: etacca vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā upāyajño 'mātyān uvāca / ayaṃ vitaśokastīrthyābhiprasannaḥ / upāyena bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasādayitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Having heard these words, the king, skilled in stratagems, said to his ministers: 'This <s>Vītaśoka</s> is devoted to the <s>tīrthyas</s> (heterodox teachers). He must be brought to faith in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> by means of a stratagem.'

body.text: amātyāḥ āhuḥ / deva kimājñāpayasi / rājāha / yadāhaṃ rājālaṅkāraṃ mauli paṭṭaṃ cāpanayitvā snānaśālāṃ praviṣṭo bhavāmi, tadā yūyaṃ vītaśokasya upāyena mauli paṭṭaṃ ca baddhvā [enaṃ] siṃhāsane niṣādayiṣyatha / evamastviti /
body.translated_text: The ministers said: 'Lord, what do you command?' The king said: 'When I remove the royal ornaments and the <s>mauli-paṭṭa</s> (crown turban) and enter the bathing hall, then you should, by a stratagem, bind the <s>mauli-paṭṭa</s> on <s>Vītaśoka</s> and seat him on the throne.' 'So be it!'

body.text: yāvad rājā rājālaṅkāraṃ maulipaṭṭaṃ cāpanayitvā snānaśālāyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ / tato 'mātyairvītaśoka ucyate / rājño 'śokasyātyayāt
body.translated_text: Then the king removed the royal ornaments and the <s>mauli-paṭṭa</s> and entered the bathing hall. Then the ministers said to <s>Vītaśoka</s>: 'After the death of King <s>Aśoka</s>,

body.text: tvaṃ rājā bhaviṣyasi / imaṃ tāvadrājālaṅkāraṃ pravaramaulipaṭṭaṃ ca baddhvā [tvāṃ] siṃhāsane niṣādayiṣyāmaḥ / kiṃ śobhase na ve 'ti /
body.translated_text: you will become king. Come, let us bind these royal ornaments and the supreme <s>mauli-paṭṭa</s> on you and seat you on the throne. Let us see whether they become you or not.'

body.text: sa
body.translated_text: They bound the ornaments and the <s>mauli-paṭṭa</s> on him and seated him on the throne. And the king was informed.

body.text: taistadābharaṇaṃ maulipaṭṭaṃ ca baddhvā siṃhāsane niṣāditaḥ / rājñaśca niveditaṃ /
tato rajāśoko vītaśokaṃ rājālaṅkāramaulipaṭṭabaddhaṃ ca siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati / adyāpyahaṃ jīvāmi, tvaṃ rājā saṃvṛttaḥ / tato rājñābhihitaṃ / ko 'traṃ /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, seeing <s>Vītaśoka</s> bound with the royal ornaments and <s>mauli-paṭṭa</s> and seated on the throne, said: 'I am still alive, and you have become king!' Then the king said: 'Who is responsible for this?'

body.text: tato yāvad vadhyaghātakā nīlāmbaravāsinaḥ pralambakeśā ghaṇṭāśabdapāṇayo rājñaḥ pādayornipatyocuḥ / deva kimājñāpayasi /
body.translated_text: Then the executioners, dressed in dark blue garments, with disheveled hair, bells ringing in their hands, fell at the king's feet and said: 'Lord, what do you command?'

body.text: rājāha /
body.translated_text: The king said:

body.text: vītaśoko mayā parityakta iti / yāvad vītaśoka ucyate / saśastraivaidhyaghātairasmābhiḥ parivṛto 'sīti / tatomātyā rājñaḥ pādayornipatya ūcuḥ / deva marṣaya vītaśokaṃ / devasyaiṣa bhrātā /
body.translated_text: '<s>Vītaśoka</s> has been abandoned by me!' Then <s>Vītaśoka</s> was told: 'You are surrounded by us, the armed executioners!' Then the ministers fell at the king's feet and said: 'Lord, forgive <s>Vītaśoka</s>. He is your brother.'

body.text: tato rājñābhihitaṃ / saptāhamasya marṣayāmi / bhrātā caiṣa mama / bhrātuḥ snehādasya saptāhaṃ rājyaṃ prayacchāmi /
body.translated_text: Then the king said: 'I grant him a reprieve of seven days. He is my brother. Out of brotherly affection, I grant him kingship for seven days.'

body.text: yāvat tūryaśatāni saṃpravāditāni / jayaśabdaiścānanditaṃ / prāṇiśatasahasraiścāñjaliḥ kṛtaḥ / strīśataiśca parivṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then hundreds of musical instruments were sounded. He was cheered with cries of 'Victory!' Hundreds of thousands of beings joined their palms in reverence. And he was attended by hundreds of women.

body.text: vadhyaghātakāśca dvāri tiṣṭhanti / divase gate vītaśokasyāgrataḥ sthitvā ārocayanti / nirgataṃ vītaśoka ekaṃ divasaṃ / ṣaḍahānyavaśiṣṭāni / evaṃ dvitīye divase / vistareṇa yāvat saptāhadivase vītaśoko rājālaṅkāravibhūṣito rājño 'śokasya samīpamupanītaḥ /
body.translated_text: But the executioners stood at the door. As each day passed, they stood before <s>Vītaśoka</s> and announced: 'One day has passed, <s>Vītaśoka</s>. Six days remain.' Likewise on the second day. In detail — until on the seventh day, <s>Vītaśoka</s>, adorned with the royal ornaments, was brought before King <s>Aśoka</s>.

body.text: tato rājñāśokenābhihitaṃ / vītaśoka kaccit sugītaṃ sunṛtyaṃ suvāditamiti / vītaśoka uvāca / na me dṛṣṭaṃ vā syācchru taṃ veti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s> said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, was the singing good, the dancing good, the music good?' <s>Vītaśoka</s> said: 'I have neither seen nor heard anything.' And he said:

children.text: yena śrutaṃ bhaved gītaṃ nṛtyaṃ cāpi nirīkṣitaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'He who has heard the singing, who has watched the dancing,

children.text: rasāścāsvāditā yena sa brūyāt tava nirṇayaṃ //
children.translated_text: who has savored the flavors — let him give you his verdict.'

body.text: rājāha / vītaśoka idaṃ mayā rājyaṃ saptāhaṃ tava dattaṃ / taryaśatāni saṃpravāditāni / jayaśabdaiścānanditaṃ / añjaliśatāni pragṛhītāni / strīśataiśca paricīrṇaḥ / kathaṃ tvaṃ kathayasi naiva me dṛṣṭaṃ na śrutamiti / vītaśoka uvāca /
body.translated_text: The king said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, I gave you this kingship for seven days. Hundreds of instruments were sounded. You were cheered with cries of victory. Hundreds of joined palms were raised. You were attended by hundreds of women. How can you say "I have neither seen nor heard anything"?' <s>Vītaśoka</s> said:

children.text: na me dṛṣṭaṃ nṛtyaṃ na ca nṛpa śruto gītaninadaḥ
children.translated_text: 'I have not seen the dancing, nor, O king, have I heard the sound of singing;

children.text: na me gandhā ghrātā na ca khalu rasā me 'dya viditāḥ /
children.translated_text: I have not smelled any fragrance, nor indeed have I known any flavor today;
I have not felt the touch of gold, gems, and necklaces upon my body —
surrounded by women, my mind was bound by [the thought of] death.'
'Women, dancing, singing, palatial beds, rules of seating,
youth, beauty, wealth, and the earth rich with many varied gems —

children.text: nirānandā śūnyā mama tu varaśayyā gatasukhā
children.translated_text: all were joyless, empty; even the finest couch was devoid of comfort for me,
seeing the executioners standing at the door in their dark blue garments.'
'Having heard the dreadful sound of the bells of the one dressed in dark blue,
a terrible fear of death arose in me, O lord of kings.'
'Pierced by the arrow of death, I did not hear the excellent singing,

children.text: nādrākṣaṃ nṛpate nṛtyaṃ na ca bhoktuṃ manaḥspṛhā //
children.translated_text: I did not see the dancing, O king, nor did my mind desire to eat.'
'Seized by the fever of death, I could not even sleep;
my entire night passed in contemplating death alone.'

body.text: rājāha / vītaśoka / mā tāvat / tavaikajanmikasya maraṇabhayāt tava rājaśriyaṃ prāpya harṣo notpannaḥ / kiṃ punarbhikṣavo ye janmaśatamaraṇabhayabhītāḥ sarvāṇyupapattyāyatanāni duḥkhānyanusṛtāni paśyanti / narake tāvaccharīrasaṃtāpakṛtamagnidāhaduḥkhaṃ ca tiryakṣvanyonyabhakṣaṇaparitrāsaduḥkhaṃ, preteṣu kṣuttarṣaduḥkhaṃ / paryeṣṭisamudācāraduḥkhaṃ manuṣyeṣu / cyavanapatanabhraṃśaduḥkhaṃ deveṣu / ebhiḥ pañcabhirduḥkhaistrailokyamanuṣaktaṃ śārīramānasairduḥkhairutpīḍitā vadhakabhūtān skandhān paśyanti / śūnyagrāmabhūtānyāyatanāni, caurabhūtāni viṣayāṇi kṛtsnaṃ ca traidhātukamanityāgninā pradīptaṃ paśyanti / teṣāṃ rāgaḥ kathamutpadyate / āha ca /
body.translated_text: The king said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, wait — you, [fearing] the death of a single lifetime, did not experience joy even upon attaining royal glory. How much more so the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), who, fearing the death of a hundred births, see all the abodes of rebirth as suffused with suffering! In the hells, there is the suffering of burning by fire caused by bodily torment; among animals, the suffering of the terror of being devoured by one another; among <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), the suffering of hunger and thirst; among humans, the suffering of seeking and social interaction; among the gods, the suffering of falling, descending, and losing one's station. By these five sufferings, the triple world is afflicted; tormented by bodily and mental sufferings, they see the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as executioners, the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) as empty villages, the sense-objects as thieves, and the entire triple realm as blazing with the fire of impermanence. How could passion arise in them?' And he said:

children.translated_text: 'When from the fear of death of just one lifetime, no joy arises in you
whose mind is constantly scorched by pleasant sense-objects —
how much less will joy in food and the like arise in the minds of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks)
who contemplate the death yet to come over hundreds of births?'

children.text: teṣāṃ na vastraśayanāsanabhojanādi mokṣe 'bhiyuktamanasāṃ janayeta saṅgaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Clothing, beds, seats, food, and the like should not produce attachment in those whose minds are devoted to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) —
they who see the body as resembling a murderous enemy, and the impermanent existences as a house on fire.'

children.text: kathaṃ ca teṣāṃ na bhaved vimokṣo mokṣārthināṃ janmaparāṅamukhāṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'And how would liberation not be [attained] by those seekers of liberation who have turned away from birth,
whose minds turn away from all objects of pleasure, as water [rolls off] a lotus petal?'

body.text: yadā vītaśoko rājñāśokenopāyena bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasāditaḥ sa kṛtakarapuṭa uvāca / deva eṣo 'haṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi / dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃṅghaṃ ceti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: When <s>Vītaśoka</s> had been brought to faith in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> through King <s>Aśoka</s>'s stratagem, he joined his palms and said: 'Lord, I go for refuge to that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One — and to the <s>Dharma</s> and the community of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks).' And he said:

children.translated_text: 'I go for refuge to [the one with] eyes pure as a newly-blossomed lotus, the Awakened One,
honored by the wise, the divine, and humans — the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), free from passion, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'

body.text: atha rājāśoko vītaśokaṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajyovāca / na tvaṃ mayā parityaktaḥ / api tu buddhaśāsanābhiprasādārthaṃ tava mayā eṣa upāyaḥ pradarśitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s> embraced <s>Vītaśoka</s> by the neck and said: 'You were not abandoned by me. Rather, this stratagem was shown to you by me for the purpose of bringing you to faith in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: tato vītaśoko gandhapuṣpamālyādivāditrasamudayena bhagavataścaityānarcayati / saddharmaṃ ca śrṛṇoti / saṅghe ca kārāṃ kurute /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vītaśoka</s> honored the shrines of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with an assemblage of incense, flowers, garlands, and instrumental music. He listened to the true <s>Dharma</s>. And he made offerings to the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

body.text: sa kukkuṭārāmaṃ gataḥ / tatra yaśo nāma sthaviraḥ arhan ṣaḍabhijñaḥ / sa tasya purato niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya / sthaviraśca tamavalokayitumārabdhaḥ /
body.translated_text: He went to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery). There was an elder named <s>Yaśas</s>, an <s>arhat</s> (worthy one) possessed of the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges). He [<s>Vītaśoka</s>] sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And the elder began to observe him.

body.text: sa paśyati vītaśokamupacitahetukaṃ caramabhavikaṃ tenaivāśrayenārhattvaṃ prāptavyaṃ / tena tasya pravrajyāyā varṇo bhāṣitaḥ / tasya śrutvā
body.translated_text: He saw that <s>Vītaśoka</s> had accumulated [sufficient] causes, was in his final existence, and would attain <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an arhat) in that very body. He then praised the virtues of going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>) to him. Hearing this,

body.text: spṛhā jātā / pravrajeyaṃ bhagavacchāsane / tata utthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ sthaviramuvāca / labheyamahaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ careyamahaṃ bhavato 'ntike brahmacaryaṃ / sthavira uvāca / vatsa / rājānamaśokamanujñāpayasveti /
body.translated_text: a longing arose [in him]: 'I would go forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then, rising and joining his palms, he said to the elder: 'May I obtain the going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), the full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s> (Doctrine and Discipline)? May I practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in your presence.' The elder said: 'Child, you must obtain the permission of King <s>Aśoka</s>.'

body.text: tato vītaśoko yena rājāśokastenopasaṃkramya kṛtāñjaliruvāca / deva anujānīhi māṃ / pravrajiṣyāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye samyageva śraddhayāgārādanāgārikāṃ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vītaśoka</s> approached King <s>Aśoka</s>, and with joined palms said: "Lord, give me permission! I wish to go forth into the homeless life from the household life with right faith in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline)." And he said:

children.text: ubhdānto 'smi niraṃkuśo gaja iva vyāvartito vibhramāt
children.translated_text: "I have been tamed, like an elephant freed from the goad, turned back from delusion
by the goad born of your wisdom, properly, through the teachings of the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: ekaṃ tvarhasi me varaṃ pravarituṃ tvaṃ pārthivānāṃ pate
children.translated_text: You should grant me this one boon, O lord of kings:
may I wear the auspicious mark of the supreme teaching of the one who is the light of the world."
