body.text: śrutvā ca rājā sāśrukaṇṭho vītaśokaṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajyovāca / vītaśoka / alamanena vyavasāyena / pravrajyā khalu vaivarṇīkābhyupagatā vāsa pāṃśukūlaṃ /
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king, his throat choked with tears, embracing <s>Vītaśoka</s> around the neck, said: "<s>Vītaśoka</s>! Enough of this resolve! The going forth indeed involves a discolored appearance, wearing <s>pāṃśukūla</s> (rag-robes),

body.text: prāvaraṇaṃ parijanojjhitam / āhāroṃ bhaikṣaṃ parakule / śayanāsanaṃ vṛkṣamūle tṛṇasaṃstaraḥ parṇasaṃstaraḥ / byābādhe khalvapi bhaiṣajyamasulabhaṃ / pūtimuktaṃ ca bhojanaṃ / tvaṃ ca sukumāraḥ śītoṣṇakṣitpipāsānāṃ duḥkhānāmasahiṣṇuḥ / prasīda nivartaya mānasaṃ /
body.translated_text: a garment cast off by others, food obtained by begging in others' houses, sleeping and sitting at the foot of trees on a bed of grass or leaves. Even in illness, medicine is hard to obtain, and the food is putrid and plain. But you are delicate, unable to endure the sufferings of cold, heat, hunger, and thirst. Please, turn your mind from this!"

body.text: vītaśoka uvāca / deva /
body.translated_text: <s>Vītaśoka</s> said: "Lord,

children.text: naivāhaṃ tanna jāne na viṣayatṛṣito nāyāsavihataḥ
children.translated_text: it is not that I do not know this, nor that I am thirsting for sense pleasures, nor that I am afflicted by weariness;
I am not one desiring to go forth because my power has been seized by enemies, nor am I a wretched noble.
Having seen this world afflicted by suffering, carried away by death, overcome by calamities,
fearing birth, I am resolved to go on the auspicious, fearless path."

body.text: śrutvā rājāśokaḥ saśabdaṃ praruditumārabdhaḥ / atha vītaśoko rājānamanunayannuvāca / deva /
body.translated_text: Having heard this, King <s>Aśoka</s> began to weep aloud. Then <s>Vītaśoka</s>, consoling the king, said: "Lord,

children.text: saṃsāradolāmabhiruhya lolāṃ yadā nipāto niyataḥ prajānāṃ /
children.translated_text: when beings have ascended the unsteady swing of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence), the fall of creatures is certain;

children.text: kimārthamāgacchati vikriyā te sarveṇa sarvasya yadā viyogaḥ //
children.translated_text: why does distress come to you, when separation from everything is inevitable for all?"

body.text: rājāha / vītaśoka / bhaikṣe tāvadabhyāsaḥ kriyatāṃ / rājakule vṛkṣavāṭikāyāṃ tasya tṛṇasaṃstaraḥ saṃstṛtaḥ / bhojanaṃ cāsya dattaṃ / so 'ntaḥpuraṃ paryaṭati mahārhaṃ cāhāraṃ labhate /
body.translated_text: The king said: "<s>Vītaśoka</s>, at least let practice in begging be undertaken first." In the royal grounds, in a garden, a bed of grass was spread for him. And food was given to him. He wandered within the inner palace and received fine food.

body.text: tato rājñāntaḥpurikābhihitā / pravrajitasārūpyamasyāhāramanuprayaccheti / tena yāvadabhidūṣitā pūtikamāṣā labdhāḥ / tāṃśca
body.translated_text: Then the king instructed the women of the inner palace: "Give him food befitting a renunciant." Thereupon, spoiled beans were obtained for him. And those

body.text: paribhoktumārabdhaḥ / dṛṣṭvā rājñāśokena nivāritaḥ / anujñātaśca pravraja, kintu pravrajitvā upadarśayiṣyasi /
body.translated_text: he began to eat. Seeing this, King <s>Aśoka</s> stopped him and gave him permission: "Go forth! But after going forth, you must come to see me."

body.text: sa yāvat kukkuṭārāmaṃ gataḥ / tasya buddhirutpannā / yadi iha pravrajiṣyāmi ākīrṇo bhaviṣyāmi / tato videheṣu janapadeṣu gatvā pravrajitaḥ / tatastena yujyatā yāvadarhattvaṃ prāptaṃ /
body.translated_text: He went to <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (the Cock's Monastery). The thought arose in him: "If I go forth here, I will be surrounded by crowds." So he went to the <s>Videha</s> country and went forth there. Then, applying himself diligently, he attained <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat).

body.text: athāyuṣmato vītaśokasya arhattvaṃ prāptasya vimuktiprītisukhasaṃvedina etadabhavat / asti khalu me [draṣṭukāmo bhrātā / tataḥ pāṭaliputrāya prasthitaḥ /] pūrvaṃ rājño 'śokasya gṛhadvāramanuprāptaḥ / tato dauvārikamuvāca / gaccha rājño 'śokasya nivedaya vītaśoko dvāritiṣṭhati devaṃ draṣṭukāma iti /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, having attained <s>Arhattva</s>, experiencing the bliss of liberation, thought: "My brother surely wishes to see me." So he set out for <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. He first arrived at the gate of King <s>Aśoka</s>'s residence. Then he said to the doorkeeper: "Go, announce to King <s>Aśoka</s> that <s>Vītaśoka</s> stands at the door, wishing to see the king."

body.text: tato dauvāriko rājānamaśokamabhigamyovāca / deva, diṣṭyā vṛddhi rvītaśoko 'bhyāgato dvāri tiṣṭhati devaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ / tato rājñābhihitaṃ / gaccha śīghraṃ praveśayeti /
body.translated_text: Then the doorkeeper approached King <s>Aśoka</s> and said: "Lord, by good fortune and prosperity, <s>Vītaśoka</s> has arrived and stands at the door wishing to see the king." Then the king said: "Go, bring him in quickly!"

body.text: yāvad vītaśoko rājakulaṃ praviṣṭaḥ / dṛṣṭvā ca rājāśokaḥ siṃhāsanādutthāya mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa [bhūmau nipatitaḥ / tataḥ sa] āyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ prarudannuvāca /
body.translated_text: When <s>Vītaśoka</s> entered the royal palace, King <s>Aśoka</s>, seeing him, rose from the lion-throne and fell to the ground with his whole body, like a tree cut at the root. Then, gazing at the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, he wept and said:

children.text: bhūteṣu saṃsargagateṣu nityaṃ dṛṣṭvāpi māṃ naiti yathā vikāraṃ /
children.translated_text: "Among beings who are always subject to association, even seeing me, he does not undergo any change of emotion;
I think he is satiated with the supreme flavor of wisdom, a flavor beyond all other flavors, attained through the force of detachment."

body.text: atha rājño 'śokasya rāghagupto nāmāgrāmātyaḥ / sa paśyatyāyuṣmato vītaśokasya pāṃśukūlaṃ ca cīvaraṃ mṛnmayaṃ pātraṃ yāvadannabhakṣaṃ lūhapraṇītaṃ / dṛṣṭvā ca rājñaḥ pādayornipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca / deva yathāyamalpecchaḥ santuṣṭaśca niyatamayaṃ kṛtakaraṇīyo bhaviṣyati / prītirutpādyeta / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now King <s>Aśoka</s> had a chief minister named <s>Rādhagupta</s>. He saw the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>'s <s>pāṃśukūla</s> (rag-robe) garment, his earthen bowl, and his coarse and plain food. Seeing this, he fell at the king's feet and said with joined palms: "Lord, since he is of few desires and contented, he will surely have accomplished what was to be done. Let joy arise! For what reason?

children.translated_text: He whose food is obtained by begging, whose garment is a <s>pāṃśukūla</s> (rag-robe),

children.text: nivāso vṛkṣamūlaṃ ca tasya hyaniyataṃ kathaṃ //
children.translated_text: and whose dwelling is at the root of a tree — how can he not be one who has attained certainty?

children.text: nirāsravaṃ yasya mano viśālaṃ nirāmayaṃ copacitaṃ śarīraṃ /
children.translated_text: He whose mind is vast and free from defilements, whose body is healthy and well-nourished,

children.text: svacchandato jīvitasādhanaṃ ca nityotsavaṃ tasya manuṣyaloke //
children.translated_text: who sustains his life as he pleases — for him there is an eternal festival in the world of men."

body.text: śrutvā tato rājā prītamanā uvāca /
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king, with a pleased mind, said:

children.translated_text: "Having relinquished the <s>Maurya</s> lineage, the city of <s>Magadha</s>, and the entire collection of jewels,
seeing him who has come under self-control, who has abandoned pride, conceit, delusion, and aggression,

children.text: atyuddhatamiva manye yaśasā pūtaṃ puramiva gehaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: I consider it supremely exalted — his fame has purified this city and home, as it were.
May the noble teaching of the <s>Daśabaladhara</s> (Bearer of the Ten Powers) be followed by you!"

body.text: atha rājāśokaḥ sarvāṅgeṇa parigṛhya prajñapta evāsane niṣādayāmāsa / praṇītena cāhāreṇa svahastaṃ santarpayati / bhuktavantaṃ
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, embracing him with all his limbs, seated him on a prepared seat. He served him fine food with his own hand. Having learned that he had eaten,

body.text: viditvā ghautahastamapanītapātramāyuṣmato vītaśokasya purato niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: with hands washed and the bowl removed, he sat before the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: athāyuṣmān vītaśoko rājānamaśokaṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayannuvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, instructing King <s>Aśoka</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, said:

children.translated_text: "With diligence, let the royal sovereignty be exercised;
always honor the Three Jewels, which are hard to obtain, O king!"

body.text: sa yāvad dharmyayā kathayā saṃpraharṣayitvā saṃprasthitaḥ / atha rājāśokaḥ kṛtakarapuṭaḥ pañcabhiramātyaśataiḥ parivṛto 'nekaiśca paurajanasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛta āyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokamanuvrajitumārabdhaḥ / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: Having thus gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he set out to depart. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, with palms joined, surrounded by five hundred ministers and accompanied and honored by many thousands of citizens, began to follow the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>. For it will be said:

children.translated_text: "The younger brother is followed by the elder king with respect;
this indeed is the praiseworthy, visible fruit of the going forth."

body.text: tata āyusmān vītaśokaḥ svaguṇānubhdāvayan paśyataḥ sarvajanakāyasya ṛddhyā vaihāyasamutpatya prakrāntaḥ / atha rājāśokaḥ kṛtakarapuṭaḥ prāṇikaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto gaganatalāvasaktadṛṣṭirāyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokaṃ nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, manifesting his spiritual powers, rose into the sky by <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) and departed, before the eyes of all the people. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, with palms joined, surrounded and honored by hundreds of thousands of living beings, gazing upward at the sky, watching the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, said:

children.translated_text: "Free from attachment to your own kinfolk, you depart like a bird,
as if rebuking us who are bound by the fetters of passion for wealth and glory.
This is the fruit of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) for one who is self-dependent, peaceful, and who moves according to the mind's resolve,
but it cannot be seen by those blinded by passion.

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: "Indeed, we who were proud of our glory have been humbled by this supreme supernatural power;
indeed, we who were puffed up with pride in our wisdom have been made to bow our heads by this insight.
We who were blind and deluded in mind regarding the fruits of attainment have been shaken by one who has achieved his goal;
in short, we who have tearful faces and are full of sorrow have rightly been set free."

body.text: tatrāyuṣmān vītaśokaḥ pratyantikeṣu janapadeṣu śayyāśanāya nirgataḥ / tasya ca mahāvyādhirutpannaḥ / śrutvā ca rājñāśokena bhaiṣajyamupasthāyakāśca visarjitāḥ / tasya tena vyādhinā spṛṣṭasya śiraḥ khustamabhavat / yadā ca vyādhirnirgatastasya viruḍhāni śirasi romāṇi / tena vaidyopasthāyakāśca visarjitāḥ / tasya ca gorasaḥ prāya āhāronusevyate / sa ghoṣaṃ gatvā bhaikṣaṃ paryaṭati /
body.translated_text: There the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> went to the border regions for his lodging and sustenance. And a great illness arose in him. Hearing this, King <s>Aśoka</s> sent medicine and attendants. Afflicted by that illness, his head became bald. When the illness departed, the hair on his head grew back. He then sent away the doctors and attendants. His food was mostly dairy products. He went to a cowherds' settlement and wandered for alms.

body.text: tasmiṃśca samaye puṇḍavardhananagare nirgranthopāsakena buddhapratimā nirgranthasya pādayornipatitā citrārpitā / upāsakenāśokasya rājño niveditaṃ / śrutvā ca rājñābhihitaṃ śīghramānīyatāṃ /
body.translated_text: At that time, in the city of <s>Puṇḍavardhana</s>, a lay follower of the <s>Nirgrantha</s> (Jain) sect had painted a picture showing the image of the <s>Buddha</s> bowing at the feet of a <s>Nirgrantha</s>. A lay Buddhist reported this to King <s>Aśoka</s>. Hearing this, the king ordered: "Bring him here at once!"

body.text: tasyordhvaṃ yojanaṃ yakṣāḥ śruṇvanti / adho yojanaṃ nāgāḥ / yāvattaṃ tatkṣaṇena yakṣairupanītaṃ / dṛṣṭvā ca rājñā ruṣitenābhihitaṃ / puṇḍavardhane sarve ājīvikāḥ praghātayitavyāḥ / yāvadekadivase 'ṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi ājīvikānāṃ praghātitāni /
body.translated_text: The <s>Yakṣas</s> (spirits) hear commands up to a <s>yojana</s> (league) above, and the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) a <s>yojana</s> below. That man was brought instantly by the <s>Yakṣas</s>. Seeing him, the enraged king ordered: "All <s>Ājīvikas</s> in <s>Puṇḍavardhana</s> are to be slaughtered!" In a single day, eighteen thousand <s>Ājīvikas</s> were killed.

body.text:
tataḥ pāṭaliputre bhūyo 'nyena nirgranthopāsakena buddhapratimā nirgranthasya pādayornipatitā citrārpitā / śrutvā ca rājñāmarṣitena sa nirgranthopāsakaḥ sabandhuvargo gṛhaṃ praveśayitvāgninā dagdhaḥ / ājñaptaṃ ca yo me nirgranthasya śiro dāsyati tasya dīnāraṃ dāsyāmi / iti ghoṣitaṃ /
sa cāyuṣmān vītaśoka ābhīrasya gṛhe rātrivāsamupagataḥ / tasya ca vyādhinā kliṣṭasya lūhāni cīvarāṇi dīrghakeśanakhaśmaśru / ābhīryā buddhirutpannā nirgrantho 'yamasmākaṃ gṛhe rātrivāsamupagataḥ / svāminamuvāca / āryaputra sampanno 'yamasmākaṃ dīnāraḥ / imaṃ nirgranthaṃ praghātayitvā śiro rājño 'śokasyopanāmayeyamiti /
body.translated_text:
Then in <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, yet another lay follower of the <s>Nirgranthas</s> painted a picture showing the image of the <s>Buddha</s> bowing at the feet of a <s>Nirgrantha</s>. Hearing this, the king in his fury had that <s>Nirgrantha</s> lay follower, together with his relatives, confined in his house and burned with fire. And a decree was proclaimed: "Whoever brings me the head of a <s>Nirgrantha</s>, I will give him a <s>dīnāra</s> (gold coin)." This was publicly announced.
Now the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> had taken up night-lodging in the house of an <s>Ābhīra</s> (cowherd). Due to his illness, his robes were ragged, and his hair, nails, and beard had grown long. The <s>Ābhīra</s>'s wife thought: "This <s>Nirgrantha</s> has come to stay the night in our house." She said to her husband: "Noble husband, our <s>dīnāra</s> is secured! Let us kill this <s>Nirgrantha</s> and present his head to King <s>Aśoka</s>."

body.text: tataḥ sa ābhīro 'siṃ niṣkoṣaṃ kṛtvā āyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokamabhigataḥ / āyuṣmatā ca vītaśokena pūrvāntaṃ jñānaṃ kṣiptaṃ / paśyati svayaṃkṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalamidamupasthitaṃ / tataḥ karmapratiśaraṇo bhūtvāvasthitaḥ / tena tathāsyābhīreṇa śiraśchinnaṃ / rājño 'śokasyopanītaṃ / dīnāraṃ prayaccheti /
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Ābhīra</s>, having unsheathed his sword, approached the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>. The venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> cast his knowledge into the past. He saw that this was the ripening of actions he himself had done. Then, taking refuge in <s>karma</s> (the law of actions), he remained still. The <s>Ābhīra</s> thus cut off his head and brought it to King <s>Aśoka</s>, saying: "Give me the <s>dīnāra</s>."

body.text: dṛṣṭvā ca rājñāśokena na parijñātaṃ / viralāni cāsya śirasi romāṇi na vyaktimupagacchanti / tato vaidyā upasthāyakā ānītāḥ / tairdṛṣṭvābhihitaṃ / deva vītaśokasyait śiraḥ / śrutvā rājā murcchito bhūmau patitaḥ / yāvaj jalasekaṃ dattvā sthāpitaḥ / amātyaiścābhihitaṃ / deva vītarāgāṇāmapi atra pīḍā jātā / dīyatāṃ sarvasattveṣvabhayapradānaṃ /
body.translated_text: Seeing it, King <s>Aśoka</s> did not recognize it, for the hairs on the head were sparse and not clearly visible. Then doctors and attendants were brought. Having examined it, they said: "Lord, this is the head of <s>Vītaśoka</s>." Hearing this, the king fainted and fell to the ground. They revived him by sprinkling water. The ministers said: "Lord, even for those free from passion, suffering has arisen here. Let a grant of safety be given to all beings."

body.text: yāvadrājñābhayapradānaṃ dattaṃ, na bhūyaḥ kaścit praghātayitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king gave a grant of safety: no one else shall be killed henceforth.

body.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayachettāram āyuṣmantamupaguptaṃ pṛcchanti / kiṃ karma kṛtamāyuṣmatā vītaśokena yasya karmaṇo vipākena śastreṇa praghātitaḥ / sthavira uvāca / tena hyāyuṣmantaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu / śūyatāṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having doubts, asked the venerable <s>Upagupta</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What <s>karma</s> (action) was done by the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, by the ripening of which he was killed by the sword?" The elder said: "Then listen, venerable ones, to the actions done by him in previous births.

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani anyatamo lubdho mṛgān praghātayitvā jīvikāṃ kalpayati / aṭavyāmudapānaṃ / sa tatra lubdho gatvā paśān yantrāṃśca sthāpayitvā mṛgān praghātayati /
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past, a certain hunter made his living by killing deer. In the forest there was a water-hole. That hunter went there, set traps and snares, and killed the deer.

body.text: asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante / vistaraḥ / anyataraḥ pratyekabuddhas tasminnudapāne āhārakṛtyaṃ kṛtvodapānāduttīrya vṛkṣamūle paryaṅkeṇa niṣaṇṇaḥ / tasya gandhena mṛgāstasminnudapāne
body.translated_text: In the absence of <s>Buddhas</s> arising in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) appear. In detail: a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, having attended to his meal at that water-hole, climbed out and sat cross-legged at the root of a tree. Because of his scent, the deer at that water-hole

body.text: nābhyāgatāḥ / sa lubdha āgatya paśyati naiva mṛgā udapānamabhyāgatāḥ / padānusāreṇa ca taṃ pratyekabuddhamabhigataḥ / dṛṣṭvā cāsya buddhirutpannā / anenaiṣa ādīnava utpāditaḥ / tenāsiṃ niṣkoṣaṃ kṛtvā sa pratyekabuddhaḥ praghātitaḥ /
body.translated_text: did not come. The hunter, arriving, saw that no deer had come to the water-hole. Following the footprints, he approached that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Seeing him, the thought arose in him: "This one has caused this misfortune." Then, unsheathing his sword, he killed that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve āyuṣmantaḥ / yo 'sau lubdhaḥ sa eṣa vitaśokaḥ / yatrānena mṛgāḥ praghātitās tasya karmaṇo vipākena mahān vyādhirutpannaḥ /
body.translated_text: What do you think, venerable ones? That hunter was none other than this <s>Vītaśoka</s>. As a result of the <s>karma</s> of killing those deer, a great illness arose in him.

body.text: yatpratyekabuddhaḥ śastreṇa praghātitastasya karmaṇo vipākena bahūni varṣasahasrāṇi narakeṣu duḥkhamanubhūya pañcajanmaśatani manuṣyaṣupapannaḥ śastreṇa praghātitaḥ / tatkarmāvaśeṣeṇaitarhi arhattvaprāpto 'pi śastreṇa praghātitaḥ /
body.translated_text: As the ripening of the deed of slaying a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) with a weapon, having experienced suffering in the hells for many thousands of years, and having been born as a human for five hundred lifetimes and slain by a weapon [each time] — by the residual force of that <s>karma</s>, even now, though he had attained <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an arhat), he was slain by a weapon.

body.text: kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena uccakule upapannaḥ / arhattvaṃ ca prāptaṃ /
body.translated_text: What <s>karma</s> did he perform by which he was born into a high family? And by which he attained <s>arhattva</s>?

body.text: sthavira uvāca / kāśyape samyaksambuddhe pravrajitaḥ / abhūt pradānaruciḥ / tena dāyakadānapatayaḥ saṅghabhaktāḥ kārāpitāḥ / tarpaṇāni yavāgūpānāni nimantraṇākāni [kārāpitāni] stūpeṣu ca chatrāṇyavaropitāni / dhvajapatākāgandhamālyapuṣpavāditrasamudayena pūjāḥ kṛtāḥ / tasya karmaṇo vipākenoccakula upapannaḥ / yāvad daśavarṣasahasrāṇi brahmacaryaṃ caritvā samyak praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ / tasya karmaṇo vipākenārhattvaṃ prāptamiti /
body.translated_text: The elder said: Under the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s> (<s>Buddha</s>), he went forth into the homeless life. He was fond of giving. Through his efforts, donors and patrons of giving were established, communal meals for the <s>Saṅgha</s> were arranged, ritual feedings, rice-gruel offerings, and invitation-ceremonies [were arranged], and parasols were placed upon <s>stūpas</s>. Worship was performed with an assembly of banners, flags, incense, garlands, flowers, and musical instruments. As the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he was born into a high family. And having practised <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate spiritual life) for ten thousand years and having made a proper aspiration, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he attained <s>arhattva</s>.

body.text: iti śrīdivyāvadāne vītaśokāvadānamaṣṭāviṃśatitamaṃ /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the noble <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Vītaśokāvadāna</s> (The Legend of <s>Vītaśoka</s>) is the twenty-eighth.

children.translated_text: <s>Kunālāvadāna</s> (The Legend of <s>Kunāla</s>)
The Sub-tale of the Minister <s>Yaśas</s>

body.text: sa idānīmacirajātaprasādo buddhāśāsane yatra śākyaputrīyān dadarśa, ākīrṇe rahasi vā tatra śirasā pādayornipatya vandate sma /
body.translated_text: Now he [King <s>Aśoka</s>], whose faith in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> had recently arisen, wherever he saw the sons of the <s>Śākya</s> (Buddhist monks), whether in a crowd or in a secluded place, would bow down with his head at their feet and pay homage.

body.text: tasya ca yaśo nāmāmātyaḥ paramaśrāddho bhagavati / sa taṃ rājānamuvāca /
body.translated_text: He had a minister named <s>Yaśas</s>, who was supremely devoted to the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). He said to the king:

body.text: deva nārhasi sarvarṇapravrajitānāṃ praṇipātaṃ kartuṃ / santi hi śākyaśrāmaṇerakāścaturbhyo varṇebhyaḥ pravrajitā iti / tasya rājā na kiṃcidavocad /
body.translated_text: "Your Majesty should not make prostrations to those who have gone forth from all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes). For among the <s>Śākya</s> ascetics there are those ordained from all four <s>varṇas</s>." The king said nothing to him in reply.

body.text: atha sa rājā kenacit kālāntareṇa sarvasacivān uvāca / vividhānāṃ prāṇināṃ śirobhiḥ kāryaṃ / tattvamamukasya prāṇinaḥ śīrṣamānaya tvamamukasyeti / yaśo 'mātyaḥ punarājñaptastvaṃ mānuṣaṃ śīrṣamānayeti / samānīteṣu ca śīraḥsvabhihitāḥ / gacchatemāni śirāṃsi mūlyena vikrīṇidhvamiti /
body.translated_text: Then, after some time, the king said to all his ministers: "I need the heads of various creatures. You, bring the head of such-and-such an animal; and you, of such-and-such." To the minister <s>Yaśas</s>, however, the command was given: "You, bring a human head." When the heads had been brought, the king said: "Go and sell these heads for a price."

body.text: atha sarvaśirāṃsi vikrītāni / tadeva mānuṣaṃ śiro na kaścij
body.translated_text: Then all the heads were sold. But that human head, no one

body.text: jagrāha / tato rājñābhihitaḥ / vināpi mūlyena kasmaicid etacchiro dehiti /
body.translated_text: would take. Then the king commanded: "Give this head to someone even without a price."

body.text: na cāsya kaścit pratigrāhako babhūva / tato yaśo 'mātyastasya śirasaḥ pratigrāhakamanāsādya savrīḍo rājānamupetyedamarthamuvāca /
body.translated_text: But no one would accept it. Then the minister <s>Yaśas</s>, finding no one to accept the head, approached the king in embarrassment and spoke thus:

children.translated_text: "The heads of cows, donkeys, camels, deer, and birds have been purchased by men for a price;

children.text: śirastvidaṃ mānuṣamapraśastaṃ na gṛhyate mūlyamṛte 'pi rājan //
children.translated_text: But this ignoble human head is not accepted even without a price, O king."

body.text: atha sa rājā tamamātyamuvāca / kimidamiti / idaṃ mānuṣaśiro na kaścid gṛṇhātīti /
body.translated_text: Then the king said to the minister: "What does this mean?" "This human head — no one will take it."

body.text: amātya uvāca / jugupsitatvāditi / rājābravīt / kimetadeva śiro jugupsitamāhosvit sarvamānuṣaśirāṃsīti / amātya uvāca / sarvamānuṣaśirāṃsīti /
body.translated_text: The minister said: "Because it is an object of disgust." The king said: "Is only this head an object of disgust, or all human heads?" The minister said: "All human heads."

body.text: rājābravīt / kimidaṃ madīyamapi śiro jugupsitamiti / sa ca bhayānnecchati tasmād bhūtārthamabhidhātuṃ / sa rājñābhihitaḥ / amātya satyamucyatāmiti / sa uvāca / evamiti /
body.translated_text: The king said: "Is this head of mine also an object of disgust?" But he [the minister], out of fear, did not wish to state the truth. The king said to him: "Minister, speak the truth." He replied: "It is so."

body.text: tataḥ sa rājā tamamātyaṃ pratijñāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya pratyādiśannimamarthamuvāca / haṃ bho rūpaiśvaryajanitamadavismita yuktamidaṃ bhavataḥ / yasmāttvaṃ bhikṣucaraṇapraṇāmaṃ māṃ vicchandayitumicchasi /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having made the minister stand upon his pledge, admonished him and spoke these words: "Ha! Sir, dazzled by the pride born of beauty and sovereignty — it befits you indeed! For you wish to dissuade me from bowing at the feet of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks).

children.text: vināpi mūlyairvijugupsitatvāt pratigrahītā bhuvi yasya nāsti /
children.translated_text: "He whose head, even without a price, because of its utter loathsomeness, has no one on earth willing to accept it —

children.text: śirastadāsādya mameha puṇyaṃ yadyarjitaṃ kiṃ viparītamatra //
children.translated_text: If, having taken up this [very] head, I have earned merit here, what is wrong in that?

children.text: jātiṃ bhavān paśyati śākyabhikṣuṣvantargatāṃsteṣu guṇānna ceti /
children.translated_text: "You see the birth-class in the <s>Śākya</s> monks, but not the virtues contained within them;
Therefore, out of the intoxication and arrogance of birth, you harm yourself and others through delusion.

children.text: āvāhakāle 'tha vivāhakāle jāteḥ parīkṣā na tu dharmakāle /
children.translated_text: "At the time of betrothal and marriage, there is an examination of birth — but not at the time of practising <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dharmakriyāyā hi guṇā nimitta guṇāśca jātiṃ na vicārayanti //
children.translated_text: For virtues are the basis of the practice of <s>Dharma</s>, and virtues do not inquire into birth.
"If faults found in those of high birth meet with censure in this world,
How then should virtues found in those of low birth not merit honor?

children.text: cittavaśena hi puṃsāṃ kaḍevaraṃ nindyate 'tha satkriyate /
children.translated_text: "It is by the disposition of the mind that men's bodies are either despised or honored;
And since the minds of the <s>Śākya</s> ascetics are pure, I therefore honor the <s>Śākyas</s>.

children.text: yadi guṇaparivarjito dvijātiḥ patita iti prathito 'pi yātyavajñāṃ /
children.translated_text: "If a twice-born man, bereft of virtues, renowned as 'fallen,' meets with contempt,

children.text: nanu nidhanakulodgato 'pi jantuḥ śubhaguṇayukta iti praṇamyapūjyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then surely a being born of a lowly family, if endowed with auspicious qualities, is worthy of being bowed to and worshipped.

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: "Moreover:

children.text: kiṃ te kāruṇikasya śākyavṛṣabhasyaitad vaco na śrutaṃ
children.translated_text: "Have you not heard this teaching of the compassionate Bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>?

children.text: prājñaiḥ sāramasārakebhya iha yantrebhyo grahītuṃ kṣamaṃ /
children.translated_text: The wise are able to extract the essence from things both essential and non-essential here.
If I wish to carry out the command of him whose words are never false,

children.text: vyāhantuṃ ca bhavān yadi prayatate naitat suhṛllakṣaṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: And you endeavor to obstruct it — that is not the mark of a true friend.

children.text: ikṣukṣodavad ujjhito bhuvi yadā kāyo mama svapsyati
children.translated_text: "When this body of mine, cast upon the earth like crushed sugarcane,
Shall lie there, incapable of rising, bowing, joining palms in homage, or performing acts of devotion —

children.text: kāyenāhamanena kinnu kuśalaṃ śakṣyāmi kartuṃ tadā
children.translated_text: What good deed shall I then be able to do with this body?

children.text: tasmān nvarhamataḥ śmaśānanidhanāt sāraṃ grahītuṃ mayā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is fitting that I now extract the essence from it before its end in the cremation ground.
"Those who, from a body destined for destruction — as from a burning house, or as from a treasure-ship sinking in the waters —
Do not extract the essence,
They, not seeing the essence, unskilled in distinguishing the essential from the non-essential, unwise —
They despair at the moment of entering the jaws of the sea-monster of death.
"Through the use of curds, ghee, fresh butter, and milk,
Better is the earthen pot from which the essence has been extracted, even if broken,
Than one that is not much to be lamented. Even so with the body —
When its essence has been extracted through good conduct, no grief comes at the time of death.
"But for those who turn away from good conduct, who are proud,
When death forcibly shatters the pot of the body here,
Then the fire of grief burns their hearts,
Just as in a broken [pot] from which the essence of curds [and ghee] was never obtained.

children.text: kartuṃ vighnamato na me 'rhati bhavān kāyapraṇāmaṃ prati
children.translated_text: "Therefore, you ought not create an obstacle to my bodily prostrations;
For he who, without examination, reckons 'I am superior,' is enveloped in the darkness of delusion.
But the wise man who examines the body by the lamp of the teaching of the <s>Daśabala</s> (the One of Ten Powers, the <s>Buddha</s>)
Does not perceive any inequality in the body between a king and a servant.

body.text:
tvaṅmāṃsāsthiśirāyākṛtprabhṛto bhāvā hi tulyā nṛṇāṃ
āhāryaistu vibhūṣaṇairadhikatā kāyasya niṣpādyate /
etat sāramiheṣyate tu yadimaṃ niśritya kāyādhamaṃ
pratyutthānanamaskṛtādi kuśalaṃ prājñaiḥ samutthāpyate /
iti /
body.translated_text: For the constituents of skin, flesh, bone, sinew, and so forth are indeed alike in all men; it is through adventitious ornaments that superiority of the body is produced. But if this is considered the essence here — that, relying upon this base body, the wise generate wholesome merit through rising, bowing, and the like — [then that is the true purpose]."

body.text: rājāśokopākhyānaṃ
body.translated_text: The Sub-tale of King <s>Aśoka</s>

body.text: athāśoko rājā hi kṣodakasikatāpiṇḍairaṇḍakāṣṭhebhyo 'pi asārataratvaṃ kāyasyāvetya, praṇāmādibhyaḥ samutthasya phalasya bahukalpaśaḥ sthāpayitvā sumeruvan, mahāpṛthivībhyaḥ sārataratāmavekṣya bhagavataḥ
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having understood that the body is even more insubstantial than pellets of powdered sand, castor-oil-plant sticks, and the like, and having perceived that the fruit arising from prostrations and such is, when maintained for many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), more substantial than <s>Sumeru</s> and the great earth, desiring to adorn himself for the worship of the <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One),

body.text: stūpavandanāyām ātmānamalaṅkartukāmo 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ kukkuṭārāmaṃ gatvā tatra vṛddhānte sthitvā kṛtāñjalir uvāca /
body.translated_text: surrounded by his retinue of ministers, went to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery), and standing there at the assembly of elders, with palms joined, said:

children.translated_text: "Is there anyone else designated by the All-Seeing One,
As I was designated by that wise one through the gift of dust?"

body.text: tatra yaśo nāmnā saṅghasthavira uvāca / asti mahārāja / yadā bhagavataḥ parinirvāṇakālasamayastadāpalālaṃ nāgaṃ damayitvā kumbhakārīṃ caṇḍālīṃ gopālīṃ ca nāgaṃ ca mathurāmanuprāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> named <s>Yaśas</s> said: "There is, O great king. When the time of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing) drew near, having tamed the <s>Nāga</s> <s>Apalāla</s> and the potter-woman, the <s>caṇḍālī</s>, and the cowherd-woman, and having arrived at <s>Mathurā</s> with them,

body.text: tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandam āmantrayata / asyāmānanda mathurāyāṃ varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya gupto nāmnā gāndhiko bhaviṣyati / tasya putro bhaviṣyatyupagupto nāmnā avavādakānāmagraḥ alakṣaṇako buddho yo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyati /
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'In this <s>Mathurā</s>, O <s>Ānanda</s>, a hundred years after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a perfume-seller named <s>Gupta</s>. His son will be named <s>Upagupta</s>, foremost among instructors, a Buddha without the marks, who a hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> will carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: paśyasi tvamānanda dūrata eva nīlanīlāmbararājiṃ / evaṃ bhadanta / eṣa ānanda urumuṇḍo nāma parvato 'tra varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya naṭabhaṭikā nāmāraṇyāyatanaṃ bhaviṣyati / etadagraṃ me
body.translated_text: 'Do you see, O <s>Ānanda</s>, that dark-blue line in the distance?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'That, O <s>Ānanda</s>, is the mountain called <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s>. Here, a hundred years after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a forest hermitage called <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>. This will be the foremost'

body.text: ānanda bhaviṣyati śamathānukūlānāṃ śayyāsanānāṃ yaduta naṭabhaṭikā nāmāraṇyāyatanam / āha ca /
body.translated_text: 'of dwelling-places and seats conducive to <s>śamatha</s> (tranquillity meditation) for me, O <s>Ānanda</s> — namely, the forest hermitage called <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>.' And he said:

children.translated_text: "<s>Upagupta</s>, the foremost among instructors, of great renown,
Designated by the Lord of the World, shall carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: rājāha /
body.translated_text: The king said:

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ sa śuddhasattva upapannaḥ / athādyāpi notpadyata iti / sthavira uvāca / utpannaḥ sa mahātmā urumuṇḍe parvate jitakleśo 'rhadgaṇaiḥ parivṛtastiṣṭhati lokānukampārthaṃ / api ca deva /
body.translated_text: "Has that being of pure essence been born? Or has he not yet arisen?" The elder said: "That great soul has been born. On Mount <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s>, having conquered the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), he dwells surrounded by assemblies of <s>arhats</s>, out of compassion for the world. Moreover, O lord:

children.text: sarvajñalīlo hi sa śuddhasattvo dharmaṃ praṇītaṃ vadate gaṇāgre /
children.translated_text: "That being of pure essence, playful as the Omniscient One, teaches the noble <s>Dharma</s> before the assembly;
He shall lead gods, lords of <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and humans by the thousands to the city of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)."

body.text: tena khalu samayenāyuṣmānupagupto 'ṣṭādaśabhirarhatsahasraiḥ parivṛto naṭabhaṭikāraṇyāyatane prativasati / śrutvā ca rājāmātyagaṇān āhūya kathayati /
body.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Upagupta</s>, surrounded by eighteen thousand <s>arhats</s>, was dwelling in the forest hermitage of <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>. Having heard [the elder's words], the king summoned his retinue of ministers and said:

children.translated_text: "Let the army of elephants, chariots, and horses be readied! I shall set out swiftly for Mount <s>Urūmuṇḍa</s>;
I shall behold the noble <s>Upagupta</s>, an <s>arhat</s> freed from all <s>āsravas</s> (defilements), face to face."

body.text: tato 'mātyairabhihitaḥ / deva dūtaḥ preṣayitavyo viṣayanivāsī sa devasya svayamevāgamiṣyati / rājāha / nāsāvasmāka arhatyabhigantum kiṃtu vayamevārhāmastasyābhigantum / api ca /
body.translated_text: Then the ministers said: "Your Majesty, a messenger should be sent. He is a dweller within your domain and will come to Your Majesty of his own accord." The king said: "He is not obliged to come to us; rather, it is we who are obliged to go to him. Moreover:

children.translated_text: "I consider the body of <s>Upagupta</s>, who is equal to the Teacher, to be made of diamond, surpassing even a mountain —
For what man would cast aside the command of <s>Upagupta</s>, who is equal to the Master?"

body.text: yāvad rājñā sthaviropaguptasya sakāśaṃ dūtaḥ preṣitaḥ sthaviradarśanāya āgamiṣyāmīti / sthaviropaguptaścintayati / yadi rājāgamiṣyati mahājanakāyasya pīḍā bhaviṣyati / gocarasya ca / tataḥ sthavireṇābhihitaṃ / svayamevāgamiṣyāmīti /
body.translated_text: Then the king sent a messenger to the elder <s>Upagupta</s> [saying]: 'I shall come for an audience with the elder.' The elder <s>Upagupta</s> reflected: 'If the king comes, there will be hardship for the great multitude, and for the alms-gathering as well.' Then the elder declared: 'I myself shall come.'

body.text: tato rājñā sthaviropaguptasyārthe nauyānenāgamiṣyatīti yāvacca mathurāṃ yāvacca pāṭaliputramantarān nausaṅkramo 'vasthāpitaḥ / atha sthaviropagupto rājño 'śokasya anugrahārtham aṣṭādaśabhirarhatsahasraiḥ parivṛto nāvamabhiruhya pāṭaliputramanuprāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king, [knowing] that the elder <s>Upagupta</s> would come by boat, established a chain of boats between <s>Mathurā</s> and <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, for the purpose of bestowing grace upon King <s>Aśoka</s>, surrounded by eighteen thousand <s>arhats</s>, boarded a boat and arrived at <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.

body.text: tato rājapuruṣai rājño 'śokasya niveditaṃ / deva diṣṭyā vardhasva / anugrahārthaṃ tava sopaguptaścitteśvaraḥ śāsanakarṇadhāraḥ puraskṛtastīrṇabhavaughapāraiḥ sārdhaṃ samabhyāgata eṣa pabhdyāṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the royal attendants reported to King <s>Aśoka</s>: "Your Majesty, rejoice and prosper! For your benefit, <s>Upagupta</s>, the master of minds, the helmsman of the [<s>Buddha</s>'s] teaching, accompanied by those who have crossed to the far shore of the flood of existence, has arrived on foot."

body.text: śrutvā ca rājñā prītamanasā śatasahasramūlyo muktāhāraḥ svaśarīrādavanīya priyākhyāyino dattaḥ / ghāṇṭikaṃ cāhūya kathayati / ghūṣyantāṃ pātaliputre ghaṇṭāḥ / sthaviropaguptasyāgamanaṃ nivedyatāṃ / vaktavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king, his heart filled with joy, removed a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [coins] from his own body and gave it to the bearer of the glad tidings. He then summoned the bell-ringer and said: "Let the bells be rung throughout <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>! Let the arrival of the elder <s>Upagupta</s> be announced! Let it be proclaimed:

children.translated_text: "'He who would cast away poverty, the root of all misfortune, and desires resplendent glory and prosperity here,

children.text: svargāpavargāya ca hetubhūtaṃ sa paśyatāṃ kāruṇikopaguptaṃ //
children.translated_text: And that which is the cause of heaven and final liberation — let him come and behold the compassionate <s>Upagupta</s>!'

children.text: yebhirna dṛṣṭo dvipadapradhānaḥ śāstā mahākāruṇikaḥ svayambhūḥ /
children.translated_text: "'Those who have not seen the supreme among bipeds, the Teacher, the greatly compassionate, self-arisen one —
Let them behold the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, equal to the Teacher, the noble one, the lamp of the three worlds!'"

body.text: yāvadrājñā pāṭaliputre ghaṇṭāṃ ghoṣayitvā nagaraśobhāṃ ca kārayitvā ardhatṛtīyāni yojanāni gatvā sarvavādyena sarvapuṣpagandhamālyena sarvapauraiḥ sarvamātyaiḥ saha sthaviropaguptaṃ pratyudgataḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having caused the bells to be rung throughout <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> and having arranged the adornment of the city, traveled two and a half <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) and, with all musical instruments, with all flowers, incense, and garlands, accompanied by all the citizens and all the ministers, went forth to meet the elder <s>Upagupta</s>.

body.text: dadarśa rājā sthaviropaguptaṃ durata eva aṣṭādaśabhirarhatsahasrairardhacandreṇopaguptaṃ / yadantaraṃ ca rājā sthaviropaguptamadrākṣīt tadantaraṃ hastiskandhād avatīrya padbhyāṃ nadītiramabhigamya ekaṃ pādaṃ nadītīre sthāpya dvitīyaṃ nauphalake sthaviropaguptaṃ sarvāṅgeṇānuparigṛhya nāva uttāritavān / uttārya ca mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇopaguptasya pādayornipatito mukhatuṇḍakena ca pādāvanuparimārjya utthāya dvau jānumaṇḍalau pṛthivītale nikṣipya kṛtāñjaliḥ sthaviropaguptaṃ nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca /
body.translated_text: The king saw the elder <s>Upagupta</s> from a great distance, surrounded in a half-moon [formation] by eighteen thousand <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones). As soon as the king caught sight of the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, he descended from the elephant's back, went on foot to the riverbank, placed one foot on the riverbank and the second on the deck of the boat, and having embraced the elder <s>Upagupta</s> with his whole body, brought him onto the boat. Having brought him across, like a tree cut at the root, he fell with his entire body at <s>Upagupta</s>'s feet, and with the tip of his mouth he wiped the feet all around; then, rising, placing both his knees on the ground, with hands joined in reverence, gazing at the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, he spoke:

children.text: yadā mayā śatrugaṇān nihatya prāptā samudrābharaṇā saśailā /
children.translated_text: When, having slain the hosts of enemies, I obtained this earth adorned with oceans and mountains,

children.text: ekātapatrā pṛthivī tadā me prītirna sā yā sthaviraṃ nirīkṣya //
children.translated_text: sheltered under a single royal umbrella — that joy was not [as great] as [the joy of] beholding the elder.
From seeing you, a twofold serenity arises in me at the beginning of this supreme teaching;

children.text: tvaddarśanāccaiva paropi śuddho dṛṣṭo mayādya apratimaḥ svayambhūḥ //
children.translated_text: and from seeing you, even the supreme one is purified — today I have seen the incomparable Self-born one [through you].

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: śāntiṃgate kāruṇike jinendre tvaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kuruṣe triloke /
children.translated_text: When the compassionate lord of the <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors) has gone to peace, you perform the work of the <s>Buddha</s> in the three worlds;
when the one who bewilders the world, with eyes closed, has perished, you, like the sun, are the maker of the light of knowledge.
You are equal to the Teacher, the single eye of the world, the foremost refuge for those who would instruct;

children.text: vibho mamājñāṃ vada śīghramadya kartāsmi vākyaṃ tava śuddhasattva //
children.translated_text: O powerful one, tell me your command quickly today — I shall carry out your word, O pure-natured one.

body.text: atha sthaviropagupto dakṣiṇena pāṇinā rājānaṃ śirasi parimārjayannuvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, stroking the king's head with his right hand, spoke:

children.translated_text: With diligence, having accomplished [your duties], let your kingly sovereignty continue;
always worship the Three Jewels, which are difficult to obtain, O king.

body.text: api ca mahārāja tena bhagavatā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena tava ca mama śāsanamupanyastaṃ sattvasārathivareṇa gaṇamadhye parīttaṃ paripālyaṃ yatnato 'smābhiḥ / rājāha / sthavira yathāhaṃ nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā tadevānuṣṭhīyate / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, great king, by that <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the supreme charioteer of beings, the teaching has been entrusted to both you and me; the assembly must be diligently protected and guarded by us. The king said: 'Elder, as I have been instructed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, that very thing is being carried out. For:

children.translated_text: With splendid <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary mounds) resembling mountain peaks, with parasols and banners raised aloft, adorned with varied jewels,

children.text: saṃśobhitā me pṛthivī samantād vaistārikā dhātudharāḥ kṛtāśca //
children.translated_text: my earth has been beautified all around, and extensive <s>dhātu</s>-holders (relic shrines) have been established.

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: ātmā putro gṛhaṃ dārāḥ pṛthivī kośameva ca /
children.translated_text: Self, son, household, wife, the earth, and the treasury —
nothing has remained unrenounced under the command of the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of <s>Dharma</s>).

body.text: sthaviropagupta āha / sādhu sādhu mahārāja / etadevānuṣṭheyaṃ / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: The elder <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'Well done, well done, great king! This very thing should be carried out. For:

children.translated_text: Those who live for the <s>Dharma</s> with their bodies, enjoyments, and lives,

children.text: gate kāle na śocanti iṣṭaṃ yānti surālayaṃ //
children.translated_text: when the time comes, they do not grieve; they go to the desired abode of the gods.

body.text: yāvad rājā mahatā śrīsamudayena sthaviropaguptaṃ rājakule praveśayitvā sarvāṅgeṇānuparigṛhya prajñapta evāsane niṣādayāmāsa / sthaviropaguptasya śarīraṃ mṛdu sumṛdu / tadyathā tūlapiśurvā karpāsapiśurvā /
body.translated_text: Then the king, with great pomp and splendor, having brought the elder <s>Upagupta</s> into the royal palace and having embraced him with his whole body, seated him upon a prepared seat. The elder <s>Upagupta</s>'s body was soft, exceedingly soft — like a ball of cotton-wool or a ball of <s>karpāsa</s> (cotton).

body.text: atha rājā sthaviropaguptasya śarīrasaṃsparśamavagamya kṛtāñjaliruvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having perceived the touch of the elder <s>Upagupta</s>'s body, spoke with joined hands:

children.text: mṛdūni te 'ṅgāni udārasattva tūlopamāṅgaṃ kāśikopamaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Your limbs are soft, O noble-natured one, your body is like cotton, comparable to <s>Kāśi</s> (Benares silk);
while I am unfortunate, with rough and harsh limbs, a body devoid of [pleasant] touch, and of coarse nature.

body.text: sthavira uvāca /
body.translated_text: The elder said:

children.text: dānaṃ manāpaṃ suśubhaṃ praṇitaṃ dattaṃ mayā hyapratipudgalasya /
children.translated_text: Agreeable, supremely auspicious, and excellent gifts were given by me to the Incomparable One;

children.text: na pāṃśudānaṃ hi mayā pradattaṃ yathā tvayādāyi tathāgatasya //
children.translated_text: but the gift of dust was not given by me as it was given by you to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: rājāha / sthavira /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Elder,

children.translated_text: in my childhood, long ago, having obtained the supreme field [of merit],
I planted dust there — such is my fruit.'

body.text: atha sthaviro rājānaṃ saṃharṣayannuvāca / mahārāja /
body.translated_text: Then the elder, gladdening the king, spoke: 'Great king,

children.translated_text: behold the greatness of the field [of merit] where even dust grows [into great fruit];
by which you have obtained royal splendor and unsurpassed sovereignty.'
Having heard this, the king, with eyes wide open in wonder, summoned his ministers and said:
'The sovereignty of a <s>balacakravartin</s> (universal monarch) was obtained by me through a mere gift of dust;
why then, O lords, should the <s>Bhagavān</s> not be worshipped with effort?'

body.text: atha rājā sthaviropaguptasya pādayornipatyovāca / sthaviro 'yaṃ me manoratho ye bhagavatā buddhena pradeśā adyuṣitāstān arceyaṃ / cinhāni ca kuryāṃ paścimasyāṃ janatāyāmanugrahārthaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the king, falling at the feet of the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, spoke: 'Elder, this is my heart's desire — that I should worship those places where the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s> once dwelt, and that I should make memorial markers for the benefit of future generations.'

body.text: sthavira uvāca / sādhu mahārāja śobhanaste cittotpādaḥ / ahaṃ pradarśayiṣyāmyadhunā /
body.translated_text: The elder said: 'Well done, great king, excellent is your mental resolve! I shall now show [them to you].

children.translated_text: Those places where the <s>Buddha</s> dwelt — I shall salute them with joined hands,

children.text: gatvā cinhāni teṣveva kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: and having gone, I shall make memorial markers in those very places — of this there is no doubt.'

body.text: atha rājā caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhya gandhamālyapuṣpamādāya sthaviropaguptasahāyaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ / atha sthaviropagupto rājānamaśokaṃ sarvaprathamena lumbinīvanaṃ praveśayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ hastamabhiprasāryovāca / asmin mahārāja pradeśe bhagavān jātaḥ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having marshalled his fourfold army, taking perfumes, garlands, and flowers, set out accompanied by the elder <s>Upagupta</s>. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, first leading King <s>Aśoka</s> into the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, extending his right hand, spoke: 'In this place, great king, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was born.' And he said:

children.translated_text: This indeed is the first <s>caitya</s> (sacred site) of the <s>Buddha</s>, the one of supreme vision;

children.text: jātamātreha sa muniḥ prakrāntaḥ saptapadaṃ bhuvi //
children.translated_text: as soon as the sage was born here, he took seven steps upon the earth.
Having surveyed the four directions, he spoke these words of old:
'This is my last birth, and this is my last dwelling in a womb.'

children.text: atha rājā sarvaśarīreṇa tatra pādayor nipatyotthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ prarudannuvāca /
children.translated_text: Then the king, falling at [the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s] feet there with his whole body, rising with joined hands and weeping, spoke:
Blessed are they, and meritorious, who saw that great sage,
born [into this world], and who heard his delightful words.

body.text: atha sthaviro rājñaḥ prasādabuddhyarthamuvāca / mahārāja kiṃ drakṣyasi tāṃ devatāṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the elder, for the purpose of generating faith in the king, spoke: 'Great king, would you like to see that deity

children.text: yayā dṛṣṭaḥ prajāyan sa vane 'smin vadatāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: by whom he was seen being born in this grove, the foremost of speakers,

children.text: kramamāṇaḥ padān sapta śrutvā vāco yayā muneḥ //
children.translated_text: taking seven steps, and by whom the words of the sage were heard?'

body.text: rājāha / paraṃ sthavira drakṣyāmi / atha sthaviropagupto yasya vṛkṣasya śākhāmavalambaya devī mahāmāyā prasūtā tena dakṣiṇahastamabhiprasārya uvāca /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Yes indeed, elder, I would see [her].' Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, extending his right hand toward the branch of the tree by which Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s> had supported herself when she gave birth, spoke:

children.text: naivāsikā ya ihāśokavṛkṣe sambuddhadarśinī yā devakanyā /
children.translated_text: That divine maiden dwelling here in this <s>aśoka</s> tree, who witnessed the Perfectly Awakened One —

children.text: sākṣādasau darśayatu svadehaṃ rājño hyaśokasya prasādavṛddhyai //
children.translated_text: let her now reveal her own form, for the increase of faith in King <s>Aśoka</s>.

body.text: yāvat sā devatā svarūpeṇa sthaviropaguptasamīpe sthitvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca / sthavira kimājñāpayasi / atha sthaviro rājānamaśokamuvāca / mahārāja iyaṃ sā devatā yayāṃ dṛṣṭo bhagavāñ jāyamānaḥ / atha rājā kṛtāñjalistāṃ devatāmuvāca /
body.translated_text: Thereupon that deity, standing in her own form before the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, spoke with joined hands: 'Elder, what do you command?' Then the elder spoke to King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'Great king, this is that deity by whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> was seen being born.' Then the king, with joined hands, said to that deity:

children.translated_text: You saw him whose limbs were adorned with [the thirty-two] marks, being born, with lotus-wide eyes;

children.text: śrutāstvayā tasya nararṣabhasya vāco manojñāḥ prathamā vane 'smin //
children.translated_text: you heard the first delightful words of that bull among men, here in this grove.

body.text: devatā prāha /
body.translated_text: The deity said:

children.text: mayā hi dṛṣṭaḥ kanakāvadātaḥ prajāyamāno dvipadapradhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed I saw him, radiant as gold, being born, the foremost of bipeds;

children.text: pādāni sapta kramamāṇa eva śrutāśca vācā api tasya śāstuḥ //
children.translated_text: taking his very seven steps, the words of the Teacher were also heard by me.

body.text: rājāha / kathaya devate kīdṛśī bhagavato jāyamānasya śrīrbabhūveti / devatā prāha / na śakyaṃ mayā vāgbhiḥ saṃprakāśayitumapi tu saṃkṣepataḥ śrṛṇu /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Tell me, O deity, what was the splendor of the <s>Bhagavān</s> as he was being born?' The deity said: 'It is not possible for me to express it in words; but hear [it] in brief:

children.translated_text: With a radiance like that of a divine creation, bright as gold, delightful to the eyes in the three worlds including <s>Indra</s>'s realm,

children.text: sasāgarāntā ca mahī saśailā mahārṇavasthā iva nauścacāla //
children.translated_text: the earth with its mountains, bounded by the oceans, trembled like a ship on the great ocean.

body.text: yāvadrājñā jātyāṃ śatasahasraṃ dattaṃ / caityaṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpya rājā prakrāntaḥ / atha sthaviropagupto rājānaṃ kapilavastu niveśayitvā dakṣiṇahastamabhiprasāryovāca / asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvo rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyopanāmitaḥ / taṃ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaśarīramasecanakadarśanaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā rājā sarvaśarīreṇa bodhisattvasya padayornipatitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king gave a hundred thousand [coins] at the birthplace. Having established a <s>caitya</s> (memorial shrine), the king proceeded onward. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, leading the king into <s>Kapilavastu</s> and extending his right hand, spoke: 'In this place, great king, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was presented to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.' Seeing [the place of] him whose body was adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, and whose appearance was captivating, the king fell with his entire body at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [i.e. at the sacred site].

body.text: idaṃ mahārāja śākyavardhaṃ nāma devakulam / atra bodhisattvo jātamātra upanīto devamarcayiṣyatīti / sarvadevatā ca bodhisattvasya pādayornipatitā / tato rājñā śuddhodanena bodhisattvo devatānāmapyayaṃ deva iti tena bodhisattvasya devātideva iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtaṃ / asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvo brāhmaṇānāṃ naimittikānāṃ vipaścikānām upadarśitaḥ / asmin pradeśe 'sitena ṛṣiṇā nirdiṣṭo buddho loke bhaviṣyatīti /
body.translated_text: 'This, great king, is the temple called <s>Śākyavardha</s> (Increaser of the <s>Śākyas</s>). Here the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as soon as he was born, was brought to worship the deity. And all the deities fell at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Therefore King <s>Śuddhodana</s> [said] 'This one is a god even among the gods,' and gave the <s>Bodhisattva</s> the name <s>Devātideva</s> (God above Gods). In this place, great king, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was shown to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who were soothsayers and seers. In this place, the seer <s>Asita</s> declared: "He will become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world."'

body.text: asmin pradeśe mahārāja mahāprajāpatyā saṃvardhitaḥ / asmin pradeśe lipijñānaṃ śikṣāpitaḥ / asmin pradeśe hastigrīvāyāmaśvapṛṣṭhe rathe śaradhanugrahe tomaragrahe 'ṅakuśagrahe kulānurūpāsu vidyāsu pāragaḥ saṃvṛtaḥ / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya vyāyāmaśālā babhūva / asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvo devatāśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ ṣaṣṭibhiḥ strīsahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ ratimanubhūtavān /
body.translated_text: 'In this place, great king, he was raised by <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>. In this place, he was taught the knowledge of writing. In this place, he became accomplished in the arts befitting his family — on the elephant's neck, on horseback, on the chariot, in grasping arrows and bows, in wielding the javelin, in handling the elephant-goad. This was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s exercise hall. In this place, great king, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of deities, enjoyed pleasures together with sixty thousand women.'

body.text: asmin pradeśe bodhisattvo jīrṇāturamṛtasaṃdarśanodvigno vanasaṃśritaḥ / asmin pradeśe jambucchāyāyāṃ niṣadya viviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhamanāsravasadṛśaṃ prathamadhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ / atha pariṇate madhyānhe 'tikrānte bhaktakālasamaye 'nyeṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ chāyā prācīnanimnā prācīnapravaṇā prācīnaprāgbhārā jambucchāyā bodhisattvasya kāyaṃ na jahāti / dṛṣṭvā ca punar rājā śuddhodanaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa bodhisattvasya pādayornipatitāḥ / anena dvāreṇa bodhisattvo devatāśatasahasraiḥ parivṛto 'rdharātre kapilavastuno nirgataḥ /
body.translated_text: 'In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, distressed by the sight of old age, sickness, and death, resorted to the forest. In this place, seated in the shade of a <s>jambu</s> (rose-apple) tree, secluded from sensual pleasures and unwholesome states, with applied thought and sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion, he attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), which resembled the supramundane [state]. Then, when the afternoon had advanced and mealtime had passed, while the shadows of the other trees fell eastward, sloping east, inclining east, the shadow of the <s>jambu</s> tree did not leave the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And seeing this, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> again fell with his entire body at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. By this gate, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of deities, departed from <s>Kapilavastu</s> at midnight.'

body.text: asmin pradeśe bodhisattvena chandakasyāśvamābharaṇāni ca dattvā pratinivartitaḥ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: 'In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having given the horse and ornaments to <s>Chandaka</s>, sent him back.' And he said:

children.translated_text: '<s>Chandaka</s>, the ornaments, and the horse were sent back at this place;
the hero, without an attendant, entered the forest of austerities alone.'

body.text: asmin pradeśe bodhisattvo lubdhakasakāśāt kāśikairvastraiḥ kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇī grahāya pravrajitaḥ / asmin pradeśe bhārgaveṇāśrameṇopanimantritaḥ / asmin pradeśe bodhisattvo rājñā bimbisāreṇārdharājyenopanimantritaḥ / asmin pradeśe ārāḍodrakamabhigataḥ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: 'In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> exchanged his <s>Kāśi</s> (Benares) garments for ochre robes from a hunter and went forth [into the homeless life]. In this place, he was invited to stay at the hermitage of <s>Bhārgava</s>. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was offered half the kingdom by King <s>Bimbisāra</s>. In this place, he approached <s>Ārāḍa</s> and <s>Udraka</s>.' And he said:

children.translated_text: The sages named <s>Udraka</s> and <s>Ārāḍaka</s>, in this forest of austerities,
were surpassed by the noble-natured lord of men.

body.text: asmin pradeśe bodhisattvena ṣaḍvarṣāṇi duṣkaraṃ cīrṇaṃ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: 'In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practiced severe austerities for six years.' And he said:

children.translated_text: Having performed bitter austerities for six years, the great sage,

children.text: nāyaṃ mārgo hyabhijñāyā iti jñātvā samatyajat //
children.translated_text: knowing 'this is not the path to higher knowledge,' abandoned [that practice].

body.text: asmin pradeśe bodhisattvena nandāyā nandabalāyāśca grāmikaduhitroḥ sakāśāt ṣoḍaśaguṇitaṃ madhupāyasaṃ paribhuktaṃ /
body.translated_text: 'In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> consumed sixteen-fold sweetened milk-rice from <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the daughters of a village headman.'

body.text: āha ca /
body.translated_text: And he said:

children.text: asmin pradeśe nandāyā bhuktvā ca madhupāyasaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'In this place, having eaten the milk-rice of <s>Nandā</s>,
the great hero, the foremost of speakers, went to the <s>Bodhi</s> tree.'

body.text: asmin pradeśe bodhisattvaḥ kālikena nāgarājena bodhimūlamabhigacchan saṃstutaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going toward the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, was praised by the <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) king <s>Kālika</s>.'

body.text: āha ca /
body.translated_text: And he said:

children.translated_text: 'Praised by the serpent lord <s>Kālika</s>, the foremost of speakers,
set out by this path toward the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of enlightenment), seeking the immortal.'

body.text: atha rājā sthavirasya pādayornipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca
body.translated_text: Then the king, falling at the feet of the elder with joined hands, spoke:

children.translated_text: 'Might we see that lord of <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) by whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> was seen,
proceeding by this path, with the stride of a lordly elephant in rut?'

body.text: atha kāliko nāgarājaḥ sthavirasamīpe sthitvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca / sthavira kimājñāpayasīti / atha sthaviro rājānamuvāca / ayaṃ sa mahārāja kāliko nāgarājā yena bhagavān anena mārgeṇa bodhimūlaṃ nirgacchan saṃstutaḥ / atha rājā kṛtāñjaliḥ kalikaṃ nāgarājamuvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) king <s>Kālika</s>, standing near the Elder, spoke with joined palms: 'Elder, what do you command?' Then the Elder said to the king: 'This, great king, is <s>Kālika</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king, by whom the Blessed One was praised as he went forth by this path to the seat of awakening (<s>Bodhimūla</s>).' Then the king, with joined palms, spoke to <s>Kālika</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king:

children.translated_text: You have seen the Teacher, equal in complexion to blazing gold, incomparable to me, with a face like the autumn moon —

children.text: ākhyāhi me daśabalasya guṇaikadeśaṃ tatkīdṛśī vada hi śrīḥ sugate tadānīṃ //
children.translated_text: tell me even a fraction of the virtues of the One of Ten Powers (<s>Daśabala</s>); describe, what was the glory of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) at that time?

body.text: kālika uvāca / na śakyaṃ vāgbhiḥ saṃprakāśayitumapi tu saṃkṣepaṃ śṛṇu /
body.translated_text: <s>Kālika</s> said: 'It is not possible to fully express it in words, but hear it in brief:'

children.translated_text: Struck by the soles of his feet, the earth together with its mountains trembled with a sixfold quaking,
and the radiance of the <s>Sugata</s>'s moon-like splendor, surpassing the rays of the sun, was imperishable and enchanting in the world of men.

body.text: yāvad rājā caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya prakrāntaḥ / atha sthaviropagupto rājānaṃ bodhimūlamupanāmayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ karamabhiprasāryovāca / asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvena mahāmaitrīsahāyena sakalaṃ mārabalaṃ jitvānuttarā samyaksambodhirabhisambuddhā / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having established a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), departed. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having led the king to the <s>Bodhimūla</s> (the foot of the Bodhi tree), extending his right hand, said: 'At this place, great king, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with great loving-kindness (<s>Mahāmaitrī</s>) as his companion, having conquered the entire army of <s>Māra</s>, attained the supreme, perfect awakening (<s>Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' And he said:

children.text: iha munivṛṣabheṇa bodhimūle namucibalaṃ vikṛtaṃ nirastamāśu /
children.translated_text: Here, at the seat of awakening, by the bull among sages (<s>Munivṛṣabha</s>), the monstrous army of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) was swiftly dispelled,
and this deathless, sublime, supreme awakening (<s>Agrabodhi</s>) was attained by that incomparable one.

body.text: yāvad rājñā bodhau śatasahasraṃ dattaṃ / caityaṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpya rājā prakrāntaḥ / atha sthaviropagupto rājānamaśokamuvāca / asmin pradeśe bhagavān caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sakāśāc catvāri śailamayāni pātrāṇi grahāya ekapātramadhiyuktaṃ / asmin pradeśe trapuṣabhallikayorvaṇijorapi piṇḍapātraṃ pratigṛhītaṃ / asmin pradeśe bhagavān vārāṇasīmabhigacchan upagaṇenājīvikena saṃstutaḥ / yāvat sthaviro rājānam ṛṣipatanam upanīya dakṣiṇaṃ hastamabhiprasāryovāca / asmin pradeśe mahārāja bhagavatā triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ dhārmyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitaṃ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the king gave one hundred thousand at the <s>Bodhi</s> (tree). Having established a <s>caitya</s>, the king departed. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> said to King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'At this place, the Blessed One received four stone bowls from the four Great Kings (<s>Mahārāja</s>) and combined them into one bowl. At this place, he accepted alms-food from the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>. At this place, the Blessed One, on his way to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, was greeted by <s>Upaga</s>, an <s>Ājīvika</s> ascetic.' Then the Elder, having led the king to <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Deer Park), extending his right hand, said: 'At this place, great king, the Blessed One turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma), righteous and consisting of Dharma, with three turnings and twelve aspects.' And he said:

children.translated_text: The auspicious wheel made of <s>Dharma</s>, for turning back <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth),
was set in motion at this place by the Protector (<s>Nātha</s>), unsurpassed.

body.text: asmin pradeśe jaṭilasahasraṃ pravrājitaṃ / asmin pradeśe rājño bimbisārasya dharmaṃ deśitaṃ / rājñā ca bimbisāreṇa satyāni dṛṣṭāni
body.translated_text: At this place, one thousand <s>jaṭilas</s> (matted-hair ascetics) were ordained. At this place, the <s>Dharma</s> was taught to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>. And King <s>Bimbisāra</s> saw the Truths,

body.text: caturaśītibhiśca devatāsahasrair anekaiśca māgadhakair brāhmaṇagṛhapatisahasraiḥ / asmin pradeśe bhagavatā śakrasya devandrasya dharmo deśitaḥ / śakreṇa ca satyāni dṛṣṭāni caturaśītibhiśca devatāsahasraiḥ / asmin pradeśe mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ / asmin pradeśe bhagavān deveṣu trayāstriṃśeṣu varṣā uṣitvā māturjanayitryā dharmaṃ deśayitvā devagaṇaparivṛtaḥ avatīrṇaḥ / vistareṇa yāvat sthaviro rājānamaśokaṃ kuśinagarīmupanāmayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ karatalamabhiprasāryovāca / asmin pradeśe mahārāja bhagavān sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: along with eighty-four thousand deities and many thousands of <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders. At this place, the Blessed One taught the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods (<s>Devendra</s>). And <s>Śakra</s> saw the Truths, along with eighty-four thousand deities. At this place, the great miracle (<s>Mahāprātihārya</s>) was displayed. At this place, the Blessed One, having spent the rains retreat (<s>Varṣā</s>) among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods and having taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the mother who gave him birth, descended surrounded by hosts of gods. In detail: then the Elder led King <s>Aśoka</s> to <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, and extending his right palm, said: 'At this place, great king, the Blessed One, having completed the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, attained final passing (<s>Parinirvṛta</s>) in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder (<s>Nirupadhiśeṣa Nirvāṇadhātu</s>).' And he said:

children.translated_text: Having wisely disciplined the world with its gods, humans, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s> in the imperishable <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline),
his mind at peace due to the absence of beings yet to be trained, the supremely compassionate great sage (<s>Maharṣi</s>) attained final peace (<s>Śānti</s>).

body.text: śrutvā ca rājā mūrcchitaḥ patitaḥ / yāvaj jalapariṣekaṃ kṛtvotthāpitaḥ / atha rājā kathaṃcit saṃjñāmupalabhya parinirvāṇe śatasahasraṃ dattvā caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya pādayornipatyovāca / sthavira ayaṃ me manoratho ye ca bhagavatā śrāvakā agratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭāsteṣāṃ śarīrapūjāṃ kariṣyāmīti / sthavira uvāca / sādhu sādhu mahārāja / śobhanaste cittotpādaḥ / sthaviro rājānamaśokaṃ jetavanaṃ praveśayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ karamabhiprasāryovāca / ayaṃ mahārāja sthaviraśāriputrasya stūpaḥ / kriyatāmasyārcanamiti / rājāha / ke tasya guṇā babhūvuḥ / sthavira uvāca / sa hi dvitīyaśāstā dharmasenādhipatirdharmacakrapravartanaḥ prajñāvatāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the king fainted and fell. He was revived by sprinkling water upon him. Then the king, having somehow regained consciousness, gave one hundred thousand at the site of the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), established a <s>caitya</s>, fell at his feet, and said: 'Elder, this is my heart's desire — I wish to perform worship of the relics (<s>Śarīrapūjā</s>) of those disciples whom the Blessed One designated as foremost.' The Elder said: 'Excellent, excellent, great king! Noble is your intention (<s>cittotpāda</s>).' The Elder, having led King <s>Aśoka</s> into <s>Jetavana</s>, extending his right hand, said: 'This, great king, is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s>. Let worship be performed for him.' The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The Elder said: 'He was a second Teacher, the commander of the army of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmasenādhipati</s>), the one who turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, designated by the Blessed One as foremost among those endowed with wisdom (<s>Prajñā</s>).'

children.translated_text: All the wisdom of the entire world, setting aside the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
does not equal even a sixteenth part of the wisdom of <s>Śāriputra</s>.

body.text: āha ca /
body.translated_text: And he said:

children.translated_text: The incomparable wheel of the True <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Saddharma</s>) that was set in motion by the Victor (<s>Jina</s>),

children.text: anuvṛttaṃ hi tat tena śāriputreṇa dhīmatā //
children.translated_text: was kept turning by the wise <s>Śāriputra</s>.
Who, other than the <s>Buddha</s>, is the man capable of speaking the praises of <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>)?
Knowing him to be a treasury of virtues, who could describe them in their entirety?

body.text:
tato rājā prītamanāḥ sthaviraśāradvatīputrastūpe śatasahasraṃ dattvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca /
śāradvatīputramahaṃ bhakttyā vande vimuktabhavasaṅgaṃ / lokaprakāśakirtiṃ jñānavatāmuttamaṃ vīraṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the king, with a delighted heart, having given one hundred thousand at the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>), spoke with joined palms: 'I devotedly pay homage to <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, who is freed from attachment to existence (<s>Bhavasaṅga</s>), whose fame illuminates the world, the supreme hero among the wise.'

body.text: yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthaviramahāmaudgalyāyanasya stūpamupadarśayannuvāca / ayaṃ mahārāja sthaviramahāmaudgalyāyanasya stūpaḥ / kriyatāmasyārcanamiti / rajāha / ketasya guṇā babhūvuriti / sthavira uvāca / sa hi ṛddhimatāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā yena dakṣiṇena pādāṅaguṣṭhena śakrasya devendrasya vaijayantaḥ prāsādaḥ prakampito nandopanandau nāgarājānau vinītau / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, showing the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said: 'This, great king, is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Let worship be performed for him.' The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The Elder said: 'He was designated by the Blessed One as foremost among those endowed with supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>). With the big toe of his right foot, he made <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods' (<s>Devendra</s>) palace <s>Vaijayanta</s> tremble, and he tamed the <s>Nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>.' And he said:

children.translated_text: He by whom <s>Śakra</s>'s palace was made to tremble with the big toe of his foot —
<s>Kolita</s> (<s>Maudgalyāyana</s>), that best of the twice-born, should be worshipped with diligence.
The two fearsome lords of serpents, exceedingly difficult to tame in this world, were tamed by him —
who could reach the far shore of the ocean of virtues of that one of pure understanding?

body.text: yāvad rājā mahāmaudgalyāyanasya stūpe śatasahasraṃ dattvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having given one hundred thousand at the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, spoke with joined palms:

children.translated_text: He who is foremost among those endowed with supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>), freed from birth, old age, grief, and suffering —
I pay homage to the renowned <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, bowing my head in reverence.

body.text: yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthaviramahākāśyapasya stūpam upadarśayannuvāca / ayaṃ mahārāja sthaviramahākāśyapasya stūpaḥ / kriyatāmasyārcanamiti / rājāha / ke tasya guṇā babhūvuḥ / sthavirovāca / sa hi mahātmāpecchānnāṃ santuṣṭānāṃ dhūpaguṇavādināmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā, ardhāsanenopanimantritaḥ śvetacīvareṇācchādito dīnāturagrāhakaḥ śāsanasaṃdharakaśceti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, showing the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, said: 'This, great king, is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>. Let worship be performed for him.' The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The Elder said: 'That great soul was designated by the Blessed One as foremost among those who are content with few desires, who are satisfied, and who speak in praise of ascetic qualities (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>). He was invited to share half the seat, covered with the white robe, one who takes in the destitute and afflicted, and the upholder of the Teaching (<s>Śāsana</s>).' And he said:

children.translated_text: A sublime field of merit (<s>Puṇyakṣetra</s>), one who takes in the destitute and afflicted, effortless in practice,
bearer of the robe of the Omniscient One (<s>Sarvajña</s>), upholder of the Teaching, endowed with wisdom.

children.text: kastasya gurormanujo vaktuṃ śakto guṇān niravaśeṣān /
children.translated_text: What human could speak the complete virtues of that venerable one,
he of excellent understanding, to whom the Victor (<s>Jina</s>) gave half his seat?

body.text: tato rājāśokaḥ sthaviramahākāśyapasya stūpe śatasahasraṃ dattvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having given one hundred thousand at the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, spoke with joined palms:

children.translated_text: Having his dwelling in a mountain cave, facing death with equanimity, turned away from enmity, endowed with tranquility,
abounding in the virtues of contentment — I pay homage indeed to the Elder <s>Kāśyapa</s>.

body.text: yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthavirabatkulasya stūpaṃ darśayannuvāca / ayaṃ mahārāja sthavirabatkulasya stūpaḥ / kriyatāmarcanamiti / rājāha / ketasya guṇā babhūvuriti /
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, showing the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Bakkula</s>, said: 'This, great king, is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Bakkula</s>. Let worship be performed for him.' The king said: 'What were his virtues?'

body.text: sthavira uvāca / sa mahātmālpabādhānām agro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā / api ca na tena kasyacid dvipadikā gāthā śrāvitā / rājāha / dīyatāmatra kākaṇiḥ / yāvadamātyairabhihitaḥ / deva kimarthaṃ tulyeṣvavasthiteṣvatra kākaṇī dīyata iti / rājāha / śrūyatāmatrābhiprāyo mama /
body.translated_text: The Elder said: 'That great soul was designated by the Blessed One as foremost among those with few ailments. Moreover, he never taught even a couplet (<s>gāthā</s>) to anyone.' The king said: 'Give a single <s>kākaṇī</s> (small coin) here.' Then the ministers said: 'Your Majesty, why is only a <s>kākaṇī</s> given here when they are of equal standing?' The king said: 'Hear my reason for this:'

children.text: ājñāpradīpena mahogṛhasthaṃ hṛtaṃ tamo yadyapi tena kṛtsnaṃ /
children.translated_text: Although by the lamp of his wisdom (<s>ājñā</s>), the entire darkness of the house of existence was removed by him,

children.text: alpecchabhāvānna kṛtaṃ hi tena yathā kṛtaṃ sattvahitaṃ tadanyaiḥ //
children.translated_text: due to his nature of desiring little (<s>alpeccha</s>), he did not accomplish the welfare of beings as others did.

body.text: sā pratyāhatā tasyaiva rājñaḥ pādamūle nipatitā / yāvad amātyā vismitā ūcuḥ / aho tasya mahātmano 'lpecchatā / babhūvānayāpyanarthī /
body.translated_text: That <s>kākaṇī</s>, rejected, fell back at the feet of the king himself. Then the ministers, astonished, said: 'Oh, how great is the contentment of that great soul! Even by this small offering he was not pleased.'

body.text: yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthavirānandasya stūpamupadarśayannuvāca / ayaṃ sthavirānandasya stūpaḥ / kriyatāmasyārcanamiti / rājāha / ke tasya guṇā babhūvuriti / sthavira uvāca / sa hi bhagavata upasthāyako babhūva / bahuśrutānāmagryo pravacanagrāhakaśceti / āha ca /

children.translated_text: Skilled in guarding the bowl of the Sage (<s>Muni</s>), firm in mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), retention (<s>dhṛti</s>), and intellect (<s>mati</s>), an ocean of learning (<s>śruta</s>),
with clear and sweet speech, honored by gods and humans — ever-joyful <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, showing the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, said: 'This is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>. Let worship be performed for him.' The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The Elder said: 'He was the personal attendant (<s>Upasthāyaka</s>) of the Blessed One, foremost among the learned (<s>Bahuśruta</s>), and the preserver of the sacred word (<s>Pravacana</s>).' And he said:

children.translated_text: Skilled in understanding the mind of the Fully Awakened One, discerning in all things, a casket of virtues,
praised by the Victor (<s>Jina</s>), victorious in battle, honored by gods and humans — ever-joyful <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.text: yāvad rājñā tasya stūpe koṭirdattā / yāvad amātyairabhihitaḥ / kimarthamayaṃ deva sarveṣāṃ sakāśādadhikataraṃ pūjyate /
body.translated_text: Then the king gave a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) at his <s>stūpa</s>. The ministers said: 'Why, Your Majesty, is this one honored more than all the others?'

body.text: rājāha / śrūyatāmabhiprāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Hear my reason:'

children.text: yattaccharīraṃ vadatāṃ varasya dharmātmano dharmamayaṃ viśuddhaṃ /
children.translated_text: The body of the best of speakers, the righteous one, pure and composed of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: tad dhāritaṃ tena viśokanāmnā tasmād viśeṣeṇa sa pūjanīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: was preserved by that one named <s>Viśoka</s> (<s>Ānanda</s>, 'the Sorrowless') — therefore he is especially worthy of worship.
That the lamp of <s>Dharma</s> blazes among the people today, destroying the darkness of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) —

children.text: tat tatprabhāvāt sugatendrasūnostasmād viśeṣeṇa sa pūjanīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: that is through the power of the son of the Lord of the <s>Sugatas</s> — therefore he is especially worthy of worship.

children.text: yathā sāmudraṃ salilaṃ samudrairdhāryeta kaccin na hi goṣpadena /
children.translated_text: Just as the water of the ocean can be held by oceans, but certainly not by a cow's hoofprint,
so, perceiving this nature of the <s>Dharma</s>, the Protector (<s>Nātha</s>) consecrated this Elder as the keeper of the <s>Sūtras</s> (<s>Sūtrāntaka</s>).

body.text: atha rājā sthavirāṇāṃ stūpārcanaṃ kṛtvā sthaviropaguptasya pādayornipatya prītimanā uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having performed worship at the <s>stūpas</s> of the Elders and falling at the feet of the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, spoke with a delighted heart:

children.translated_text: Human birth has been made fruitful — that which is obtained through hundreds of auspicious seasons —
from sovereignty, royal glory, and transient splendors, the supreme essence has been grasped.
