This world has been adorned with hundreds of <s>caityas</s> radiant as peaks of white clouds,

children.text: asyādyāpratimasya śāsanakṛte kiṃ no kṛtaṃ duṣkaraṃ //
children.translated_text: for the sake of the Teaching of this incomparable one — what difficult deed has not been accomplished by us?

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: yāvad rājā sthaviropaguptasya praṇāmaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having paid homage to the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, departed.

body.text: yāvad rājñāśokena jātau bodhau dharkacakre parinirvāṇe ekaikaśatasahasraṃ dattaṃ / tasya bodhau viśeṣataḥ prasādo jāta iha bhagavatānuttarā samyaksambodhirabhisambuddheti / sa yāni viśeṣayuktāni ratnāni tāni bodhiṃ preṣayati /
body.translated_text: King <s>Aśoka</s> gave one hundred thousand each at the place of birth, the <s>Bodhi</s> (tree), the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (first turning of the wheel), and the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing). His devotion was especially aroused at the <s>Bodhi</s> (tree), thinking: 'Here the Blessed One attained the supreme, perfect awakening (<s>Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' He sent his most precious jewels to the <s>Bodhi</s> (tree).

body.text: atha rājño 'śokasya tiṣyarakṣitā nāmāgramahiṣī / tasyā buddhirutpannā / ayaṃ rājā mayā sārdhaṃ ratimanubhavati viśeṣayuktāni ca ratnāni bodhau preṣayati / tayā mātaṅgī vyāharitā / śakyasi tvaṃ bodhiṃ mama sapatnīṃ praghātayituṃ / tayābhihitaṃ / śakṣyāmi kintu kārṣāpaṇān dehīti /
body.translated_text: Now King <s>Aśoka</s> had a chief queen named <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>. She thought: 'This king enjoys pleasures with me, yet sends his most precious jewels to the <s>Bodhi</s> (tree).' She summoned a <s>Mātaṅgī</s> (outcaste sorceress) and said: 'Can you destroy the <s>Bodhi</s> (tree), my rival?' She replied: 'I can, but give me <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins).'

body.text: yāvan mātaṅgyā bodhivṛkṣo mantraiḥ parijaptaḥ sūtraṃ ca baddhaṃ / yāvad bodhivṛkṣaḥ śoṣṭumārabdhaḥ / tato rājapuruṣai rājñe niveditaṃ / deva bodhivṛkṣa śuṣyata iti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Mātaṅgī</s> enchanted the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with spells and tied a cord around it. The <s>Bodhi</s> tree began to wither. Then the king's men reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, the <s>Bodhi</s> tree is withering.' And he said:

children.translated_text: Where the <s>Tathāgata</s> sat and duly awakened this entire world —

children.text: sarvajñatā cādhigatā narendra bodhidrumo 'sau nidhanaṃ prayāti //
children.translated_text: Omniscience was attained, O king, and that <s>Bodhi</s> tree is perishing.

body.text:
śrutvā ca rājā murcchito bhūmau patitaḥ / yāvaj jalasekaṃ dattvā utthāpitaḥ / atha rājā kathaṃcit saṃjñāmupalabhya prarudannuvāca /
dṛṣṭvā nvahaṃ taṃ drumarājamūlaṃ jānāmi dṛṣṭo 'dya mayā svayambhūḥ /
nāthadrūme caiva gate praṇāśaṃ prāṇāḥ prayāsyanti mamāpi nāśaṃ /
body.translated_text: Upon hearing this, the king fainted and fell to the ground. They revived him by sprinkling water. Then the king, having somehow regained consciousness, spoke while weeping: "Having seen the root of that king of trees, I know that I have today beheld the <s>Svayambhū</s> (Self-existent One) himself. Now that the tree of the Protector has gone to destruction, my very life-breaths too shall perish."

body.text: atha tiṣyarakṣitā rājānaṃ śokārtamavekṣyovāca / deva, yadi bodhirna bhaviṣyatyahaṃ devasya ratimutpādayiṣyāmi / rājāha / na sā strī api tu bodhivṛkṣaḥ / sa yatra bhagavatānuttarā samyaksambodhiradhigata / tiṣyarakṣitā mātaṅgīmuvāca / śakyasi tvaṃ bodhivṛkṣaṃ yathāpaurāṇamavasthāpayituṃ / mātaṅgī āha / yadi tāvat prāṇaṇukamavaśiṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati, yathāpaurāṇamavasthāpayiṣyāmīti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, seeing the king afflicted with grief, said: "Lord, if the <s>Bodhi</s> tree shall cease to exist, I will produce delight for the lord." The king said: "That is not a woman but the <s>Bodhi</s> tree — the place where the <s>Bhagavān</s> attained supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>)." <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> said to the <s>Mātaṅgī</s> woman: "Are you able to restore the <s>Bodhi</s> tree to its former state?" The <s>Mātaṅgī</s> said: "If even a small portion of its life-root remains, I shall restore it to its former state."

body.text: vistareṇa yāvat tayā sūtraṃ muktvā vṛkṣaṃ sāmantena khanitvā divase kṣīrakumbhasahasreṇa pāyayati / yāvadalpairahobhiryathāpaurāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / tato rājapuruṣai rājñe niveditaṃ / deva, diṣṭyā vardhasva / yathāpaurāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / śrutvā ca prītimanā bodhivṛkṣaṃ nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca /
body.translated_text: In detail — she released a thread around it, dug around the tree on all sides, and watered it daily with a thousand pots of milk. Within a few days it was restored to its former state. Then the king's men informed the king: "Lord, rejoice! It has been restored to its former state." Upon hearing this, the king, delighted in mind, gazing at the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, said:

children.translated_text: That which was not done by kings beginning with <s>Bimbisāra</s>, those splendid lords of the earth —
that I shall do: a twofold supreme offering.
I shall bathe the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with pots filled with fragrant water,
and I shall make an offering to the <s>Saṅgha</s> at a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival).

body.text: atha rājā sauvarṇarūpyavaiḍūryasphaṭikamayānāṃ kumbhānāṃ sahasraṃ gandhodakena pūrayitvā prabhūtaṃ cānnapānaṃ samudānīya gandhamālyapuṣpasañcayaṃ kṛtvā snātvāhatāni vāsāṃsi navāni dīrghadaśāni prāvṛtyāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatamupavāsamupoṣya dhūpakaṭacchukamādāya śaraṇatalamabhiruhya
body.translated_text: Then the king, having filled a thousand pots made of gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), and crystal with fragrant water, and having gathered abundant food and drink, and having prepared heaps of incense, garlands, and flowers, and having bathed and put on fresh, new garments with long fringes, and having observed the fast endowed with eight factors (<s>aṣṭāṅga-upavāsa</s>), and taking up an incense ladle, and ascending to the terrace of the shelter,

body.text: caturdiśamāyācitumārabdhaḥ / ye bhagavato buddhasya śrāvakāste mamānugrahāyāgacchantu /
body.translated_text: he began to invoke the four directions: "May those who are disciples of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s> come for my benefit!"

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: And further:

children.text: samyaggatā ye sugatasya śiṣyāḥ śāntendriyā nirjitakāmadoṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those disciples of the <s>Sugata</s> who have gone rightly, whose senses are calmed, who have conquered desire and fault —
worthy of honor, revered by kings among men — may they come here out of compassion for me.
Those who delight in tranquility and self-control, free from attachment, the excellent sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, kings of the <s>Dharma</s>,
whose noble conduct is honored by <s>asuras</s>, gods, and men — may they come here out of kindness toward me.

children.text: vasanti kāśmīrapure suramye ye cāpi dhīrāstamasovane 'smin /
children.translated_text: Those steadfast ones who dwell in the lovely city of <s>Kāśmīra</s> and in this <s>Tamasa</s> forest,

children.text: mahāvane revatake ya āryā anugrahārthaṃ mama te 'bhyupeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: the noble ones in <s>Mahāvana</s> and <s>Revataka</s> — may they come for my benefit.

children.text: anavataptahrade nivasanti ye girinadīṣu ca parvatakandareḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who dwell at <s>Anavatapta</s> lake, in mountain rivers and in mountain caves,

children.text: jinasutāḥ khalu dhyānaratāḥ sadā samudayantviha te 'dya kṛpābalāḥ //
children.translated_text: sons of the <s>Jina</s>, ever delighting in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) — may they assemble here today, moved by the power of compassion.

children.text: śaīrīṣake ye pravare vimāne vasanti putrā vadatāṃ varasya /
children.translated_text: Those sons of the Best of Speakers who dwell in the excellent <s>Śairīṣaka</s> mansion,

children.text: anugrahārthaṃ mama te viśokā hyāyāntu kāruṇyaniviṣṭabhāvāḥ //
children.translated_text: free from sorrow — may they come for my benefit, their hearts imbued with compassion.
And those of great splendor who dwell on <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain —
may they come here, having aroused compassion, being invited.

body.text: evamukte ca rājñi trīṇi śatasahasrāṇi bhikṣūṇāṃ saṃnipatitāni / tatraikaṃ śatasahasramarhatāṃ dve śaikṣāṇāṃ pṛthagjanakalyāṇakānāṃ ca / na kaścid vṛddhāsanamākramyate sma / rājāha / kimarthaṃ vṛddhāsanaṃ tan nākramyate / tatra yaśo nāmnā vṛddhaḥ ṣaḍabhijñaḥ / sa uvāca / mahārāja vṛddhasya tadāsanamiti / rājāha / asti sthavira tvatsakāśādanyo vṛddhatara iti / sthavira uvāca / asti mahārāja / vadatāṃ vareṇa vaśinā nirdiṣṭaḥ siṃhanādināmagryaḥ / piṇḍolabharadvājasyaitad agrāsanaṃ nṛpate /
body.translated_text: When the king had spoken thus, three hundred thousand monks assembled. Of these, one hundred thousand were <s>arhats</s>, two hundred thousand were learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and virtuous ordinary persons. No one ascended the elder's seat. The king asked: "Why is that elder's seat not occupied?" There an elder named <s>Yaśas</s>, possessed of the six supernatural knowledges (<s>ṣaḍabhijña</s>), said: "Great king, that is the seat of an elder." The king asked: "Elder, is there one older than you?" The elder said: "There is, great king. Designated by the Best of Speakers, the Conqueror, as foremost among those who make the lion's roar — this is the chief seat of <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, O king."

body.text: atha rājā kadambapuṣpavadāhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ kathayati / asti kaścid buddhadarśī bhikṣurghriyata iti /
body.translated_text: Then the king, his hair standing on end like <s>kadamba</s> flowers, asked: "Is there any monk who has seen the <s>Buddha</s> still living?"

body.text: sthavira uvāca / asti mahāraja piṇḍolabharadvājo nāmnā buddhadarśī tiṣṭhata iti /
body.translated_text: The elder said: "There is, great king — one named <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s> who has seen the <s>Buddha</s>. He still abides."

body.text: rājā kathayati / sthavira, śakyaḥ so 'smābhirdṛṣṭimiti / sthavira uvāca / mahārāja idānīṃ drakṣyasi / ayaṃ tasya āgamanakāla iti / atha rājā prītimānā uvāca /

children.text: lābhaḥ paraḥ syād atulo mameha mahāsukhaścāyamanuttamaśca /
children.translated_text: "This would be my supreme, incomparable, and most excellent great fortune —
that I should see that noble being of generous nature, <s>Bhāradvāja</s> by clan name, in person."

body.translated_text: The king asked: "Elder, is it possible for us to see him?" The elder said: "Great king, you shall see him now. This is the time of his coming." Then the king, filled with joy, said:

body.text: tato rājā kṛtakarapuṭo gaganatalāvasaktadṛṣṭiravasthitaḥ / atha sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvājo 'nekairarhatsahasrairardhacandrākāreṇopagūḍho rājahaṃsa
body.translated_text: Then the king stood with palms joined, his gaze fixed upon the sky. Then the elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, surrounded by many thousands of <s>arhats</s> in a crescent formation, like a royal swan,

body.text: iva gaganatalādavatīrya vṛddhānte niṣasād / sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvājaṃ dṛṣṭvā tānyanekāni bhikṣuśatasahasrāṇi pratyupasthitāni /
body.translated_text: descended from the sky and sat upon the elder's seat. Upon seeing the elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, those many hundreds of thousands of monks stood up in attendance.

body.text: adrākṣīd rājā piṇḍolabharadvājaṃ śvetapalitaśirasaṃ pralambubhrūlalāṭaṃ nigūḍhākṣitārakaṃ pratyekabuddhāśrayaṃ / dṛṣṭvā ca rājā mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvājasya pādayoḥ patitaḥ / mukhatuṇḍakena ca pādāvanuparimārjyotthāya tau jānumaṇḍalau pṛthivītale pratiṣṭhāpya kṛtāñjaliḥ sthavirapīṇḍolabharadvājaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ prarudannuvāca /
body.translated_text: The king saw <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s> — his head white with grey hair, his brows hanging long over his forehead, his pupils hidden deep within, bearing the appearance of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Having seen him, the king, like a tree cut at the root, fell with his whole body at the feet of the elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>. Wiping the elder's feet with the tip of his face, he rose, placed both knees on the ground, and with palms joined, gazing at the elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, spoke while weeping:

children.text: yadā mayā śatrugaṇān nihatya prāptā samudrābharaṇā saśailā /
children.translated_text: "When, having slain hosts of enemies, the earth girdled by oceans, with its mountains, was won by me,

children.text: ekātapatrā pṛthivī tadā me prītīrna sā yā sthaviraṃ nirīkṣya //
children.translated_text: under a single parasol — that joy was not equal to what I feel upon beholding the elder."

body.text: tvaddarśanād bhavati dṛṣṭo 'dya tathāgataḥ / karuṇālābhāt tvaddarśanācca dviguṇaprasādo mamotpannaḥ / api ca sthavira dṛṣṭaste trailokyanātho gururme bhagavān buddha iti / tataḥ sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvāja ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ bhruvamunnāmya rājānamaśokaṃ nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca /
body.translated_text: "By seeing you, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is as if seen today. From the gain of compassion and from seeing you, a twofold faith has arisen in me. Moreover, elder, did you see the Lord of the Three Worlds, my teacher, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>?" Then the elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, lifting his brows with both hands, gazing at King <s>Aśoka</s>, said:

body.text:
dṛṣṭo mayā hyasakṛdapratimo maharṣiḥ / santaptakāñcanasamopamatulyatejaḥ /
dvātriṃśalakṣaṇadharaḥ śaradinduvaktro brāhmasvarādhikaraṇo hyaraṇāvihārī //
body.translated_text: "I have seen, not just once, that incomparable great sage, whose splendor was like that of heated gold, bearing the thirty-two marks (<s>dvātriṃśat-lakṣaṇa</s>), whose face was like an autumn moon, whose voice was that of <s>Brahmā</s>, and who dwelt in the forest."

body.text: rājāha / sthavira kutra te bhagavān dṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃ ceti / sthavira uvāca / yadā mahārāja bhagavān vijitamāraparivāraḥ pañcabhirarhacchataiḥ sārdhaṃ prathamato rājagṛhe varṣāmuṣito 'haṃ tatkālaṃ tatraivāsam / mayā sa dakṣiṇīyaḥ samyag dṛṣṭa iti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: The king asked: "Elder, where and how did you see the <s>Bhagavān</s>?" The elder said: "When, great king, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having conquered <s>Māra</s> and his retinue, spent the first rainy season in <s>Rājagṛha</s> together with five hundred <s>arhats</s>, I was there at that time. I saw that worthy one properly." And he said:

children.translated_text: "Surrounded by those free from passion, the great sage himself free from passion,

children.text: yadā rājagṛhe varṣā uṣitaḥ sa tathāgataḥ //
children.translated_text: when the <s>Tathāgata</s> spent the rains at <s>Rājagṛha</s> —
at that time I was there, in the presence of the Fully Awakened One.

children.text: yatha paśyasi māṃ sākṣādevaṃ dṛṣṭo mayā muniḥ //
children.translated_text: Just as you see me before you, so did I see the Sage."

body.text: yadāpi mahārāja bhagavatā śrāvastyāṃ tīrthyān vijayārthaṃ mahāprātihārya kṛtaṃ buddhāvataṃsakaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanaṃ nirmitaṃ mahat tatkālaṃ tatraivāhamāsam / mayā tad buddhavikrīḍitaṃ duṣtamiti /
body.translated_text: "And when, great king, the <s>Bhagavān</s> performed the great miracle at <s>Śrāvastī</s> to defeat the heretics — the <s>buddhāvataṃsaka</s> (garland of Buddhas) manifested up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven, a magnificent display — I was there at that time. That sport of the <s>Buddha</s> was seen by me."

body.text: āha ca /
body.translated_text: And he said:

children.text: tīrthyā yadā bhagavatā kupathaprayātā ṛddhiprabhāvavidhinā khalu nirgṛhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: "When the heretics who had gone on a wrong path were subdued by the <s>Bhagavān</s> through the method of supernatural power and might,

children.text: vikrīḍītaṃ daśabalasya tadā hyudāraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ mayā tu nṛpa harṣakaraṃ prajānāṃ //
children.translated_text: that magnificent sport of the Possessor of the Ten Powers (<s>Daśabala</s>), delighting the people, was seen by me, O king."

body.text: yadāpi mahārāja bhagavatā deveṣu trayastriṃśeṣu varṣā uṣitvā māturjanayitryā dharmaṃ deśayitvā devagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sāṃkāśye nagare 'vatīrṇo 'haṃ tatkālaṃ tatraivāsam / mayā sā devamanuṣyasaṃpadā dṛṣṭā utpalavarṇayā ca nirmitā cakravartisaṃpadā iti /
body.translated_text: "And when, great king, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having spent the rains among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and having taught the <s>Dharma</s> to his mother who bore him, descended at the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s> surrounded by hosts of gods — I was there at that time. I saw that splendor of gods and men, and also the manifestation of the majesty of a <s>Cakravartin</s> created by <s>Utpalavarṇā</s>."

children.text: yadāvatīrṇo vadatāṃ variṣṭho varṣāmuṣitvā khalu devaloke /
children.translated_text: "When the Best of Speakers descended, having spent the rains in the world of the gods,

children.text: tatrāpyahaṃ sannihito babhūva dṛṣṭo mayāsau muniragrasattvaḥ //
children.translated_text: there too I was present — I saw that Sage, the foremost of beings."

body.text: yadā mahārāja sumāgadhayā anāthapiṇḍaduhitrā upanimantritaḥ pañcabhirarhacchataiḥ sārdhamṛddhyā puṇḍavardhanaṃ gatastadāhaṃ ṛddhyā parvataśailaṃ grahāya gaganatalamākramya puṇḍavardhanaṃ gataḥ / tvannimittaṃ ca me bhagavatājñā kṣiptā / na tāvatte parinirvātavyaṃ yāvaddharmo nāntarhita iti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: "When, great king, <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, invited him, and he went by supernatural power to <s>Puṇḍavardhana</s> together with five hundred <s>arhats</s> — then I, seizing a mountain peak by supernatural power, traversed the sky and went to <s>Puṇḍavardhana</s>. And for your sake the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave me a command: 'You shall not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> until the <s>Dharma</s> has not disappeared.'" And he said:

children.translated_text: "When the Leader, the Teacher, went by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), invited by <s>Sumāgadhā</s>,

children.text: tadā gṛhītvarddhibalena parvataṃ jagāma tūrṇaṃ khalu puṇḍavardhanaṃ //
children.translated_text: then, having seized a mountain by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s>, I swiftly went to <s>Puṇḍavardhana</s>.

children.text: ājñā tadā śākyakuloditena dattā ca me kāruṇikena tena /
children.translated_text: A command was then given to me by the One born of the <s>Śākya</s> lineage, that compassionate one:

children.text: tāvannate nirvṛtirabhyupeyā antarhito yāvadayaṃ na dharmaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirvṛti</s> (final release) shall not come to you until this <s>Dharma</s> has not disappeared.'"

body.text: yadāpi mahārāja tvayā pūrvaṃ bālabhāvād bhagavato rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭasya saktuṃ dāsyāmīti pāṃśvañjalirbhagavataḥ pātre prakṣipto rādhaguptena cānumoditaṃ tvaṃ ca bhagavatā nirdiṣṭo 'yaṃ dārako varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mama pāṭaliputre nagare 'śoko nāma rājā bhaviṣyati caturbhāgacakravartī dhārmiko dharmarājā yo me śarīradhātukaṃ vaistārikaṃ kariṣyati caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyatyahaṃ tatkālaṃ tatraivāsam / āha ca /
body.translated_text: "And when, great king, you formerly in your childhood, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms, threw a handful of dirt into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s bowl saying 'I will give barley-meal,' and <s>Rādhagupta</s> rejoiced in it, and you were prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This boy, a hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, shall become a king named <s>Aśoka</s>, a sovereign of a fourth part, righteous, a <s>Dharmarāja</s>, who shall make a vast distribution of my bodily relics and shall establish eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> stūpas' — I was there at that time." And he said:

children.translated_text: "When a handful of dirt was given by you into the vessel of the <s>Buddha</s>,
having made an offering in childish faith — I was right there at that time."

body.text: rājāha / sthavira / kutredānīmuṣyata iti / sthavira uvāca /
body.translated_text: The king asked: "Elder, where do you dwell now?" The elder said:

children.translated_text: "North of <s>Sararāja</s> (Lake <s>Anavatapta</s>), on <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain,
I dwell there, O king, together with my fellow practitioners of the holy life."

body.text: rājāha / kiyantaḥ sthavirasya parivārāḥ / sthavira uvāca /
body.translated_text: The king asked: "How many are in the elder's retinue?" The elder said:

children.translated_text: "Sixty thousand <s>arhats</s> form my retinue, O best of men,
with whom I dwell — desireless ones who have conquered all defilements."

body.text: api ca mahārāja kimanena sandehena kṛtena / pariviṣyatāṃ bhikṣusaṅghaḥ / bhuktavato bhikṣusaṅghasya pratisaṃmodanaṃ kariṣyāmi / rājāha / evamastu yathā sthavira ājñāpayati / kintu buddhasmṛtipratibodhito 'haṃ bodhisnapanaṃ tāvat kariṣyāmi / samanantaraṃ ca manāpena cāhāreṇa bhikṣusaṅghamupasthāsyāmīti /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, great king, what is the use of this deliberation? Let the <s>Bhikṣu-saṅgha</s> be served food. After the <s>Bhikṣu-saṅgha</s> has eaten, I shall give the concluding benediction." The king said: "So be it, as the elder commands. But first, awakened by the remembrance of the <s>Buddha</s>, I shall perform the bathing of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree. Immediately after, I shall serve the <s>Bhikṣu-saṅgha</s> with agreeable food."

body.text: atha rājā sarvamitram udghoṣakamāmantrayati / aham āryasaṅghasya śatasahasraṃ dāsyāmi / kumbhasahasreṇa ca bodhiṃ snāpayiṣyāmi / mama nāmnā ghuṣyatāṃ pañcavārṣikamiti /
body.translated_text: Then the king addressed <s>Sarvamitra</s>, the herald: "I shall give a hundred thousand to the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>. I shall bathe the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with a thousand pots. Let the <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival) be proclaimed in my name."

body.text: tatkālaṃ ca kunālasya nayanadvayamavipannamāsīt / sa rājño dakṣiṇe pārśve sthitaḥ / tenāṃgulidvayamutkṣiptaṃ na tu vāg bhāṣitā / dviguṇaṃ tvahaṃ pradāsyāmītyākārayati / pāṇau vardhitamātre ca kunālena sarvajanakāyena hāsyaṃ muktaṃ /
body.translated_text: At that time, both eyes of <s>Kunāla</s> were intact. He stood at the king's right side. He raised two fingers but did not speak a word — indicating "I shall give double." When <s>Kunāla</s> raised the bid, the entire assembly burst into laughter.

body.text: tato rājā hāsyaṃ muktvā kathayati / aho rādhagupta kenaitad vardhitamiti /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having laughed, said: "O <s>Rādhagupta</s>, by whom was this bid raised?"

body.text: rādhaguptaḥ kathayati / deva bahavaḥ puṇyārthinaḥ prāṇino yaḥ puṇyārthī tena vardhitamiti /
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhagupta</s> said: "Lord, many beings seek merit. Whoever seeks merit has raised the bid."

body.text: rājāha / śatasahasratrayaṃ dāsyāmītyāryasaṅghe / kumbhasahasreṇa ca bodhiṃ snapayiṣyāmi / mama nāmnā ghuṣyatāṃ pañcavārṣikamiti /
body.translated_text: The king said: "I shall give three hundred thousand to the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>. I shall bathe the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with a thousand pots. Let the <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival) be proclaimed in my name."

body.text: yāvat kunālena catasro 'ṅagulaya utkṣiptā / tato rājā rūṣito rādhaguptamuvāca / aho rādhagupta ko 'yamasmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ pratidvandvayati alokajñaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s> raised four fingers. The king, angered, said to <s>Rādhagupta</s>: 'O <s>Rādhagupta</s>, who is this ignorant one who rivals me?'

body.text: ruṣitaṃ ca rājānamavekṣya rādhagupto rājñaḥ pādayornipatyovāca / deva kasya śaktirnarendreṇa sārdhaṃ vispardhituṃ bhavet / kunālo guṇavān pitrā sārdhaṃ vikurute / atha rājā dakṣiṇena parivṛtya kunālamavalokyovāca / sthavira ahaṃ kośaṃ sthāpayitvā rājyamantaḥpuramamātyagaṇamātmānaṃ ca kunālaṃ cāryasaṅghe niryātayāmi / suvarṇarūpyasphaṭikavaiḍūryamayaiḥ pañcakumbhasahasrairnānāgandhapūrṇaiḥ kṣīracandanakuṃkumakarpūravāsitairmahābodhiṃ snapayiṣyāmi / puṣpaśatasahasrāṇi ca bodhipramukhe cāryasaṅghe dadāmi / mama nāmnā ghuṣyatāṃ pañcavārṣikamiti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Seeing the king angered, <s>Rādhagupta</s> fell at the king's feet and said: 'Your Majesty, who has the power to compete with a sovereign? <s>Kunāla</s> is virtuous — he is merely playing with his father.' Then the king, turning to the right, looked at <s>Kunāla</s> and said: 'Elder, setting aside the treasury, I shall hand over the kingdom, the inner palace, the council of ministers, myself, and <s>Kunāla</s> to the Noble <s>Saṅgha</s>. With five thousand jars made of gold, silver, crystal, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), filled with various fragrances, scented with milk, sandalwood, saffron, and camphor, I shall bathe the <s>Mahābodhi</s> (Great Bodhi Tree). I shall give a hundred thousand flowers before the Bodhi Tree to the Noble <s>Saṅgha</s>. Let the <s>Pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival) be proclaimed in my name.' And he said:

children.text: rājyaṃ samṛddhaṃ hi saṃsthāpya kośamantaḥ purāmātyagaṇaṃ ca sarvaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having established the flourishing kingdom, the treasury, the inner palace, and the entire council of ministers,

children.text: dadāmi saṅghe guṇapātrabhūte ātmākunālaṃ ca guṇopapannaṃ //
children.translated_text: I give them to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, which is a vessel of virtues — myself and <s>Kunāla</s> too, who is endowed with virtues.

body.text: tato rājā piṇḍolabharadvājapramukhe bhikṣusaṅghe niryātayitvā bodhivṛkṣasya ca caturdiśaṃ vāraṃ baddhvā svayameva ca vāramabhiruhya caturbhiḥ kumbhasahasrai rbodhisnapanaṃ kṛtavān / kṛtamātre ca bodhisnapane bodhivṛkṣo yathāpaurāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having handed over [everything] to the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s> (community of monks) headed by <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, and having set up a barrier on all four sides of the Bodhi Tree, himself ascended the barrier and performed the bathing of the Bodhi Tree with four thousand jars. As soon as the bathing of the Bodhi Tree was completed, the Bodhi Tree became as it had been in ancient times. For it will be said:

children.translated_text: As soon as the supreme bathing of the Bodhi Tree was performed by the king,
the Bodhi Tree then became green-leaved and tender with new shoots.
Seeing it rich with green leaves, tender with new shoots and sprouts,
the king was overcome with joy, together with his council of ministers and the citizens.

body.text: atha rājā bodhisnapanaṃ kṛtvā bhikṣusaṅghaṃ pariveṣṭumārabdhaḥ / tatra yaśo nāmnā sthaviraḥ / tenābhihitaṃ / mahārāja mahānayaṃ paramadakṣiṇīya āryasaṅghaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ / tathā te pariveṣṭavyaṃ yathā tena kṣatirna syāditi /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having performed the bathing of the Bodhi Tree, began to serve food to the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>. There was an Elder named <s>Yaśas</s>. He said: 'Great King, this supremely worthy Noble <s>Saṅgha</s> has assembled in great numbers. You should serve them in such a way that no harm comes to any of them.'

body.text: tato rājā svahastena pariveṣayan yāvan navakāntaṃ gataḥ / tatra dvau śrāmaṇerau saṃrañjanīyaṃ dharmaṃ samādāya vartataḥ / ekenāpi saktavo dattā dvitīyenāpi saktavaḥ / ekena khādyakā dvitīyenāpi khādyakā eva / ekena modakā dvitīyenāpi modakāḥ / tau dṛṣṭvā rājā hasitaḥ / imau śrāmaṇerau bālakrīḍayā krīḍataḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the king, serving with his own hand, went to the section of the newly ordained. There, two novice monks (<s>śrāmaṇeras</s>) were observing the conduct that inspires confidence. One asked for barley-meal, and the second also asked for barley-meal. One asked for sweetmeats, and the second also asked for sweetmeats. One asked for round sweets, and the second also asked for round sweets. Seeing them, the king laughed: 'These novices are playing like children!'

body.text: yāvad rājñā bhikṣusaṅghaṃ pariveṣya vṛddhāntamārūḍhaḥ / sthavireṇa cānuyuktaḥ / mā devena kutracid aprasāda utpādita iti /
body.translated_text: After the king had served the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>, he ascended to the senior section. The Elder asked him: 'Your Majesty has not generated displeasure toward anyone, I hope?'

body.text: rājāha / neti / api tu asti dvau śrāmaṇerau bālakrīḍayā krīḍayo yathā bāladārakāḥ pāṃśvāgāraiḥ krīḍantyevaṃ tau śrāmaṇerau saktukrīḍayā krīḍataḥ khādyakrīḍayā krīḍataḥ /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'No. However, there are two novice monks who play childish games — just as young boys play with mud houses, so these two novices play the barley-meal game, the sweetmeat game.'

body.text: sthavira uvāca / alaṃ mahārāja / ubhau hi tau ubhayato bhāgavimuktau arhantau /
body.translated_text: The Elder said: 'Enough, Great King! Both of them are <s>Arhats</s> (Worthy Ones), liberated on both sides.'

body.text: śrutvā ca rājñaḥ prītimanaso buddhirutpannā / tau śramaṇerāvāgamya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ paṭenācchādayiṣyāmi / tatastau śrāmaṇerau rājño 'bhiprāyamavagamya bhūyo 'nye 'smābhiḥ svaguṇā ubhdāvayitavyā iti [cintitau] / tayorekena kaṭāhakā upasthāpitā dvitīyena raṅgaḥ samudānītaḥ /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the king, with a mind filled with joy, thought: 'I shall approach those two novice monks and cover the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s> with cloth.' Then those two novice monks, understanding the king's intention, [thought]: 'We must display yet more of our virtues.' One of them prepared dyeing vats, and the second gathered dye.

body.text: rājñā pṛṣṭau śrāmaṇerakau / kimidamārabdhaṃ / tayorabhihitaṃ / devo 'smākamāgamya bhikṣusaṅghaṃ paṭenācchāditukāmaḥ / tān paṭān rañjayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: The king asked the novice monks: 'What have you begun?' They said: 'Your Majesty wishes to approach us and cover the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s> with cloth. We shall dye those cloths.'

body.text: śrutvā ca rājño buddhirutpannā / mayā kevalaṃ cintitaṃ na tu vāṅa niścāritā / paracittavidāvetau mahātmānau / tataḥ sarvaśarīreṇa pādayornipatyaṃ kṛtāñjaliruvāca /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the king thought: 'I merely thought it — I did not utter a word. These great souls know the minds of others.' Then, prostrating himself with his entire body at their feet, he said with joined palms:

children.translated_text: The <s>Maurya</s> king, with his servants, his people, and his citizens, having well-obtained gain and purpose and having well-performed sacrifice,

children.text: yasyedṛśaḥ sādhujana prasādaḥ kāle tathotsāhi karoti dānaṃ //
children.translated_text: he in whom there is such grace from virtuous people — he makes offerings at the proper time with zeal.

body.text: yāvad rājñābhihitaṃ / yuṣmākamāgamya tricīvareṇa bhikṣusaṅghamācchādayiṣyāmīti / tato rājāśokaḥ pañcavārṣike paryavasite sarvabhikṣūn tricīvareṇācchādya catvāri śatasahasrāṇi saṅghāsyācchādanāni
body.translated_text: Then the king said: 'I shall approach you and cover the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s> with the triple robe.' Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, when the <s>Pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival) was concluded, having covered all the monks with the triple robe and having given four hundred thousand coverings for the <s>Saṅgha</s>

body.text: dattvā pṛthivīmantaḥpuramamātyagaṇamātmānaṃ ca kunālaṃ ca niṣkrītavān / bhūyasā bhagavacchāsane śraddhā pratilabdhā / caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam / iti /
body.translated_text: redeemed the earth, the inner palace, the council of ministers, himself, and <s>Kunāla</s>. His faith in the teaching of the Blessed One was greatly increased. He established eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> (stūpas of the Dharma King). Thus concludes [this section].

children.translated_text: The Tale of <s>Kunāla</s>

body.text:
yasminneva divase rājñāśokena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ tasminneva divase rājño 'śokasya padmāvatī nāmnā devī prasūtā / putro jātaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko nayanāni cāsya paraśobhanāni /
yāvad rājño 'śokasya niveditaṃ / deva diṣṭyā vṛddhirdevasya putro jātaḥ / śrutvā rājā āttamanāḥ kathayati /
body.translated_text: On the very day that King <s>Aśoka</s> established the eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> (stūpas), on that very day, the queen of King <s>Aśoka</s> named <s>Padmāvatī</s> gave birth. A son was born — handsome, pleasing to behold, attractive — and his eyes were exceedingly beautiful. When it was reported to King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'Your Majesty, by good fortune the royal house has prospered — a son is born!' — hearing this, the king, overjoyed, said:

children.text: prītiḥ parā me vipulā hyavāptā mauryasya vaṃśasya parā vibhūtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Supreme and abundant joy has been obtained by me; the glory of the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty is supreme.

children.text: dharmeṇa rājyaṃ mama kurvato hi jātaḥ suto dharmavivardhano 'stu //
children.translated_text: For as I rule the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), may my son be one who increases <s>Dharma</s>!

body.text: tasya dharmavivardhana iti nāma kṛtaṃ / yāvat kumāro rājño 'śokasyopanāmitaḥ / atha rājā kumāraṃ nirīkṣya prītamanāḥ kathayati /
body.translated_text: He was given the name <s>Dharmavivardhana</s> (Increaser of Dharma). When the prince was brought before King <s>Aśoka</s>, the king, gazing at the prince with a pleased mind, said:

children.translated_text: The excellent eyes of my son, supremely meritorious, resembling well-born blue lotuses —

children.text: alaṅkataṃ śobhati yasya vaktraṃ sampūrṇacandrapratimaṃ vibhāti //
children.translated_text: his face, thus adorned, shines beautifully, radiant like the full moon.

body.text: yāvad rājāmātyān uvāca / dṛṣṭāni bhavabhdiḥ kasyedṛśāni nayanāni / amātyā ūcuḥ / deva manuṣyabhūtasya na dṛṣṭāni / api tu deva, asti himavati parvatarāje kunālo nāma pakṣī prativasati / tasya sadṛśāni nayanāni / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the king said to his ministers: 'Have you ever seen such eyes?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, we have not seen such in any human being. But, Your Majesty, there is a bird named <s>Kunāla</s> that dwells on the king of mountains, the <s>Himālaya</s>. Its eyes are similar.' And they said:

children.translated_text: On the peak of the great mountain, the lord <s>Himālaya</s>, rich with water, where coral flowers bloom,

children.text: kunālanāmneti nivāsi pakṣī netrāṇi tenāsya samānyamūni //
children.translated_text: there dwells a bird named <s>Kunāla</s> — its eyes are equal to his.

body.text: tato rājñābhihitaṃ / kunālaḥ pakṣī ānīyatāmiti /
body.translated_text: Then the king said: 'Let the <s>Kunāla</s> bird be brought!'

body.text: tasyordhvato yojanaṃ yakṣāḥ śrṛṇvanti / adho yojanaṃ nāgāḥ / tato yakṣistatkṣaṇena kunālaḥ pakṣī ānītaḥ / atha rājā kunālasya netrāṇi suciraṃ nirīkṣya na kiṃcid viśeṣaṃ paśyati / tato rājñābhihitaṃ / kumārasya kunālasadṛśāni nayanāni / bhavatu kumārasya kunāla iti nāma / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: Above it, for one <s>yojana</s> (league), the <s>Yakṣas</s> hear; below, for one <s>yojana</s>, the <s>Nāgas</s> hear. Then a <s>Yakṣa</s> instantly brought the <s>Kunāla</s> bird. The king, gazing at the <s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes for a long time, saw no difference. Then the king said: 'The prince's eyes are like those of the <s>Kunāla</s>. Let the prince be named <s>Kunāla</s>.' For it will be said:

children.text: netrānurāgeṇa sa pārthivendraḥ sutaṃ kunāleti tadā babhāṣe /
children.translated_text: Out of delight in his eyes, that lord of kings then called his son <s>Kunāla</s>;

children.text: tato 'sya nāma prathitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ tasyāryasattvasya nṛpātmajasya //
children.translated_text: and thus the name of that prince of noble character became renowned throughout the earth.

body.text: vistareṇa yāvat kumāro mahān saṃvṛttaḥ / tasya kāñcanamālā nāma dārikā patnyarthe ānītā /
body.translated_text: In due course, the prince grew up. A girl named <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> (Golden Garland) was brought as his wife.

body.text: yāvad rājāśokaḥ kunālena saha kukkuṭārāmaṃ gataḥ / tatra yaśo nāmnā saṅghasthaviraḥ arhan ṣaḍabhijñaḥ / sa paśyati kunālasya na cirān nayanavināśo bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s> went with <s>Kunāla</s> to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery). There, the Elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> was named <s>Yaśas</s>, an <s>Arhat</s> with the six supernatural powers (<s>ṣaḍabhijñā</s>). He foresaw that before long, <s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes would be destroyed.

body.text: tena rājābhihitaḥ / kimarthaṃ kunālaḥ svakarmaṇi na niyujyate / tato rājñābhihitaḥ / kunāla saṅghasthaviro yadājñāpayati tat paripālayitavyaṃ / tataḥ kunālaḥ sthavirasya pādayornipatya kathayati / sthavira kimājñāpayasi / sthavira uvāca / cakṣuḥkunāla anityamiti kuru / āha /
body.translated_text: He said to the king: 'Why is <s>Kunāla</s> not assigned to his own duties?' Then the king said: '<s>Kunāla</s>, whatever the Elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> commands, that must be observed.' Then <s>Kunāla</s>, falling at the feet of the Elder, said: 'Elder, what do you command?' The Elder said: 'Contemplate that the eye is impermanent, O <s>Kunāla</s>.' He said:

children.text: kumāra cakṣuḥ satataṃ parīkṣyaṃ calātmakaṃ duḥkhasahasrayuktaṃ /
children.translated_text: O prince, the eye is to be constantly examined — it is of restless nature, conjoined with a thousand sufferings;
attached to it, the many ordinary people perform deeds that bring no benefit.

body.text: sa ca tathābhyāsaṃ karoti manasikāraprayuktaḥ / ekābhirāmaḥ praśamārāmaśca saṃvṛttaḥ / sa rājakule vivikte sthāne 'vasthitas cakṣurādīnyāyatanāni anityādibhir ākāraiḥ parīkṣate /
body.translated_text: He practiced accordingly, engaged in mindful contemplation. He became one delighting in solitude, delighting in tranquility. Stationed in a secluded place within the royal palace, he examined the eye and other sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>) with reflections on impermanence and the like.

body.text: tiṣyarakṣitā ca nāmnāśokasyāgramahiṣī taṃ pradeśamabhigatā / sā taṃ kunālamekākinaṃ dṛṣṭvā nayanānurāgeṇa gātreṣu pariṣvajya kathayati /
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, the chief queen of <s>Aśoka</s>, came to that place. Seeing <s>Kunāla</s> alone, with eyes full of passion, she embraced his limbs and said:

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tavedaṃ nayanābhirāmaṃ śrīmad vapurnetrayugaṃ ca kāntaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having seen this form of yours, delightful to the eyes, glorious, and your pair of beautiful eyes,

children.text: daṃdahyate me hṛdayaṃ samantād dāvāgninā prajvalate ca kakṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: my heart is burning all around, and the forest of my being blazes like a wildfire.

body.text: śrutvā kunāla ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ karṇau pidhāya kathayati /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Kunāla</s>, covering both his ears with his hands, said:

children.text: vākyaṃ na yuktaṃ tava vakttumetat sūnoḥ purastāj jananī mamāsi /
children.translated_text: It is not proper for you to speak such words — you are my mother, standing before your son.

children.text: adharmamārgaṃ parivarjayasva apāyamārgasya sa eva hetuḥ //
children.translated_text: Abandon this path of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) — it is indeed the cause of the path to the lower realms.

body.text: tatastiṣyarakṣitā tatkālamalabhamānā ṛddhā kathayati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, not obtaining [her desire] at that time, said in anger:

children.translated_text: Since you do not desire me here, though I have come to you filled with passion,

children.text: na cirādeva durbuddhe sarvathā na bhaviṣyasi //
children.translated_text: before long, O fool, you shall utterly cease to exist!

body.text: kunāla uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Kunāla</s> said:

children.text: mama bhavatu maraṇaṃ māta sthitasya dharme viśuddhabhāvasya /
children.translated_text: Let death come to me, O mother, while I stand firm in <s>Dharma</s>, with a purified disposition;

children.text: na tu jīvitena kāryaṃ sajjanajanadhikkṛtena mama //
children.translated_text: I have no use for a life that is despised by virtuous people.

children.text: svargasya dharmalopo yato bhavati jīvitena kiṃ tena /
children.translated_text: Since the fall from <s>Dharma</s> leads to loss of heaven, what use is such a life —
a life that is the cause of my death, scorned and despised by the wise?

body.text: yāvat tiṣyarakṣitā kunālasya chidrānveṣiṇi avasthitā /
body.translated_text: From that time, <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> remained watchful, seeking an opportunity against <s>Kunāla</s>.

body.text: rājño 'śokasyottarāpathe takṣaśilā nagaraṃ viruddhaṃ / śrutvā ca rājā svayamevābhiprasthitaḥ / tato 'mātyairabhihitaḥ / deva kumāraḥ preṣyatāṃ /
body.translated_text: The city of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> in the northern region revolted against King <s>Aśoka</s>. Hearing this, the king was about to set out himself. Then the ministers said: 'Your Majesty, let the prince be sent.'

body.text: atha rājā kunālamāhūya kathayati / vatsa kunāla gamiṣyasi takṣaśilānagaraṃ saṃnāmayituṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having summoned <s>Kunāla</s>, said: 'Dear son <s>Kunāla</s>, will you go to the city of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> to bring it to submission?'

body.text: kunāla uvāca / paraṃ deva gamiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: <s>Kunāla</s> said: 'Indeed, Your Majesty, I shall go.'

children.text: tato nṛpastasya niśāmya bhāvaṃ putrābhidhānasya manorathasya /
children.translated_text: Then the king, having perceived the noble aspiration of his son,

children.text: snehācca yogyaṃ manasā ca buddvā ājñāpayāmāsa vihārayātrāṃ //
children.translated_text: and understanding out of affection and in his mind that it was fitting, commanded the departure procession.

body.text: atha rājāśoko nagaraśobhāṃ mārgaśobhāṃ ca kṛtvā jīrṇāturakṛpaṇāṃśca mārgādapanīya ekarathe 'bhiruhya kumāreṇa saha pāṭaliputrān nirgataḥ / anuvrajitvā nivartamānaḥ kunālaṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya nayanaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ prarudannuvāca /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having arranged the decoration of the city and the road, and having removed the infirm, sick, and destitute from the road, mounted a single chariot together with the prince and departed from <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. Accompanying him partway and then turning back, he embraced <s>Kunāla</s> around the neck and, gazing at his eyes, wept and said:

children.text: dhanyāni tasya cakṣūṃṣi cakṣuṣmantaśca te janāḥ /
children.translated_text: Blessed are his eyes, and blessed are those people
who will constantly behold the lotus-face of the prince.

body.text: yāvan naimittiko brāhmaṇaḥ paśyati kumārasya na cirān nayanavināśo bhaviṣyati / sa ca rājāśokastasya nayaneṣvatyarthamanuṣuktaḥ / dṛṣṭvā ca kathayati /
body.translated_text: Then a soothsaying <s>brāhmaṇa</s> foresaw that before long the prince's eyes would be destroyed. And King <s>Aśoka</s> was excessively attached to his eyes. Seeing [the omen], he said:

children.translated_text: The pure eyes of the prince, to which the king is deeply attached,

children.text: śriyā vivṛddhe hi sukhānukūle paśyāmi netre 'dya vinaśyamāne //
children.translated_text: auspicious and conducive to happiness, enhanced by royal splendor — I see those very eyes now being destroyed.

children.text: idaṃ puraṃ svarga iva prahṛṣṭaṃ kumārasaṃdarśanajātaharṣaṃ /
children.translated_text: This city, delighted like heaven, filled with joy at the sight of the prince —

children.text: puraṃ vipanne nayane tu tasya bhaviṣyate śokaparītacetaḥ //
children.translated_text: when his eyes are destroyed, this city will be overcome with hearts full of grief.

body.text: anupūrveṇa takṣaśilāmanuprāptaḥ / śrutvā ca takṣaśilāpaurā ardhatrikāṇi yojanāni mārgaśobhāṃ nagaraśobhāṃ ca kṛtvā pūrṇakumbhaiḥ pratyudgatāḥ / vakṣyati ca /
body.translated_text: Proceeding in due order, he arrived at <s>Takṣaśilā</s>. Hearing [of his approach], the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, having decorated the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s> and the city, came out to receive him with filled auspicious jars. And it will be said:

children.translated_text: Hearing [of his arrival], the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, bearing gem-filled jars and the like,
came out swiftly to welcome the prince, honoring him greatly.

body.text: pratyudgamya kṛtāñjaliruvāca / na vayaṃ kumārasya viruddhā na rājño 'śokasya / api tu dṛṣṭātmāno 'mātyā āgatyāsmākamapamānaṃ kurvanti / yāvat kunālo mahatā sammānena takṣaśilāṃ praveśitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Coming forth to meet him, he said with folded hands: 'We are not hostile to the prince, nor to King <s>Aśoka</s>. But the haughty ministers come and insult us.' Thereupon <s>Kunāla</s> was received into <s>Takṣaśilā</s> with great honour.

body.text: rājñaścāśokasya mahān vyādhirutpannaḥ / tasya mukhāduccāro nirgantumārabdhaḥ / sarvaromakūpebhyaścāśuci pragharati na ca śakyate cikitsituṃ / tato rājñābhihitaṃ / kunālamānayata rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti / kiṃ mamedṛśena jīvitena prayojanaṃ /
body.translated_text: King <s>Aśoka</s> was afflicted with a great illness. Excrement began to issue from his mouth. Impure matter oozed from every pore of his skin, and it could not be treated. Then the king said: 'Bring <s>Kunāla</s>; I shall install him on the throne. What use is such a life to me?'

body.text: śrutvā ca tiṣyarakṣitā cintayati / yadi kunālaṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati nāsti mama jīvitaṃ / tayābhihitaṃ / ahaṃ tvā svasthaṃ kariṣyāmi kiṃ tu vaidyānāṃ praveśaḥ pratiṣidhyatāṃ / yāvad rājñā vaidyānāṃ praveśaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ / tatastiṣyarakṣitayā vaidyānāmabhihitaṃ / yadi kaścidīdṛśena vyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ strī vā puruṣo vāgacchati mama darśayitavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> thought: 'If he installs <s>Kunāla</s> on the throne, my life is over.' She said: 'I shall cure you, but the entry of physicians must be forbidden.' Then the king forbade the entry of physicians. Thereupon <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> said to the physicians: 'If any person afflicted with such an illness — whether woman or man — comes, they must be shown to me.'

body.text: anyatamaścābhīrastādṛśenaiva vyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ / tasya patnyā vaidyāya vyādhirniveditaḥ / vaidyenābhihitaṃ / sa evāgacchatvāturo vyādhiṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaiṣajyamupadekṣyāmi / yāvadābhīro vaidyasakāśamabhigataḥ / vaidyena ca tiṣyarakṣitāyāḥ samīpamupanītaḥ / tatastiṣyarakṣitayā pratigupte pradeśe jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ / jīvitād vyaparopya kukṣiṃ pāṭayitvā paśyati ca tasya pakvāśayasthānaṃ / antrāyāṃ kṛmirmahān prādurbhūtaḥ / sa yadyūrdhvaṃ gacchati tenāśuci pragharati / athāgho gacchatyadhaḥ pragharati / yāvat tatra maricān peṣayitvā datto na ca [sa] mriyate / evaṃ pippaliṃ śrṛṅgaveraṃ ca / vistareṇa yāvat palāṇḍuṃ dattaḥ / spṛṣṭaśca
body.translated_text: Now a certain <s>Ābhīra</s> (herdsman) was afflicted with exactly the same illness. His wife reported the illness to a physician. The physician said: 'Let the sick man himself come; having seen the illness, I shall prescribe the medicine.' The <s>Ābhīra</s> went to the physician, and the physician brought him before <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>. Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, in a concealed place, killed him. Having killed him, she cut open his belly and examined the location of his intestines. A large worm had appeared in the gut. When it went upward, impure matter flowed out from above; when it went downward, it flowed from below. Then ground pepper was applied to it, but it did not die. Likewise long pepper and ginger. In detail — finally onion was applied. When touched,

body.text: mṛta uccāramārgeṇa nirgataḥ / etacca prakaraṇaṃ tayā rājñe niveditaṃ / deva palāṇḍuṃ paribhuṃkṣva svāsthyaṃ bhaviṣyati / rājāha / devi, ahaṃ kṣatriyaḥ kathaṃ palāṇḍuṃ paribhakṣayāmi / devyuvāca / deva, paribhoktavyaṃ jīvitasyārthe bhaiṣajyametat /
body.translated_text: it died and came out through the excretory passage. This procedure was reported by her to the king. 'Your Majesty, eat onion and you will be cured.' The king said: 'Queen, I am a <s>Kṣatriya</s> — how can I eat onion?' The queen said: 'Your Majesty, it must be eaten for the sake of life; this is medicine.'

body.text: rājñā paribhuktaṃ / sa ca kṛmirmṛta uccāramārgeṇa nirgataḥ / svasthībhūtaśca rājā / tena parituṣṭena tiṣyarakṣitā vareṇa pravāritā / kiṃ te vara prayacchāmi / tayābhihitaṃ / saptāhaṃ mama devo rājyaṃ prayacchatu / rājāha / ahaṃ ko bhaviṣyāmi / devyuvāca / saptāhasyātyayād deva eva rājā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: The king ate it. That worm died and came out through the excretory passage. The king was restored to health. Pleased, he offered <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> a boon: 'What boon shall I grant you?' She said: 'Let Your Majesty grant me the kingdom for seven days.' The king said: 'Then what shall I be?' The queen said: 'After seven days, Your Majesty will again be the king.'

body.text: yāvad rājñā tiṣyarakṣitāyāḥ saptāhaṃ rājyaṃ dattaṃ / tasyā buddhirutpannā / idānīṃ mayāsya kunālasya vairaṃ niryātayitavyaḥ / tayā kapaṭalekho likhitastakṣaśilakānāṃ paurāṇāṃ / kunālasya nayanaṃ vināśayitavyamiti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the king granted <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> the kingdom for seven days. She formed a plan: 'Now I must take my revenge against this <s>Kunāla</s>.' She wrote a forged letter to the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>: '<s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes are to be destroyed.' And she said:

children.text: rājā hyaśoko balavān pracaṇḍa ājñāpayattakṣaśilājanaṃ hi /
children.translated_text: The powerful and fierce King <s>Aśoka</s> commands the people of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>:

children.text: uddhāryatāṃ locanamasya śatraurmauryasya vaṃśasya kalaṅku eṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Let the eyes of this enemy be gouged out — he is the disgrace of the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty.'

body.text: rājño 'śokasya yatra kāryamāśu pariprāpyaṃ bhavati [sa] dantamudrayā mudrayati / yāvat tiṣyarakṣitā śayitasya rājñastaṃ lekhaṃ dantamudrayā mudrayiṣyāmīti rājñaḥ sakāśamabhigatā / rājā ca bhītaḥ pratibuddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Wherever King <s>Aśoka</s>'s business was to be quickly accomplished, he sealed it with his tooth-seal. Thereupon <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, thinking 'I shall seal this letter with the tooth-seal,' approached the sleeping king. But the king awoke in fright.

body.text: devī kathayati / kimidamiti / rājā kathayati / devi svapnaṃ maṃ'śobhanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ / paśyāmi dvau gṛdhrau kunālasya nayanamutpāṭayitumicchataḥ / devī kathayati / svāsthyaṃ kumārasyeti / evaṃ dvirapi rājā bhītaḥ pratibuddhaḥ kathayati / devi svapno me na śobhano dṛṣṭa iti / tiṣyarakṣitā kathayati / kīdṛśaḥ svapna iti / rājāha / paśyāmi kunālaṃ dīrghakeśanakhaśmaśruṃ pauraṃ praviṣṭaṃ / devyāha / svāsthyaṃ kumārasyeti /
body.translated_text: The queen said: 'What is this?' The king said: 'Queen, I have had an inauspicious dream. I see two vultures wanting to gouge out <s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes.' The queen said: 'All is well with the prince.' Again the king awoke in fright a second time and said: 'Queen, I have had an inauspicious dream.' <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> asked: 'What kind of dream?' The king said: 'I see <s>Kunāla</s> entering the city with long hair, nails, and beard.' The queen said: 'All is well with the prince.'

body.text: yāvat tiṣyarakṣitayā rājñaḥ śayitasya sa lekho dantamudrayā mudrayitvā takṣaśilāṃ preṣitaḥ / yāvad rājñā śayitena svapne dṛṣṭaṃ dantā viśīrṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> sealed that letter with the tooth-seal of the sleeping king and dispatched it to <s>Takṣaśilā</s>. While the king slept, he saw in a dream that his teeth were crumbling.

body.text: tato rājā tasyā eva rātreratyaye naimittikān āhūya kathayati / kīdṛśa eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ vipāka iti / naimittikāḥ kathayanti / deva ya īdṛśasvapnāni paśyati tasya putrasya cakṣurbhedo bhavati / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, at the passing of that night, summoned the interpreters of omens and said: 'What is the consequence of these dreams?' The interpreters of omens said: 'Your Majesty, one who sees such dreams will witness the blinding of his son.' And they said:

children.text: dantā yasya viśīryante svapnānte prapatanti ca /
children.translated_text: He whose teeth crumble and fall in a dream

children.text: caturbhedaṃ ca putrasya putranāśaṃ sa paśyati //
children.translated_text: will see the four-fold destruction of his son — or the loss of his son.

body.text: śrutvā ca rājāśokas tvaritamutthāyāsanāt kṛtāñjaliścaturdiśaṃ devatāṃ yācayitumārabdhaḥ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, King <s>Aśoka</s> quickly rose from his seat and, with folded hands, began to beseech the deities of the four directions. And he said:

children.text: yā devatā śāsturabhiprasannā dharme ca saṅghe ca gaṇapradhāne /
children.translated_text: May those deities who are devoted to the Teacher, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the chief of assemblies,

children.text: ye cāpi loke ṛṣayo variṣṭhā rakṣantu te 'smattanayaṃ kunālaṃ //
children.translated_text: and those who are the greatest seers in the world — may they protect my son <s>Kunāla</s>!

body.text: sa ca lekho 'nupūrveṇa takṣaśilāmupanītaḥ / atha takṣaśilāḥ paurajānapadā lekhadarśanāt kunālasya guṇavistaratuṣṭā notsahante tadapriyaṃ nivedituṃ / ciraṃ vicārayitvā caṇḍo rājā duḥśīlaḥ svaputrasya na marṣayati prāgevāsmākaṃ [kiṃ] marṣayati / āha ca /
body.translated_text: That letter was duly conveyed to <s>Takṣaśilā</s>. Then the citizens and countryfolk of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, upon seeing the letter, being gratified by the full extent of <s>Kunāla</s>'s virtues, could not bring themselves to deliver that unpleasant news. After long deliberation they thought: 'The king is harsh and ill-tempered; he does not spare even his own son — how much less would he spare us?' And they said:

children.translated_text: Of this prince, who is like a sage in conduct, peaceful, and seeking the welfare of all beings,

children.text: yasya dveṣaḥ kumārasya kasya nāsya bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: who could harbour hatred? Who would not have compassion for him?

body.text: tairyāvat kunālasya niveditaṃ / lekhaścopanītaḥ / tataḥ kunālo vācayitvā kathayati / viśrabdhaṃ yathātmaprayojanaṃ kriyatāmiti / yāvac caṇḍālā upanītāḥ kunālasya nayanam utpāṭayateti / te ca kṛtāñjalipuṭā ūcuḥ / notsahayāmaḥ / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then they reported to <s>Kunāla</s>, and the letter was presented. Then <s>Kunāla</s>, having had it read aloud, said: 'Carry out the matter with confidence, as is its purpose.' Then <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcaste executioners) were brought forward — 'Gouge out <s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes!' But they, with palms joined in supplication, said: 'We cannot bring ourselves to do it.' Why?

children.text: yo hi candramasaḥ kāntiṃ mohādabhyuddharen naraḥ /
children.translated_text: For he who would, out of delusion, snatch away the beauty of the moon from the sky —

children.text: sa candrasadṛśād vaktrāt tava netre samuddharet //
children.translated_text: only he could gouge out your eyes from your moon-like face.

body.text: tataḥ kumāreṇa makuṭaṃ dattam / anayā dakṣiṇayotpāṭayata iti / tasya tu karmaṇāvaśyaṃ vipaktavyaṃ / puruṣo hi vikṛtarūpoṣṭādaśabhirdaurvarṇikaiḥ
body.translated_text: Then the prince gave his crown and said: 'With this reward, gouge them out!' But his <s>karma</s> (past actions) had necessarily to ripen. A man of hideous appearance, endowed with the eighteen marks of disfigurement,

body.text: samanvāgato 'bhyāgataḥ / sa kathayati / ahamutpāṭayiṣyāmīti / yāvat kunālasya samīpaṃ nītaḥ / tasmiṃśca samaye kunālasya sthavirāṇāṃ vacanamāmukhībhūtaṃ / sa tad vacanamanusmṛtyovāca /
body.translated_text: arrived. He said: 'I shall gouge them out.' He was then brought before <s>Kunāla</s>. At that moment, the words of the elders came to <s>Kunāla</s>'s mind. Recollecting those words, he said:

children.translated_text: Knowing this calamity, those speakers of truth have said:

children.text: paśyānityamidaṃ sarvaṃ nāsti kaścid dhruve sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'See — all this is impermanent; no one stands on firm ground.'
They are my spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), desirous of my happiness and welfare,
by whom this <s>Dharma</s> was taught — those great-souled ones free from defilements.

children.text: anityatāṃ saṃparipaśyato me gurūpadeśān manasi prakurvataḥ /
children.translated_text: As I contemplate impermanence, carrying out in my mind the instruction of the teacher,

children.text: utpāṭane 'haṃ na bibhemi saumya netradvayasyāsthiratāṃ hi paśye //
children.translated_text: I do not fear the gouging, O gentle one, for I see the instability of my pair of eyes.

children.text: utpāṭye vā na vā netre yathā vā manyate nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether the eyes are gouged out or not, as the king sees fit —
my eye has grasped the essence through the supports of impermanence and the like.

body.text: tataḥ kunālas taṃ puruṣamuvāca / tena hi bhoḥ puruṣa ekaṃ tāvan nayanam utpāṭya mama haste 'nuprayaccha / yavat sa puruṣaḥ kunālasya nayanamutpāṭayituṃ pravṛttaḥ / tato 'nekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi vikroṣṭumārabdhāni / kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s> said to that man: 'Well then, O man, first gouge out one eye and place it in my hand.' Then that man proceeded to gouge out <s>Kunāla</s>'s eye. Thereupon hundreds of thousands of living beings began to cry out: 'How terrible!'

children.text: eṣa hi nirmalajyotsno gaganāt patate śaśī /
children.translated_text: This is the moon with its spotless radiance falling from the sky,
and the glorious lotus being uprooted from the bed of white lotuses!

body.text: teṣu prāṇiśatasahasreṣu rudatsu kunālasyaiva nayanamutpāṭya haste dattaṃ / tataḥ kunālastannayanaṃ gṛhyovāca /
body.translated_text: As those hundreds of thousands of beings wept, <s>Kunāla</s>'s eye was gouged out and placed in his hand. Then <s>Kunāla</s>, taking that eye, said:

children.text: rūpāṇi kasmānna nirīkṣase tvaṃ yathā purā prākṛtamāṃsapiṇḍa /
children.translated_text: Why do you not perceive forms as before, O lump of common flesh?

children.text: te vañcitāste ca vigarhaṇīyā ātmeti ye tvāmabudhāḥ śrayante //
children.translated_text: They are deceived and blameworthy — those foolish ones who, thinking 'this is the self,' resort to you.
Dependent on conditions, resembling a bubble, exceedingly rare, without independent power over its objects —

children.text: evaṃ pravīkṣanti sadāpramattā ye tvāṃ na te duḥkhamanuprayānti //
children.translated_text: those who are always vigilant and see you thus do not follow the path of suffering.
As he thus contemplated the impermanence of all phenomena,
the fruit of <s>Srotāpatti</s> (Stream-entry) was attained, while the multitude of people looked on.

body.text: tataḥ kunālo dṛṣṭasatyastaṃ puruṣamuvāca / idānīṃ dvitīyaṃ viśrabdhaṃ nayanamutpāṭyatāṃ / yāvattena puruṣeṇa kunālasya dvitīyaṃ nayanamutpāṭya haste dattaṃ / atha kunālo māṃsacakṣuṣi uddhṛte prajñācakṣuṣi ca viśuddhe kathayati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s>, having seen the Truth, said to that man: 'Now gouge out the second eye with confidence.' Then that man gouged out <s>Kunāla</s>'s second eye and placed it in his hand. Then <s>Kunāla</s>, his eyes of flesh having been removed and his eye of wisdom having been purified, said:

body.text:
uddhṛtaṃ māṃsacakṣurme yadyapyetat sudurlabhaṃ /
prajñācakṣurviśuddhaṃ me pratilabdham aninditaṃ /
body.translated_text: Though this exceedingly rare eye of flesh has been removed from me, the blameless eye of wisdom has been purified and gained by me.

children.translated_text: Though I have been abandoned by the king with the designation of 'son,'
I have attained sonship of the great-souled King of <s>Dharma</s> (the <s>Buddha</s>).
Though I am fallen from royal sovereignty, which is a bond of grief and suffering,
I have gained the sovereignty of <s>Dharma</s>, which destroys suffering and grief.

body.text: yāvat kunālena śrutaṃ nāyaṃ tātasyāśokasya ādeśaḥ / api tu tiṣyarakṣitāyāṃ ayaṃ prayoga iti / śrutvā ca kunālaḥ kathayati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s> learned: 'This is not the command of my father <s>Aśoka</s>; rather, this is the doing of <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>.' Having learned this, <s>Kunāla</s> said:

children.text: ciraṃ sukhaṃ tiṣṭhatu tiṣyanāmnī āyurbalaṃ pālayatāṃ ca devī /
children.translated_text: May she named <s>Tiṣyā</s> live long and happily, and may the queen preserve her life and strength,

children.text: saṃpreṣitoyaṃ hi yayā prayogo yasyānubhāvena kṛtaḥ svakārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: for it is she who dispatched this act, by whose power my own purpose has been accomplished.

body.text: tataḥ kāñcanamālayā śrutaṃ kunālasya nayanāni utpāṭitānīti / śrutvā ca bhartṛtayā kunālasamīpamupasaṃkramya parṣadamavagāhya kunālamuddhṛtanayanaṃ rudhirāvasiktagātraṃ dṛṣṭvā mūrchitā bhūmau patitā / yāvaj jalasekaṃ kṛtvā utthāpitā /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> heard that <s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes had been gouged out. Hearing this, she, out of wifely devotion, came to <s>Kunāla</s>, and entering the assembly, seeing <s>Kunāla</s> with his eyes removed and his body drenched in blood, she fainted and fell to the ground. She was revived by sprinkling water upon her.

body.text: tataḥ kathaṃcit saṃjñāmupalabhya sasvaraṃ prarudatī uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then, somehow regaining consciousness, she wept aloud and said:

children.text: netrāṇi kāntāni manoharāṇi ye māṃ nirīkṣyā janayanti tuṣṭiṃ /
children.translated_text: Those beautiful, enchanting eyes that, gazing upon me, used to bring me joy —

children.text: te me vipannā hyanirīkṣaṇīyā styajanti me prāṇasamāḥ śarīraṃ //
children.translated_text: they are now destroyed, no longer to be seen; they, dear as life itself, depart from my body.

body.text: tataḥ kunālo bhāryāmanunayannuvāca / alaṃ ruditena / nārhasi śokamāśrayituṃ / svayaṃkṛtānāmiha karmaṇāṃ phalamupasthitaṃ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s>, consoling his wife, said: 'Enough of weeping. You should not give way to grief. The fruit of actions done by oneself has arrived.' And he said:

children.text: karmātmakaṃ lokamidaṃ viditvā duḥkhātmakaṃ cāpi janaṃ hi matvā /
children.translated_text: Knowing this world to be governed by <s>karma</s> (action), and knowing people to be beset by suffering,

children.text: matvā ca lokaṃ priyaviprayogaṃ kartuṃ priye nārhasi vāṣpamokṣaṃ //
children.translated_text: and knowing the world to be subject to separation from the beloved — O dear one, you should not shed tears.

body.text: tataḥ kunālo bhāryayā saha takṣaśilāyā niṣkāsitaḥ / sa garbhādhānamupādāya paramasukumāraśariraḥ / na kiñcid utsahate karma kartuṃ / kevalaṃ vīṇāṃ vādayati / gāyati ca / tato bhaikṣyaṃ labhate kunālaḥ patnyā saha bhuṃkte /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s> was sent out from <s>Takṣaśilā</s> together with his wife. He, with a supremely delicate body, supporting the embryo she carried, was unable to do any work. He merely played the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) and sang. From that he obtained alms and ate together with his wife.

body.text: tataḥ kāñcanamālā yena mārgeṇa pātaliputrādānītā tameva mārgaṃmanusarantī bhartudvitīyā pāṭaliputraṃ gatā / yāvadaśokasya gṛhamārabdhā praveṣṭuṃ / dvārapālena ca nivāritau / yāvad rājño 'śokasya yānaśālāyāmavasthitau /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, following the very road by which she had been brought from <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, went to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> accompanied by her husband. When they approached the house of <s>Aśoka</s> and were about to enter, they were stopped by the door-keeper. They remained in the king <s>Aśoka</s>'s carriage-shed.

body.text: tataḥ kunālo rātryāḥ pratyuṣamaye vīṇāṃ vādayitumārabdhaḥ / yathā nayanānyutpāṭitāni satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tadanurūpaṃ hitaṃ ca gītaṃ prārabdhaṃ / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s>, at the break of dawn, began to play the <s>vīṇā</s>. In accordance with how his eyes had been gouged out and the vision of Truth had been attained, he began to sing a fitting and beneficial song. And he said:

children.translated_text: The wise one who perceives the eye and other sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>)
with the pure lamp of knowledge — he is freed from <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth).

children.text: yadi tava bhavaduḥkhapīḍitā bhavati ca doṣaviniścitā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: If your mind, tormented by the suffering of existence, has become resolved regarding its faults,

children.text: sukhamiha ca yadīcchasi dhruvaṃ tvaritamihāyatanāni saṃtyaja //
children.translated_text: and if you desire certain happiness here, then swiftly abandon these sense-bases!

body.text: tasya gītaśabdo rājñāśokena śrutaḥ / śrutvā ca prītamanā uvāca /

children.text: gītaṃ kunālena mayi prasaktaṃ vīṇāsvaraścaiva śrutaścireṇa /
children.translated_text: <s>Kunāla</s> has sung a song directed at me, and the sound of the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) has been heard after a long time;

children.text: abhyāgato 'pīha gṛhaṃ nu kañcin na cecchati draṣṭumayaṃ kumāraḥ //
children.translated_text: has this prince come here to the palace, yet does not wish to see me?

body.translated_text: The sound of his singing was heard by King <s>Aśoka</s>. Having heard it, with a pleased heart he said:

body.text: atha rājāśoko 'nyatamapuruṣamāhūyovāca / puruṣa lakṣyate /

children.text: na khalveṣa kiṃ gītasya kunālasadṛśo dhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: Is this not indeed the sound resembling that of <s>Kunāla</s>'s singing?
It seems to indicate both a deed and lack of resolve.

body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, summoning a certain man, said: 'Man, look carefully.

children.translated_text: By this sound, I have been greatly shaken from my composure,
like an elephant who has lost its young, hearing the call of a lost calf.

body.text: gaccha kunālamānayasveti / yāvat puruṣo yānaśālāṃ gataḥ / paśyati kunālam uddhṛtanayanaṃ vātātapaparidagdhagātramapratyabhijñāya ca rājānamaśokam abhigamyovāca / deva na hyeṣa kunālaḥ / andhaka eṣa vanīpakaḥ patnyā saha devasya yānaśālāyām avasthitaḥ / śrutvā ca rājā saṃvignaścintayāmāsa / yathā mayā svapnānyaśobhanāni dṛṣṭāni niyataṃ kunālasya nayanāni vinaṣṭāni bhaviṣyanti / āha ca /
body.translated_text: Go, bring <s>Kunāla</s>!' The man went to the carriage hall. He saw <s>Kunāla</s> with his eyes plucked out, his body scorched by wind and sun, and not recognizing him, went to King <s>Aśoka</s> and said: 'Your Majesty, this is not <s>Kunāla</s>. There is a blind peddler here, standing in Your Majesty's carriage hall with his wife.' Hearing this, the king was agitated and thought: 'Just as I saw inauspicious dreams, surely <s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes must have been destroyed.' And he said:

children.text: svapnāntare nimittāni yathā dṛṣṭāni me purā /
children.translated_text: The signs that I saw formerly in dreams --

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ kunālasya netre vai nidhanaṃ gate //
children.translated_text: without doubt, <s>Kunāla</s>'s eyes have met their destruction.

body.text: tato rājā prarudannuvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, weeping, said:

children.translated_text: Let this peddler be quickly brought to my presence;

children.text: na hi me śāmyate cetaḥ sutavyasanacintayā //
children.translated_text: my heart finds no peace, thinking of my son's calamity.

body.text: yāvat puruṣo yānaśālāṃ gatvā kunālamuvāca / kasya tvaṃ putraḥ / kiṃ ca nāma / kunālaḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: The man went to the carriage hall and said to <s>Kunāla</s>: 'Whose son are you? And what is your name?' <s>Kunāla</s> said:

children.translated_text: That king named <s>Aśoka</s>, increaser of the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty,

children.text: kṛtsneyaṃ pṛthivī yasya vaśe vartati kiṃkara //
children.translated_text: this entire earth, obedient, serves under whose command.

children.text: tasya rājñastvahaṃ putraḥ kunāla iti viśrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am the son of that king, known as <s>Kunāla</s>;
I am the son of the righteous one, a kinsman of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), a son of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: tataḥ kunāla patnyā saha rājño 'śokasya samīpamānītaḥ / atha rājāśokaḥ [paśyati] kunālamuddhṛtanayanaṃ vātātapaparidagdhagātraṃ rathyācoḍakasaṃghātapratyavareṇa vāsasā lakṣyālakṣyapracchāditakaupīnaṃ / sa tamapratyabhijñāya ākṛtimātrakaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati / tvaṃ kunāla iti / kunālaḥ prāha / evaṃ deva kunālo 'smīti / śrutvā mūrcchito bhūmau patitaḥ / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s> together with his wife was brought into the presence of King <s>Aśoka</s>. Now King <s>Aśoka</s> saw <s>Kunāla</s> with his eyes plucked out, his body scorched by wind and sun, wearing a garment patched from rags gathered from streets and gutters, with his loincloth barely and incompletely covered. Not recognizing him, seeing only his general form, he said: 'Are you <s>Kunāla</s>?' <s>Kunāla</s> replied: 'Yes, Your Majesty, I am <s>Kunāla</s>.' Hearing this, the king fainted and fell to the ground. For it is said:

children.text: tataḥ kunālasya mukhaṃ nirīkṣya netroddhṛtaṃ śokaparītacetāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, gazing upon the face of <s>Kunāla</s> with his eyes plucked out, his heart overwhelmed by grief,

children.text: rājā hyaśokaḥ patito dharaṇyāṃ hā putra śokena hi dahyamānaḥ //
children.translated_text: King <s>Aśoka</s> fell to the earth, crying: 'Alas, my son!' -- burning with sorrow.

body.text: yāvaj jalapariṣekaṃ kṛtvā rājānamutthāpayitvāsane niṣāditaḥ / atha rājā kathañcit saṃjñāmupalabhya kunālamutsaṅge sthāpayāmāsa / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: After sprinkling him with water and raising the king, he was seated on his throne. Then the king, somehow regaining consciousness, placed <s>Kunāla</s> on his lap. For it is said:

children.text: tato muhūrtaṃ nṛpa āśvasitvā kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya rasāśrukaṇṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the king, having recovered for a moment, embracing him around the neck, his throat choked with tears,

children.text: muhuḥ kunālasya mukhaṃ pramṛjya bahūni rājā vilalāpa tatra //
children.translated_text: repeatedly wiping <s>Kunāla</s>'s face, the king lamented greatly there.

children.text: netre kunālapratime vilokya sutaṃ kunāleti purā babhāse /
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Kunāla</s>'s matchless eyes, he had formerly called his son '<s>Kunāla</s>';

children.text: tadasya netre nidhanaṃ gate te putraṃ kunāleti kathaṃ ca vakṣye //
children.translated_text: now that those eyes have met their end, how shall I call my son '<s>Kunāla</s>'?

body.text: āha ca /
body.translated_text: And he said:

body.text: kathaya kathaya sādhuputra tāvad vadanamidaṃ tava kena cārunetraṃ /
body.translated_text: Tell me, tell me, dear son -- this face of yours with its beautiful eyes,

body.text: gaganamiva vipannacandratāraṃ vyapagataśobham anīkṣakaṃ kṛtaṃ te //
body.translated_text: by whom has it been made like the sky bereft of moon and stars, robbed of splendor, unseeing?

children.text: akaruṇahṛdayena tena tāta munisadṛśasya na sādhu sādhubuddheḥ /
children.translated_text: By that merciless-hearted one, O father, against one who is sage-like, of virtuous mind,
this enmity without cause against the eyes of the best of men has been committed -- the root of my immense grief.

children.text: vada suvadana kṣiprametadarthaṃ vrajati śarīramidaṃ purā vināśaṃ /
children.translated_text: Speak quickly, O fair-faced one, of this matter, before this body goes to destruction,
burned by the grief of your eyes' destruction, like a forest burned by the thunderbolt released by a serpent.

body.text: tataḥ kunālaḥ pitaraṃ praṇipatya uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kunāla</s>, bowing to his father, said:

children.text: rājannatītaṃ khalu naiva śocyaṃ kiṃ na śrutaṃ te munivākyam etat /
children.translated_text: O king, what is past should not be grieved over. Have you not heard this saying of the sage?

children.text: yatkarmabhiste 'pi jinā na muktāḥ pratyekabuddhāḥ sudṛḍhaistathaiva //
children.translated_text: From <s>karma</s> (deeds), even the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) are not freed, nor the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Awakened Ones), with their firm resolve.

children.text: labdhāphalasthāśca pṛthagjanāśca ye kṛtāni karmāṇyamṛtāni dehināṃ /
children.translated_text: And the ordinary beings who have obtained the fruit, and those who have performed immortal deeds for embodied beings --

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtānāmiha karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ kathaṃ tu vakṣyāmi parairidaṃ kṛtaṃ //
children.translated_text: how can I say that this was done by others, when the fruit of deeds done here is self-created?

body.text: ahameva mahārāja kṛtāparādhaśca sāparādhaśca / vinivartayāmi yo 'haṃ vinayāmi vipattijananāni /
body.translated_text: I myself, O great king, am both offender and offended. I, who could have turned away, who could have averted the causes of misfortune --

children.text: na śastravajrāgniviṣāṇi pannagāḥ kurvanti pīḍāṃ rabhasāpakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Weapons, thunderbolts, fire, poison, and serpents -- these violent assailants do not cause affliction;

children.text: śarīralakṣye hi dhṛte hi pārthiva patanti duḥkhānyaśivāni dehināṃ //
children.translated_text: rather, O sovereign, when the body is the target, the inauspicious sufferings of embodied beings fall upon it.

body.text: atha rājā śokāgninā saṃtāpitahṛdaya uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, his heart scorched by the fire of grief, said:

children.text: kenoddhṛtāni nayanāni sutasya mahyaṃ ko jīvitaṃ sumadhuraṃ tyajituṃ vyavastaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who plucked out the eyes of my son? Who is determined to forfeit his own sweet life?

children.text: śokānalo nipatito hṛdaye pracaṇḍaḥ ācakṣva putra laghu kasya harāmi daṇḍaṃ //
children.translated_text: A fierce fire of grief has fallen upon my heart -- speak quickly, son! Whose punishment shall I exact?

body.text: yāvad rājñāśokena śrutaṃ tiṣyarakṣitāyā ayaṃ prayoga iti / śrutvā rājā tiṣyarakṣitāmāhūyovāca /
body.translated_text: When King <s>Aśoka</s> heard that this was the doing of <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, he summoned <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> and said:

children.text: kathaṃ hyadhanye na nimajjase kṣitau chettāsmi śīrṣaṃ paraśuprahāritaṃ /
children.translated_text: How is it, O wretched woman, that you do not sink into the earth? I shall cut off your head with an axe-blow!
I cast you off, you who have committed the most heinous sin, as a self-possessed man casts off prosperity yoked with unrighteousness.

body.text: tato rājā krodhāgninā prajvalitastiṣyarakṣitāṃ nirīkṣyovāca /
body.translated_text: Then the king, blazing with the fire of rage, looking upon <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, said:

children.text: utpāṭya netre paripāṭayāmi gātraṃ kimasyā nakharaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: I shall pluck out her eyes and tear apart her body with sharp fingernails;

children.text: jīvantiśūlāmatha kārayāmi chettāsmi nāsāṃ krakacena vāsyāḥ //
children.translated_text: I shall have her impaled alive, or I shall cut off her nose with a saw.

children.text: kṣūreṇa jivhāmatha kartayāmi viṣeṇa pūrṇāmatha ghāṭayiṣye /
children.translated_text: I shall cut out her tongue with a razor, and then I shall fill her with poison and kill her.
Thus the king pronounced many and various forms of execution.

children.text: śrutvā kunālaḥ karuṇātmakastu vijñāpayāmāsa guruṃ mahātmā /
children.translated_text: But <s>Kunāla</s>, being compassionate by nature, the great soul, petitioned his father:

children.text: anāryakarmā yadi tiṣyarakṣitā tvamāryakarmā bhava mā vadhī striyaṃ //
children.translated_text: Though <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> has acted ignobly, you should act nobly -- do not kill a woman.

body.text: phalaṃ hi maitryā sadṛśaṃ na vidyate prabho titikṣā sugatena varṇitā /
body.translated_text: For there is no fruit equal to that of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), O lord; forbearance (<s>titikṣā</s>) has been praised by the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One, the Buddha).

body.text: punaḥ praṇamya pitaraṃ kumāraḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ sūnṛtavāg jagāda //
body.translated_text: The prince, bowing again to his father, with palms joined, speaking truthful and gentle words, said:

children.text: rājanna me duḥkhalavo 'sti kaścit tīvrāpakāre 'pi na manyutāpaḥ /
children.translated_text: O king, I have not the slightest particle of suffering, nor any burning of anger even toward one who has caused me grievous harm.

children.text: manaḥ prasannaṃ yadi me jananyāṃ yayoddhṛte me nayane svayaṃ hi /
children.translated_text: If my mind is truly at peace toward the mother who herself plucked out my eyes,

children.text: tattena satyena mamāstu tāvan netradvayaṃ prāktanameva sadyaḥ //
children.translated_text: then by that truth, may my pair of eyes become as they were before, at once!

body.text: ityuktamātre pūrvādhikapraśobhite netrayugme prādurbabhūvatuḥ / yāvad rājñāśokena tiṣyarakṣitāmarṣitena jatugṛhaṃ praveśayitvā dagdhā / takṣaśilāśca paurāḥ praghātitāḥ /
body.translated_text: The moment this was spoken, his pair of eyes appeared, more resplendent than before. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, furious, had <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> placed in a house of lac and burned. And the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> were slaughtered.

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayachettāramāyuṣmantaṃ sthaviropaguptaṃ pṛcchati / kiṃ kunālena karma kṛtaṃ yasya karmaṇo vipākena nayanānyutpāṭitāni /
body.translated_text: The monks, having a doubt, asked the Venerable Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s> (deed) did <s>Kunāla</s> perform, by the ripening of which his eyes were plucked out?'

body.text: sthavira uvāca / tena hyāyuṣmantaḥ śrūyatāṃ /
body.translated_text: The Elder said: 'Then listen, Venerable ones.'

body.text: bhūtapūrvamatīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāmanyatamo lubdhakaḥ / sa himavantaṃ gatvā mṛgān praghātayati / so 'pareṇa samayena himavantaṃ gataḥ / tatra cāśanipatitāni pañcamṛgaśatani ekasyā guhāyāṃ praviṣṭānyāsāditāni / tena vāgurayā sarve gṛhītāḥ / tasya buddhirutpannā / yadi
body.translated_text: In the distant past, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain hunter. He went to the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas) and slaughtered deer. On one occasion he went to the <s>Himavat</s>. There he found five hundred deer that had entered a cave, driven in by a thunderbolt. He captured them all with a net. Then the thought arose in him: 'If I

body.text: praghātayiṣyāmi māṃsaḥ kledamupayāsyati / tena pañcānāṃ mṛgaśatānāmakṣīṇyutpāṭitāni / te uddhṛtanayanā na kvacit palāyanti / evaṃ bahūnāṃ mṛgaśatānāṃ nayanānyutpāṭitāni /
body.translated_text: slaughter them, the meat will rot.' So he plucked out the eyes of the five hundred deer. Blinded, they could not flee anywhere. Thus the eyes of many hundreds of deer were plucked out.

body.text: kiṃ manyadhvamāyuṣmantaḥ / yo 'sau lubdhakaḥ sa eṣa kunālaḥ / yattatrānena bahūnāṃ mṛgaśatānāṃ nayanānyutpāṭitāni tasya karmaṇo vipākena bahūni varṣaśatasahasrāṇi narakeṣu duḥkhamanubhūya tataḥ karmaviśeṣeṇa pañcajanmaśatāni tasya nayanānyutpāṭitāni /
body.translated_text: What do you think, Venerable ones? That hunter is this very <s>Kunāla</s>. Because he plucked out the eyes of many hundreds of deer, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he experienced suffering in the hells for many hundreds of thousands of years; and then, by a residual effect of that <s>karma</s>, his eyes were plucked out in five hundred births.

body.text: kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yasya karmaṇo vipākenocce kūle upapannaḥ / prāsādikaśca saṃvṛttaḥ / satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: What <s>karma</s> did he perform, by the ripening of which he was born in a noble family, became pleasing in appearance, and attained the vision of truth?

body.text: tena hyāyuṣmantaḥ śrūyatāṃ /
body.translated_text: Then listen, Venerable ones.

body.text: bhūtapūrvamatīte 'dhvani catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ krakucchando nāma samyaksambuddho loka udapādi /
body.translated_text: In the distant past, when the lifespan of people was forty thousand years, a Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) named <s>Krakucchanda</s> arose in the world.
