body.text: yadā krakucchandaḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasyāśokena rājñā catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ kāritaḥ / yadā rājāśokaḥ kālagato 'śrāddho rājā rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ / tāni ratnānyadattādāyikairhṛtāni / pāṃśukāṣṭhaṃ cāvaśiṣṭaṃ / tatra janakāyo gatvā viśīrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā śocitumārabdhaḥ /
body.translated_text: When <s>Krakucchanda</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, having completed the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, passed into the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder, a <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary mound) made of four kinds of precious gems was erected for him by a king named <s>Aśoka</s>. When that King <s>Aśoka</s> died, a faithless king was established on the throne. The gems were carried off by dishonest people, and only dust and wood remained. People went there and, seeing it in ruins, began to grieve.

body.text: tasmiṃśca samayenyatamaśca śreṣṭhiputraḥ / tenoktaḥ / kimarthaṃ rudyata iti / tairabhihitaṃ krakucchandasya samyaksambuddhasya stūpaścatūratnamaya āsīt / sa idānīṃ viśīrṇaṃ iti /
body.translated_text: At that time there was a certain merchant's son. He asked: 'Why are you weeping?' They said: 'The <s>stūpa</s> of the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Krakucchanda</s> was made of four kinds of gems. It is now in ruins.'

body.text: tatastena yā tatra krakucchandasya samyaksambuddhasya kāyapramāṇikā pratimā babhūva viśīrṇā sābhisaṃskṛtā / samyakpraṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ / yādṛśaḥ krakucchandaḥ śāstedṛśameva śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ / mā virāgayeyamiti /
body.translated_text: Then he restored the image of <s>Krakucchanda</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, which had been in ruins there, made to the life-size proportions of his body. And he made a proper vow: 'May I encounter a teacher just like <s>Krakucchanda</s> the Teacher. May I not become averse to him.'

body.text: kiṃ manyadhvamāyuṣmantaḥ / yo 'sau śreṣṭhiputraḥ sa eṣa kunālaḥ / yatrānena krakucchandasya stūpo 'bhisaṃskṛtastasya karmaṇo vipākenoccakule upapannaḥ / yat pratimābhisaṃskṛtā tasya karmaṇo vipākena kunālaḥ prāsādikaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena kunālena [yādṛśaḥ] śākyamuniḥ samyaksambuddhastādṛśa eva śāstā samārāgito na virāgitaḥ / satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtaṃ /
body.translated_text: What do you think, Venerable ones? That merchant's son is this very <s>Kunāla</s>. Because he restored the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Krakucchanda</s>, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he was born in a noble family. Because the image was restored, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> <s>Kunāla</s> became pleasing in appearance. Because he made the vow, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, <s>Kunāla</s> encountered a teacher just like <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One -- he was not made averse. And he attained the vision of truth.

body.text: iti śrīdivyāvadāne kunālāvadanaṃ saptaviṃśatimaṃ samāptaṃ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Kunālāvadāna</s>, the twenty-seventh, is complete.

children.translated_text: <s>Aśokāvadāna</s> (The Legend of <s>Aśoka</s>)

body.text: yadā rājñāśokena bhagavacchāsane śraddhā pratilabdhā sa bhikṣūn uvāca / kena bhagavacchāsane prabhūtaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ / bhikṣava ūcuḥ / anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā / rājāha / kiyattena bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dattaṃ / bhikṣava ūcuḥ / koṭiśataṃ tena bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dattaṃ / śrutvā ca rājāśokaścintayati / tena gṛhapatinā bhūtvā koṭiśataṃ bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dattaṃ / tenābhihitaṃ / ahamapi koṭīśataṃ bhagacchāsane dānaṃ dāsyāmi /
body.translated_text: When King <s>Aśoka</s> had gained faith in the teaching of the Blessed One, he said to the monks: 'Who gave the most abundant gifts to the teaching of the Blessed One?' The monks said: 'The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.' The king asked: 'How much did he give to the teaching of the Blessed One?' The monks said: 'He gave a hundred <s>koṭis</s> (ten million each) to the teaching of the Blessed One.' Hearing this, King <s>Aśoka</s> thought: 'He, being merely a householder, gave a hundred <s>koṭis</s> to the teaching of the Blessed One.' He declared: 'I too shall give a hundred <s>koṭis</s> to the teaching of the Blessed One.'

body.text: tena yāvac caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ / sarvatra ca śatasahasrāṇi dattāni / jātau bodhau dharmacakre parinirvāṇe ca sarvatra śatasahasraṃ dattaṃ / pañcavārṣikaṃ kṛtaṃ / tatra ca catvāri śatasahasrāṇi dattāni / trīṇi śatasahasrāṇi bhikṣūṇāṃ bhojitāni / yatraikamarhatāṃ dve śaikṣāṇāṃ pṛthagjanakalyāṇakānāṃ ca / koṣaṃ sthāpayitvā mahāpṛthivīmantaḥpurāmātyagaṇamātmānaṃ kunālaṃ cāryasaṅghe niryātayitvā catvāri śatasahasrāṇi dattvā niṣkrītavān / ṣaṇṇavatikoṭyo bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dattaṃ / sa yāvad glānībhūtaḥ / atha rājā idānīṃ na bhaviṣyāmīti viklavībhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: He established eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s> (pillars of the King of Dharma). And everywhere he gave hundreds of thousands. At the sites commemorating the birth, enlightenment, the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma), and the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), he gave a hundred thousand at each place. He held the <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival), and at that he gave four hundred thousand. Three hundred thousand were spent on feeding monks -- of which one portion was for <s>Arhats</s> (Worthy Ones), two for <s>Śaikṣas</s> (learners), and for virtuous ordinary persons. Setting aside the treasury, he offered the great earth, the inner palace, the assembly of ministers, himself, and <s>Kunāla</s> to the noble <s>Saṅgha</s> (monastic community), and having given four hundred thousand, he redeemed them all. Ninety-six <s>koṭis</s> were given to the teaching of the Blessed One. Then he fell ill. And the king, thinking 'Now I shall not survive,' became distressed.

body.text: tasya rādhagupto nāmāmātyo yena saha pāṃśudānaṃ dattaṃ / tadā sa rājānamaśokaṃ viklavībhūtamavekṣya pādayornipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca /
body.translated_text: He had a minister named <s>Rādhagupta</s>, with whom he had [as boys] given the gift of dirt [to the Buddha in a past life]. Then he, seeing King <s>Aśoka</s> distraught, fell at his feet, and with palms joined said:

children.translated_text: That face of yours, O lord, radiant as the fierce sun, which was never looked upon [with defiance] by hosts of powerful enemies when assembled,

children.text: padmānanaśrīśatasaṃprapītaṃ kasmāt savāṣpaṃ tava deva vaktraṃ //
children.translated_text: drunk upon by hundreds of splendors of lotus-like beauties — why is it now tearful?

body.text: rājāha / rādhagupta, nāhaṃ dravyavināśaṃ na rājyanāśanaṃ na cāśrayaviyogaṃ śocāmi / kintu śocāmi, āryairyad, viprayokṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: The king said: '<s>Rādhagupta</s>, I do not grieve over the loss of wealth, nor the loss of the kingdom, nor separation from my refuge. But I grieve that I shall be parted from the Noble Ones.'

children.text: nāhaṃ punaḥ sarvaguṇopapannaṃ saṅghaṃ samakṣaṃ naradevapūjitaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Never again shall I worship, face to face, the <s>Saṅgha</s> (community of monks), endowed with all virtues, honored by kings of men,
with excellent food and drink — thinking upon this, these are my tears.'

body.text: api ca rādhagupta, ayaṃ me manoratho babhūva, koṭīśataṃ bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dāsyāmīti / sa ca me 'bhiprāyo na paripūrṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, '<s>Rādhagupta</s>, this was my heart's desire: "I shall give a hundred <s>koṭis</s> (ten million each) as a gift to the Blessed One's Teaching." But that intention of mine has not been fulfilled.'

body.text: tato rājñāśokena catasraḥ koṭīḥ paripurayiṣyāmīti hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ kukkuṭārāmaṃ preṣayitumārabdhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, wishing to complete [the remaining] four <s>koṭis</s>, began sending gold and silver to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery).

body.text: tasmiṃśca samaye kunālasya saṃpadī nāma putro yuvarājye pravartate / tasyāmātyair abhihitaṃ / kumāra aśoko rājā svalpakālavasthāyī /
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>Kunāla</s>'s son named <s>Saṃpadī</s> was serving as crown prince. His ministers told him: 'Prince, King <s>Aśoka</s> has but little time remaining.

body.text: idaṃ ca dravyaṃ kukkuṭārāmaṃ preṣyate / kośabalinaśca rājānaḥ / nivārayitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And this wealth is being sent to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s>. Kings are powerful through their treasury. He must be stopped.'

body.text: yāvatkumāreṇa bhāṇḍāgārikaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ / yadā rājño 'śokasyāpratiṣiddhā [sampat] tasya suvarṇabhājane āhāramupanāmyate / bhuktvā tāni suvarṇabhājanāni kukkuṭārāmaṃ preṣayati /
body.translated_text: Thereupon the prince forbade the treasurer. When King <s>Aśoka</s>'s [sending of wealth] was not obstructed, food was served to him in golden vessels. Having eaten, he would send those golden vessels to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s>.

body.text: tasya suvarṇabhājanaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ / rūpyabhājane āhāramupanāmyate / tānyapi kukkuṭārāmaṃ preṣayati / tato rūpyabhājanamapi pratiṣiddhaṃ / tasya yāvan mṛbhdājana āhāramupanāmyate /
body.translated_text: The golden vessels were forbidden to him. Food was served in silver vessels. He sent those too to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s>. Then the silver vessels were also forbidden. Eventually food was served to him in earthen vessels.

body.text: tasmiṃśca samaye rājño 'śokasyārdhāmalakaṃ karāntaragataṃ / atha rājāśokaḥ saṃvignaḥ amātyān paurāṃśca saṃnipātya kathayati / kaḥ sāmprataṃ pṛthivyāmīśvaraḥ /
body.translated_text: At that time, King <s>Aśoka</s> held half an <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan fruit) in the palm of his hand. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, deeply moved, assembled his ministers and citizens and said: 'Who is now the lord of the earth?'

body.text: tato 'mātyā utthāyāsanād yena rājāśokastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya ūcuḥ / deva pṛthivyāmīśvaraḥ / atha rājā aśokaḥ sāśrudurdinanayanavadano 'mātyān uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the ministers, rising from their seats, bowed with palms joined toward King <s>Aśoka</s> and said: 'Your Majesty is the lord of the earth.' Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, his face clouded with tears like a rainy day, said to the ministers:

children.text: dākṣiṇyādanṛtaṃ hi kiṃ kathayatha bhraṣṭādhirājyā vayaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Why do you speak an untruth out of courtesy? I have been stripped of sovereignty;
what remains — half a myrobalan — that is the extent of my dominion.
Shame on this ignoble lordship, comparable to the rushing entry of a swollen river's waters —
even to me, a king among mortals, fearful poverty has come!'

body.text: athavā ko bhagavato vākyamanyathā kariṣyati / sampattayo hi sarvā vipattinidānā iti pratijñātaṃ yadavitathavādinā gautamena na hi tad visaṃvadati / pratiśiṣyate 'smannacirājñā mama yāvatithā manasā sādya mahādriśilātale vihatāvan nadī pratinivṛttā /
body.translated_text: Or rather, who can make the words of the Blessed One otherwise? For it was declared by <s>Gautama</s>, the speaker of truth, that 'all prosperities are the root cause of calamity' — and that does not prove false. My command, which formerly, like the waters of a river striking the surface of a great mountain rock, turned back [all resistance] —

children.translated_text: Having commanded the earth under a single parasol, having shaken off the drums and kettledrums [of rival kings],
having uprooted hosts of proud enemies and having consoled the wretched and afflicted —

children.text: bhraṣṭāsthāyatano na bhāṭi kṛpaṇaḥ saṃpratyaśoko nṛpaś
children.translated_text: now, fallen from his state, the pitiable King <s>Aśoka</s> no longer shines,
like an <s>aśoka</s> tree that withers with its flowers and leaves broken, wilted, and scattered.

body.text: tato rājāśokaḥ samīpagataṃ puruṣamāhūyovāca / bhadramukha pūrvaguṇānurāgād bhraṣṭaiśvaryasyāpi mama imaṃ tāvad apaścimaṃ vyāpāraṃ kuru / idaṃ mamārdhāmalakaṃ grahāya kukkuṭārāmaṃ gatvā saṅghe niryātaya / madvacanācca saṅghasya pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā vaktavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, summoning a man who stood nearby, said: 'Good sir, out of attachment to my former virtues, even though I have lost my sovereignty, perform for me this one last service. Take this half <s>āmalaka</s> of mine, go to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s>, and deliver it to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. And having bowed at the feet of the <s>Saṅgha</s> on my behalf, say:

body.text: jambudvīpaiśvaryasya rājña eṣa sāmprataṃ vibhava iti / idaṃ tāvad apaścimaṃ dānaṃ tathā paribhoktavyaṃ yathā me saṅghagatā dakṣiṇā vistīrṇā syāditi / āha ca /
body.translated_text: 'This is now the fortune of the king who was lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.' Let this last gift be consumed in such a way that my offering directed toward the <s>Saṅgha</s> may be extensive.' And he said:

children.text: idaṃ pradānaṃ caramaṃ mamādya rājyaṃ ca taccaiva gataṃ svabhāvaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'This gift of mine today is the final one, and that kingdom too has gone the way of its nature;
for one bereft of the physician-medicine of health, I have no protector outside the assembly of Noble Ones.'

children.text: tattathā bhujyatāṃ yena pradānaṃ mama paścimaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let it be consumed in such a way that this last gift of mine

children.text: yathā saṅghagatā me 'dya vistīrṇā dakṣiṇā bhavet //
children.translated_text: may today become an extensive offering directed toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'

body.text: evaṃ deveti sa puruṣo rājño 'śokasya pratiśrutya tadardhāmalakaṃ gṛhya kukkuṭārāmaṃ gatvā vṛddhānte sthitvā kṛtāñjalistadardhāmalakaṃ saṅghe niryātayannuvāca /
body.translated_text: 'So be it, Your Majesty.' The man, having acknowledged King <s>Aśoka</s>'s [command], took that half <s>āmalaka</s>, went to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s>, stood at the end of the row of elders, and with palms joined, while delivering that half <s>āmalaka</s> to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, said:

children.translated_text: 'He who formerly commanded the earth raised beneath a single parasol,

children.text: lokaṃ tāpayati sma madhyadivasaprāpto divā bhāskaraḥ /
children.translated_text: who used to scorch the world like the midday sun at its zenith —
that king, today, having perceived a crack in his fortune, deceived by his own deeds,
stands stripped of his power, like the sun when the day has reached its end.'

body.text: bhaktyāvanatena śirasā praṇamya saṅghāya tena khalu dattamidamāmalakasyārdhaṃ lakṣmīcāpalyacinhitaṃ / tataḥ saṅghasthaviro bhikṣūnuvāca / bhadantā bhavabhdiḥ śakyamidānīṃ saṃvegamutpādayituṃ / kutaḥ / evaṃ hyuktaṃ bhagavatā- paravipattiḥ saṃvejanīyaṃ sthānamiti / kasyedānīṃ sahṛdayasya saṃvego notpādyate / kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'With head bowed in devotion, making obeisance to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, this half of a myrobalan, marked by the fickleness of fortune, has been given by him.' Then the Elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> addressed the monks: 'Venerable ones, it is possible now to arouse a sense of spiritual urgency from [witnessing] the existence-ocean. Why? For thus has the Blessed One declared: "The misfortune of others is a cause for spiritual urgency." Whose compassionate heart would not now be stirred to urgency? For:

children.translated_text: 'That lord of men, <s>Aśoka</s>, the elephant of the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty, a hero of generosity,
having been the lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, has become the lord of half a myrobalan.'
'That lord of the earth, whose authority has today been seized by his servants,
gives indeed this half of a myrobalan as a gift —
as if rebuking the minds of ordinary people
who are exceedingly proud with the intoxication of the enjoyment and display of wealth.'

body.text:
yāvad tadardhāmalakaṃ curṇayitvā yūṣe prakṣipya saṅghe cāritaṃ /
tato rājāśoko rādhaguptamuvāca / kathaya rādhagupta kaḥ sāmprataṃ pṛthivyāmīśvaraḥ /
body.translated_text:
Thereupon, that half <s>āmalaka</s> was ground to powder, mixed into broth, and distributed to the <s>Saṅgha</s>.
Then King <s>Aśoka</s> said to <s>Rādhagupta</s>: 'Tell me, <s>Rādhagupta</s>, who is now the lord of the earth?'

body.text: atha rādhagupto 'śokasya pādayornipatya kṛtāñjalir uvāca / devaḥ pṛthivyāmīśvaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Rādhagupta</s>, falling at <s>Aśoka</s>'s feet with palms joined, said: 'Your Majesty is the lord of the earth.'

body.text: atha rājāśokaḥ kathaṃcidutthāya caturdiśamavalokya saṅghāyāñjaliṃ kṛtvovāca /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, somehow rising up, looked in the four directions, made an <s>añjali</s> (gesture of reverence) toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and said:

body.text: eṣa idānīṃ mahat kośaṃ sthāpayitvā imāṃ samudraparyantāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ bhagavacchrāvakasaṅghe niryātayāmi /
body.translated_text: 'Setting aside the great treasury, I now deliver this great earth, bounded by the oceans, to the community of the Blessed One's disciples.'

body.text: āha ca /
body.translated_text: And he said:

children.translated_text: 'This earth, wearing the ocean as a splendid blue garment, her face adorned with many treasure-mines,

children.text: dadāmyahaṃ bhutadharāṃ samandarāṃ saṅghāya tasmai hyupabhujyatāṃ phalaṃ //
children.translated_text: this bearer of beings, together with her mountains — I give her to the <s>Saṅgha</s>; may the fruit be enjoyed.'

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: 'By this gift I do not desire the abode of <s>Indra</s>, nor the fruit [of rebirth] in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
much less the royal glory that is fickle as the current of rushing water.

children.text: dānasyāsya phalaṃ tu bhaktimahitaṃ yanme 'sti tenāpnuyāṃ
children.translated_text: But may the fruit of this gift, honored by devotion — whatever is mine — by that may I attain
the lordship of mind, the noble, the worthy, honored by the Noble Ones, which undergoes no transformation.'

body.text: yāvat patrābhilikhitaṃ kṛtvā dantamudrayā mudritaṃ / tato rājā mahāpṛthivīṃ saṅghe dattvā kālagataḥ / yāvadamātyairnīlapītābhiḥ śivikābhirnirharitvā śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā dhmāpayitvā rājānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāma iti [uktam] / yāvad rādhaguptenābhihitaṃ / rājñāśokena mahāpṛthivī saṅghe niryātitā iti / tato 'mātyairabhihitaṃ kimarthamiti /
body.translated_text: Having had it written on a document and sealed with his tooth-seal — then the king, having given the great earth to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, passed away. The ministers, having carried [the body] out on blue and yellow palanquins and performed the funeral rites, cremated it. [They said]: 'We shall install a [new] king.' Thereupon <s>Rādhagupta</s> said: 'King <s>Aśoka</s> delivered the great earth to the <s>Saṅgha</s>.' Then the ministers asked: 'For what purpose?'

body.text: rādhagupta uvāca / eṣa rājño 'śokasya manoratho babhūva koṭīśataṃ bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dāsyāmīti / tena ṣaṇṇvatikoṭyo dattāḥ / yāvad ājñā pratiṣiddhā / tadabhiprāyeṇa rājñā mahāpṛthivī saṅghe dattā /
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhagupta</s> said: 'This was King <s>Aśoka</s>'s heart's desire: "I shall give a hundred <s>koṭis</s> as a gift to the Blessed One's Teaching." He gave ninety-six <s>koṭis</s>. Then his authority was obstructed. With that [remaining] intention, the king gave the great earth to the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'

body.text: yāvadamātyaiścatasraḥ koṭīr bhagavacchāsane dattvā pṛthivīṃ niṣkrīya saṃpadī rājye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the ministers, having given four <s>koṭis</s> to the Blessed One's Teaching, redeemed the earth and installed <s>Saṃpadī</s> as king.

body.text: saṃpadino bṛhaspati putro bṛhaspate 'rvṛṣaseno vṛṣasenasya puṣyadharmā puṣyadharmaṇaḥ puṣyamitraḥ / so 'mātyānāmantrayate / ka upāyaḥ syād yadasmākaṃ nāma ciraṃ tiṣṭhed /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃpadī</s>'s son was <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s son was <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>'s was <s>Puṣyadharman</s>, and <s>Puṣyadharman</s>'s was <s>Puṣyamitra</s>. He consulted his ministers: 'What means is there by which our name may endure long?'

body.text: tairabhihitaṃ / devasya ca vaṃśād aśoko nāmnā rājā babhūveti / tena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ yāvad bhagavacchāsanaṃ prāpyate tāvat tasya yaśaḥ sthāsyati / devo 'pi caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayatu /
body.translated_text: They said: 'From Your Majesty's lineage there was a king named <s>Aśoka</s>. He erected eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s> (memorial shrines). As long as the Blessed One's Teaching endures, so long will his fame last. Let Your Majesty also erect eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s>.'

body.text: rājāha / maheśākhyo rājāśoko babhūva / anyaḥ kaścidupāya iti / tasya brāhmaṇapurohitaḥ pṛthagjano 'śrāddhaḥ / tenābhihitaṃ / deva, dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ nāma ciraṃ sthāsyati / rājñāśokena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ sthāpitamatastasya nāma ciraṃ tiṣṭhati / bhavāṃścet tāni nāśayed bhavato nāma cirataraṃ sthāsyatīti /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'King <s>Aśoka</s> was called "the Great Lord." Is there some other means?' His <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chaplain, an ordinary person and a non-believer, said: 'Your Majesty, for two reasons a name endures long. King <s>Aśoka</s> erected eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s>, and therefore his name endures. If Your Majesty destroys them, your name will endure even longer.'

body.text: yāvad rājā puṣyamitraścaturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhayitvā bhagavacchāsanaṃ vināśayiṣyāmīti kukkuṭārāmaṃ nirgataḥ / dvāre ca siṃhanādo muktaḥ / yāvat sa rājā bhītaḥ pāṭaliputraṃ praviṣṭaḥ / evaṃ dvirapi trirapi / yāvad bhikṣūṃśca saṅghamāhūya kathayati / bhagavacchāsanaṃ nāśayiṣyāmīti / kim icchatha stūpaṃ saṅghārāmān vā / stūpāḥ bhikṣubhiḥ
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Puṣyamitra</s>, having equipped his army of four divisions, set out for the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> [saying]: 'I shall destroy the Blessed One's Teaching.' At the gate, a lion's roar was uttered. The king, terrified, re-entered <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. This happened a second and a third time. Then he summoned the monks and the <s>Saṅgha</s> and said: 'I shall destroy the Blessed One's Teaching. What do you prefer — the <s>stūpas</s> or the monasteries?' The <s>stūpas</s> were

body.text: parigṛhītāḥ / yāvat puṣyamitro yāvat saṅghārāmaṃ [nāśayan] bhikṣūṃśca praghātayan prasthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: taken under the protection of the monks. Then <s>Puṣyamitra</s> set out, destroying monasteries and slaughtering monks.

body.text: sa yāvac chākalamanuprāptaḥ / tenābhihitaṃ / yo me śramaṇaśiro dāsyati tasyāhaṃ dīnāraśataṃ dāsyāmi / [tatra ekaḥ] dharmarājikāvāsya'rhad ṛddhyā śiro dātumārabdhaḥ / śrutvā ca rājārhantaṃ praghātayitumārabdhaḥ / sa ca nirodhaṃ samāpannaḥ / tasya paropakramo na kramate / sa taṃ samutsṛjya yāvat koṣṭhakaṃ gataḥ /
body.translated_text: He arrived at <s>Śākala</s>. He proclaimed: 'Whoever gives me the head of a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), to him I shall give a hundred <s>dīnāras</s> (gold coins).' [There,] an <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One) dwelling at the <s>dharmarājikā</s> began to offer his own head through his supernatural power. Hearing this, the king set about to kill the <s>Arhat</s>. But the <s>Arhat</s> entered the <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> (cessation-attainment). No attack could affect him. Abandoning him, the king went on to <s>Koṣṭhaka</s>.

body.text: daṃṣṭrānivāsī yakṣaścintayati / idaṃ bhagavacchāsanaṃ vinaśyati / ahaṃ ca śikṣāṃ dhārayāni / na mayā śakyaṃ kasyacidapriyaṃ kartuṃ / tasya duhitā kṛmiśena yakṣeṇa yācyate / na cānuprayacchati tvaṃ pāpakarmakārīti / yāvat sā duhitā tena kṛmiśasya dattā / bhagavacchāsanaparitrāṇārthaṃ parigrahaparipālanārthaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: The <s>yakṣa</s> (spirit) dwelling at <s>Daṃṣṭrā</s> reflected: 'The Blessed One's Teaching is being destroyed. I too uphold the precepts. I am unable to do harm to anyone.' His daughter was being asked for [in marriage] by the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kṛmiśa</s>, but he would not give her, [saying] 'You are an evildoer.' Then he gave that daughter to <s>Kṛmiśa</s> — for the protection of the Blessed One's Teaching and for the safeguarding of [his own] household.

body.text: puṣyamitrasya rājñaḥ pṛṣṭhato yakṣo mahāpramāṇo 'nubaddhaḥ / tasyānubhāvāt sa rājā na pratihanyate / yāvad daṃṣṭrānivāsī yakṣastaṃ puṣyamitrānubaddhaṃ
body.translated_text: A <s>yakṣa</s> of great size was following behind King <s>Puṣyamitra</s>. Through [that yakṣa's] power, the king could not be struck down. Then the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Daṃṣṭrānivāsin</s>, seizing that <s>yakṣa</s> who was following <s>Puṣyamitra</s>,

body.text: yakṣaṃ grahāya parvatacarye 'carat / yāvad dakṣiṇaṃ mahāsamudraṃ gataḥ / kṛmiśena ca yakṣeṇa mahāntaṃ parvatamānayitvā puṣyamitro rājā sabalavāhano 'vaṣṭabdhaḥ / tasya sunihita iti saṃjñā vyavasthāpitā / yadā puṣyamitro rājā praghātatastadā mauryavaṃśaḥ samucchinnaḥ /
body.translated_text: wandered with him in a mountain fortress. He went as far as the southern great ocean. And the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kṛmiśa</s>, having brought a great mountain, crushed King <s>Puṣyamitra</s> together with his army and mounts. [The mountain] was given the name <s>Sunihita</s> ('Well-placed'). When King <s>Puṣyamitra</s> was killed, the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty was cut off.

body.text: iti śrīdivyāvadāne 'śokāvadānaṃ samāptaṃ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Aśokāvadāna</s> (Legend of <s>Aśoka</s>) in the illustrious <s>Divyāvadāna</s> (Divine Legends).
